CAESALPINIA BONDUCELLA
(Nata)
PHARMACY - caesal. Caesalpinia bonducella.
Nata. Fever nut. Bondue nut. N. 0 . Leguminosae.
Planets: Moon. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Asthma. Chills. Depression. Fevers.
Headaches. Hemorrhage. Leprosy.Tuberculosis.
Weakness.
HERBAL- Nata is awell-known wild shrub of India.
It grows near the sea-coast in all hot countries,
the extensive distribution being due probably to
the transport of the seeds by oceanic currents.
It is pregnant with climbing prickly points and
the shrub is commonly found all over Bengali,
Bombay and practically the whole of southern
India. The plant has been known for a long time
to the Hindu and Mohammedan physicians to
contain excellent medicinal properties.
The seeds are considered in India and Persia
to be "very hot and dry" and they are found to
be very useful in dispersing swellings, arresting
hemorrhage and warding off infectious maladies.
The seeds, roasted and powdered, are employed
for hydrocele internally and externally. They are
also used internally in curing leprosy.
The powdered seeds mixed with black pepper
are found to be febrifuge and anti-periodic and are
used in chronic fevers. The fixed oil expressed
from the seeds is emollient and is employed as
an embrocation for the purpose of removing
freckles from the face, also as a cosmetic and
used also to arrest discharges from the ear. A
decoction of the roasted seeds is employed
against tuberculosis and asthma.
HOMEOPATHIC- Extreme weakness is felt after the
remission of fever, so much so that the patient is
averse even to have any talk. There is no inclination to do any work. Always likes to sleep. Lies
quit with closed eyes. No desire to leave bed.
After the remission of fever the patient feels
extreme weakness, is disinclined to do any work.
There is no desire to talk even. The patient likes
to lie down quietly in bed with closed eyes.
The fever appears between 8a.m. and 10a.m.
or between 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. In the afternoon
fever there is no thirst, but in the morning fever
there is thirst in hot stage.

COMMENTS- The Hom. Recorder of Aug., 1895,
reprinted a paper by Dr. Bredenoll of Erwitte in
which he gave his experience with this remedy in his
own case of intense kidney colic with the passage
of uric acid stones.
One of these stones was triturated in the
proportion of 5 parts to 95 of milk sugar. Of this,
he took 1/2 grain doses for a considerable time,
resulting in the formation of stones ceasing. The
tartar which had formed on his teeth dropped off,
and a nodosity of stony hardness disappeared
from the extensor tendon ofthe right middle finger.
Dr. Bredenoll writes: "In November, 1837, I was
suddenly attacked with vomiting, accompanied
with violent lancinating, sore or pinching pains in
the region of the left kidney.

Calculus rena/is
The horrible anguish and pain which Iexperienced
extorted from me involuntary screams, Iwaswrithing
like a worm in the dust.
"A calculus had descended into the ureter
and had become incarcerated in it. Repeated
doses of Nux-v relieved the incarceration and I
distinctly felt that the calculus was descending
towards the bladder. After twenty-four hours of
horrible suffering the vomiting ceased. The pain
became duller and was felt in the region where
the ureter dips into and becomes interwoven
with the tissue of the bladder.
"It continued for three days and then disappeared all of a sudden (the stone had not got
into the bladder). Thirty-six hours afterwards the
calculus entered the bulb of the urethra. I felt a
frequent desire to urinate, the urine was turbid
and bloody, until at last a calculus of four grains
made its appearance in the urine.
"After this I frequently passed gravel and
stones, at times with slight, at times violent pains,
sometimes accompanied with vomiting, I kept the
larger stones with a view of using them hereafter
as a curative agent.
"Professor Nasser of Bonn, where my son
studied medicine at the time, has analyzed the
stones and has found them to be urate of lime.
He advised me to take Mere-d. and the Sulphate
of soda for some time, it is scarcely necessary
for me to say that I did not follow his advice.
"On the 15th of February, 1839, I felt the
precursory symptoms of a new attack, which
really did break out in all its fury on the 16th
and continued on the 17th and 18th. I now took
5 grains of my kidney stones to be triturated in
my presence with 95 grains of sugar of milk,
according to the fashion of Hahnemann and took
1/2 grain in the evening of the 17th, another 112
grain in the morning of the 18th.
"On this day I passed very turbid urine with a
considerable quantity of gravel, however in the
region where the ureter dips into the bladder, I
experienced an uncomfortable sensation, but
was well otherwise.
"On the 19th I was obliged to visit a patient at
the distance of two miles, on my journey I feltthat
the calculus was descending into the bladder,
the urine which I emitted shortly afterwards was
very turbid and bloody.

CARBO FULLERENUM
(Carbon 60)
PHARMACY - Carbo fullerenum.Carbon 60. C60.
Buckministerfullerene. Planets: Saturn.Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-Allergies.Anxiety. Alzheimer's disease.
Arthritis. Bacterial, infrections. Brain fog. Cancer.
Fatigue. Heart, weakness. Immune deficiencies.
Inflammations. Insomnia. Memory, weakness.
Multiple sclerosis. Nausea. Osteoarthritis. Parkinson's disease. Skin, disorders. Sleep, disorders.
Stamina, low. Sunburns. Toxicity. Traumas.
Tumors. Viral, infrections. Vomiting.
HERBAL- Carbon 60 is a tiny molecule composed of
60 carbon atoms arranged in a sphere, and is also
known as a buckyball. Buckyballs are members of
the tullerene family of carbon structures, which also
include spheres, tubes, ellipsoids and a variety of
other shapes.
Carbon 60 fullerene was first discovered and
manufactured in 1985 by four scientists, James
Heath, Richard Smalley, Sean O'Brien and Robert
Curl. Carbon 60 was the first fullerene molecule
to be discovered, and was created while using a
laser to vaporize carbon, in an attempt to recreate
the infrared emissions from iant red carbon stars

Carbo fulferenum
The discovery of Carbon 60 led to Kroto, Curl
and Smalley being awarded the 1996 Nobel Prize
in Chemistry.
Star dust, meteorites or lightning discharges
Carbon-60 has been found in the discharge
caused from where lightning strikes the ground
or a dead tree. It has also been collected from
meteorite samples and is even found when star
dust is analyzed.
This all contributes to the idea that Carbon 60 far
predate life on Earth and are possibly a primordial
constituent of the universe and creation.
Anti-aging - Carbon 60 protecting against
the effects of aging such. Increases Longevity.
Reduces aging symptoms and extend the lifespan
of mammals, including humans. research in 2012
on the toxicity of Carbon 60 showed that not only
was it not toxic at all to rats, but that it almost
doubled their lifespan.
Alzheimer's disease - Carbon 60 actively
promotes the growth of new neurons. In Alzheimer's Disease and other neurodegenerative
disorders too, many neurons die. This results
in memory loss, cognitive decline and other
neurological problems. There is even evidence
that C60 can destroy amyloid-beta plaques, a
cause of Alzheimer's Disease
Antioxidant - Carbon 60 is a highly effective antioxidant, with the ability to "mop up"
free radicals which has an anti-aging effect. It
has been reported that this molecule has an
antioxidant capacity many times higher than
other antioxidants!
Anti-inflammation - Carbon 60 can reduce
inflammation from allergic reactions, arthritis.
Fight the degeneration that occurs during multiple
sclerosis, Parkinson's disease.
Athletetic performance - More stamina
can run longer with seemingly more effective
utilization of oxygen. Less fatigue.Cardiac
improvements. Better stamina and endurance.
Can run faster while feeling more comfortable.
More strength can lift much heavier weights,
sometimes to the point of causing tendon injury.
Can do more reps of the same weight. Carbon
60 is very helpful for athletes recovering from
workouts and traumas

Bone health • Carbon 60 has the potential to
inhibit both osteoarthritis and osteoporosis.
Carbon 60 prevented bone damage from aging.
Carbon 60 increased cartilage production and
reduced the enzymes that destroy it.
Brain health-Calmer, reduction in stress, less

Cancer and tumors - Carbon 60 prevents
certain bone marrow stem cells as well as
breast cancer cells from communicating. It is this
communication that causes rapidly spreading
(metastasis) cancer. This means Carbon 60 may
cause cancer cells to self-destruct.
Detoxification- Carbon 60 detoxifies harmful
substances and removes poisons, drugs, toxic
chemicals, from the body.
Hair loss- Certain types of skin disorders that
cause hair loss or alopecia, Carbon 60 seems
to repair this condition. Carbon 60 promotes
rapid hair growth in bald mice in the laboratory.
Immunity- Carbon 60 seems to have the ability
to prevent the spread of human cytomegalovirus, and hepatitis C. Both lymphocytes (white
blood cells) and useful cytokines, such as TNFalpha, play a key role in fighting off infections and
even tumor cells. The potent antioxidant ability of
this Carbon 60 moderates' allergies and severe
allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), which also
involve the excess production of free radicals.
Levels of histamine and allergic inflammatory
responses are also reduced with Carbon 60.
Inflammation - Carbon 60 naturally reduces
inflammation. One place it relieves inflammation is in joints and bones, reducing pain and
improving range of motion. The body produces
excessive amounts of free radicals causing the
inflammation and tissue damage associated with
arthritis. Carbon 60 neutralizes the free radicals,
reducing inflammation.
Skin health- Faster recovery of the skin after
sunburn (with topical application). In lab experiments Carbon 60 infused ointment protected the
skin from the damaging effects of UVA radiation.
In treating severe acne, Carbon 60 applied topically to skin decreased the numberof skin lesions,

Carb-ac. is a languid, painless, foul and destructive remedy. Acts primarily on the central
nervous system. It affectsthe mucus membranes,
heart, bloodand respiration. Stomach symptoms

Marked prostration , even paralytic with

in hands. Garb-s. has the flatulence of Carb-v.

column, finally of legs and arms. The contracture

COMMENTS - Cardamom seeds are sought-after
in sweet and dessert preparations. The pod is
split open to expose underlying seeds using either
fingers or small knife. The seeds are then crushed
using a hand mill just before their use in cooking.
Whole pods are preferred in savory dishes, which
give a further punch to the recipe since their peel
contains certain amounts of valuable oils.
Black cardamom (badi elaichi) - is mostly
preferred in savory dishes, to prepare rice-pilaf,
stews, and lentil-curry in many parts of Nepal,
India, and Pakistan.
Green cardamom - The fat green pods grown
in South India are considered the best in the world.
Green cardamom is available in the pod form or as
powder. The whole pod stores better and retains
the aroma of the seeds. Many Indian savories and
sweets are flavored with cardamom. This fragrant
spice is used in rich curries and milk-based preparations. In India, tea and coffee are sometimes spiked
. withcardamom.Around the world, green cardamom
is used in spiced cakes and breads.
Brown cardamom- Brown cardamom pods are
larger in size than the green cardamoms, and are
hairy. In fad, they look like tiny fibrous coconuts.
Brown cardamom is medicinal in flavor. In India,
it is used only in savories, especially to flavor rice
dishes like biryani. Along with green cardamom, it
is an essential ingredient in garam masalas [a blend
of mixed spices).
Cardamom oil-The essential oil from cardamom
is used for pharmaceutical purposes, perfumery,
flavoring liqueurs and bitters, in the preparation
of tincture, and as a stimulant. The therapeutic
properties of cardamom oil have found application
in many traditional medicines as antiseptic and
local anesthetic, antioxidant in addition to health
promoting and disease preventing roles.
Cardamom seed-Each cardamom pod encloses
several dark brown seeds which contain the entire
flavor. The typical dose of cardamom seed is
between 3 and 6 grams, crushed and powdered.
It is best used as a powder in combination with
other herbs.
Some practitioners also include cardamom seed
as part of a tea or decoction.

This thistle was used externally for wounds,
especially burns. It is said to have obtained
its name 'benedictus' from its high reputation
as a heal-all, being supposed even to cure the
plague. It is a basic ingredient of the Benedictine
Liqueur and other bitter tonics, stomach bitters.

CASSIA SOPHERA
(Senna Sophera)

PHARMACY - cassi-s. Cassia sophera. Senna
sophera. Senna esculenta. N. 0 . Leguminosae,
Caesalpinioideae. Planets: Moon. Historical
dose: nncture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Cough. Dyspnea. Knee, pain. Osteoarthritis.
HERBAL - Cassia sophera is indigenous to India
and has been frequently used by ancient Indian
physicians for its efficacy in respiratory disorders.
Its Sanskrit name 'Kasamarda' which means
'Destroyer of Cough.'
An effective herbal laxative is made from
the senna pods, and leaves. The purgative
constituents are closely allied to those of Aloes
and Rhubarb. The active substances are glycosides called sennosides. Senna pods have a
milder effect and have fewer side-effects than
Senna leaves.
The main effect is an increase in intestinal
peristalsis and a reduction in the water absorption
of the intestinal wall, which leads to accelerated
stools.
Side effects, especially from fresh senna
leaves, are intense cramp, excessive abdominal
cramps, and irritation of bladder and uterus.
Senna should not be administered to people
who suffer from hemorrhoids or enteritis. Their
use during pregnancy or the lactation period is
not recommended because of their excretion via
the mother's milk.

200th centesimal potencies.

Nash regarded "internal trembling" as a

hemorrhage associated with these symptoms.
Nash prescribed Caul. 3c for a woman of forty,
seven months pregnant, who was attacked with
severe pain and swelling of all the finger joints,
wrapping them in mustard was the only thing that
relieved her sufficiently to allow her to get sleep.
Caul. relieved the finger pains, but caused
such severe labor-like pains that it had to be
discontinued for fear of causing miscarriage.The
bearing-down then ceased and the finger pains
returned and continued until delivery, when they
ceased for a few days.
Then the lochia increased to a flooding, a
passive, dark, liquid with great weakness and
internal trembling. Now the terrible finger pains
returned. Afraid to give Caul., other remedies
were tried, but in vain. At last Nash gave Caul.
200c, which rapidly cleared up the whole case.

Cayenne pepper

HERBAL - The Cayenne is a hot red chili pepper
used to flavor dishes, and for medicinal purposes.
Named for the city of Cayenne in French Guiana.
Capsicum is related to bell peppers, jalapenos,
and others. The fruits are generally dried and
ground, or pulped and baked into cakes, which
are then ground and sifted to make the powder.
The Capsicums are ancient natives of the New
World, the oldest known specimens coming from
Mexico. Next to maize, the pepper (capsicum)
was the foremost plant grown in Central America
at the time of the Aztec Empire; of all the species of plant none was so widely used or held
in greater esteem.
Capsicum was introduced to Europe by Peter
Martyr. He reported the use of these pungent
peppers, and Dr. Chatica, reported their use as
a condiment and as a medicine.
Cayenne pepper was a mainstay of the Thomsonian School of Medicine, Samuel Thomson,
the original Botanic Physician, having featured
it along with Lobelia in his healing routines. It
was an important ingredient in his Composition
Powder, and he also used it as a stimulant and
an assist to the properties of Lobelia.
Capsaicin and other constituents in cayenne
have been shown to have several other actions,
including reducing platelet stickiness and
acting as antioxidants. Capsaicin temporarily
stimulates release of various neurotransmitters
from these nerves, leading to their depletion.
Without the neurotransmitters, pain signals can
no longer be sent.
Cayenne Pepper is the purest and best heart
stimulant ever known. It is exceedingly prompt
in its effects. Through the blood circulation, its
influence is manifest through the whole body. The
heart first, next the arteries, then the capillaries,
organs and the nerves.
Cayenne is a certain remedy for heart attack;
as a stimulant, it can start the heart into action
again, and as it facilitates blood flow throughout
the body, it will keep the heart going. Used as a
heart attack preventative, along with the mucusless diet and a healthful life-style, Cayenne can
do wonders in toning and rebuilding the heart
and keeping it in top condition.
Cayenne is a carminative, stimulant, diaphoretic. Heart tonic. Cayenne stimulates the heart
and circulation, increasing the pulse rate and
stren thenin it.

Poloponnes peninsula.

Dec. 10, 1928. The report of urine examination indicated that there was no sugar in the
urine. In other respects the patient was all right.
Ghose advised him to take occasional doses of
Cephalandra indica in 3x potency.
The patient made an eventful recovery and
no sugar could be found in his urine later on.

Charcoal activated

COMMENTS-Teste wrote, "According to Humboldt
about 500,000 pounds of this bark are annually
exported to Europe for the purpose of being
converted into sulphate of quinine." Well could
Teste add the exclamation. "Poor patients!" As
with almost every other good thing that comes into
its hands, allopathy has contrived to do an infinity
of harm with quinine to make up for the good.
The tincture is anti-septic, destroying ameboid
motion and retarding tissue change. It weakens
the heart and impairs the circulation. Chin. helps
with congestions and hemorrhages, anemia and
complete relaxation and collapse.
The result of suppression is thus sketched
by Hahnemann's master-hand: "True, he (the
patient) can no longer complain that the paroxysms of his original disease occurs any more on
regular days and at regular hours, but behold his
earthy complexion, his bloated countenance,his
languishing looks!
"Behold how difficult it is for him to breathe,
see his hard and distended abdomen the swelling of the hypochondria, see how his stomach
is oppressed and pained by everything he eats,
how his appetite is diminished, how his taste
is altered, how loose his bowels are and how
unnatural and contrary to what they should be,
how his sleep is restless, unrefreshing and full
of dreams.
"Behold him weak,out of humor and prostrated,
his sensibility morbidly excited, his intellectual
faculties weakened, how much more does he
suffer than when he was a prey to his fever !
"The number of patients who have been
consigned to an early grave by quinine probably
falls short only of the number that mercury can
claim. When first introduced it was (as chloral
and hundreds of other poisons have been since)
declared on the highest authority to be incapable
of harm "in whatever dose it may be taken."

suppuration, loss of semen, and after prolonged
strain of overwork, mental or bodily.

Great irritability. Irritability precedes headache.

stomach. Pain as from flatus wedged into flexure

abdomen. Left hypochondriac region enlarged.
Abdomen bloated, in intermittent fever.
Back - Pain in muscles between left shoulder
and neck, as if sprained, on rising from sleep,
4 p.m. Back feels weak as after a long journey.
Causations - Ill effects of tobacco. Fright.
Eggs and fish produce diarrhea.
Chest - Severe stitching pains in chest, later

Ears - Ringing in ears like bells, congestion

Eyes - Flickering with pain and lachrymation.
Keratitis. Intense photophobia and spasms of

Face pale, sallow bloated. Blueness of lips, in

Food - Anorexia. Appetite gone. Ravenous

COMMENTS- Bonino, who gave it a prolonged proving, found the chief effects were manifested on the
stomach, solar plexus, ligaments and skin.According to him, it corresponds to tobacco intoxication
and its effects, indigestion from unripe fruits, and
stomach pain from coarse food or ill-baked bread.
Marked weakness, prostration and disinclination for mental exertion. Convalescence from
long-lasting sickness. Slow circulation, relaxed
limbs. Chronic rheumatism of the joints without
swelling. Tertiary syphilis of periosteum. Colic
from incarcerated flatus intermittent fever with
predominating chills. Continuous yawning.

around eyes with chills, exaggerated sensitiveness
to alcohol and tobacco,prostration and restlessness.
(3) Enothera- effortless diarrhea with nervous exhaustion incipient hydrocephaloid. (4) Macrozarria
spiralis - extreme debility after illness, collapse.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chin-s. closely resembles Chin.
in its effects, but as it has been proved separately
and as observations of the effects of over-<:losing
have supplied many additional symptoms, there is
plenty of guidance in the selection of one in preference to the other.
In old-school practice, the Sulphate of Quinine has almost entirely taken the place of the
crude bark as a remedy. A dose of Chin-s. in
high potency sometimes arouses suppressed
malaria and brings back the paroxysm. Aside
from its undoubted influence over malaria, it is
indicated whenever there is a marked periodicity
and spinal sensitiveness.
Chin-s. acts on the nerves causing great

(Freshwater Green Algae)
PHARMACY-Chiarella vulgaris.Chiarella pyrenoidosa. Chiarella is a genus of single-cell green algae,
belonging to the phylum Chlorophyta. Planets:
Jupiter. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Acne. Allergies. Anemia. Arthritis.
Asthma.Bad,breath.Blood, pressure. Blood,sugar.

HISTORY -Chiarella vulgaris. Chiarella pyrenoidosa.
Thename Chiarella is taken from the Greek chloros,
meaning green, and the Latin diminutive suffix ella,
meaning small.
Chiarella is an emerald green, single-celled
freshwater micro-algae widely recognized as one
of the most potent nutritional whole foods on Earth.
Each chlorella cell is a self-sufficient organism with
all the plant's life functions taking place inside the
cell. The result - an unusually high concentration
of important nutrients.
Chiarella emerged over 2 billion years ago, and
was the first form of a plant with a well-defined
nucleus. Because Chiarellais a microscopic organism, it was not discovered until the late 19th century.
This algae plant contains the highest known
quantity of chlorophyll within a natural source.
Chlorophyll is the 'green blood' of all plant life and
has achemical structure very similar to hemoglobin,
our own red blood molecules.
Chiarella contains the green photosynthetic pigments chlorophyll-a and chlorophyll-b in its chloroplast. Through photosynthesis, it multiplies rapidly,
requiring only carbon dioxide, water, sunlight, and
a small amount of minerals to reproduce.

E. Z. Bacon recorded two cases of chlorine
poisoning. The first case was in a boy of 5, who,
after passing through diphtheria to apparent
complete recovery, was suddenly seized with
symptoms of croup. Loss of voice, crowing
inspiration, prolonged expiration incessant dry
cough,great restlessness, high fever, and profuse
perspiration.
The symptoms were worse lying on a lounge
by the fire, better when lying in his mother's lap
and still more relieved by being carried about.
During the previous illness, Platt's chlorides
had been placed in the room as a disinfectant
and it occurred to the doctor that chlorine vapor
is much heavier than air. He himself lay down,
and in a few minutes felt the irritating vapor and
began to cough and hack. This soon passed
away on sitting up.
The removal of the chlorides has a remarkable
effect on the child, cough and respiration were
greatly relieved. But the relief came too late, as
the cause was not discovered for several days
during which time the patient had become steadily
weaker, and he died the same afternoon.

Chlorum aqua

c

The other case was that of an old woman who
suffered from chronic bronchitis and on January
2, 1892, developed an attack of laryngitis. In three
days she was well, but in the two subsequent
weeks, on exactly the same day, a fresh attack
occurred.
As the doctor soon discovered, his patient
went to the back room, where chlorides were
kept, every Monday to wash a few things she
did not care to send to the laundry.
The chlorides were banished, and though the
washing was continued, there were no more attacks of laryngitis. Dr. Bacon added, that since
giving up the use of disinfectants, other than
plenty of fresh air, he has never had laryngeal
complications in scarlatina or diphtheria, though
his neighbors have had plenty.

HOMEOPATHIC- Cholesterinum crystallizes in leaflets with a mother-of-pearl luster and a fatty feel. It
is soluble in alcohol and ether. It occurs in the blood
and brain, yolk of eggs, seeds and buds of plants,
but most abundan~y in the bile and gallstones.
Dr. WilhelmAmeke of Berlin first mentioned this
remedy. Dr. Burnett, atAmeke's suggestion, used
the lower potencies with more or less success
for several years, a description of which Burnett
gives in his Diseases of the Liver.
Chol. was introduced by Swan. He appeared
to have taken his hint from Burnett's work and
potentized the remedy, using a gallstone.
Swan affirmed. after much experience, that it is
almost a specific for gallstone colic. It relieves
the distress at once and this after failure with
Nux-v., Chin., Card-m., Podo. and other apparently well-selected remedies.
Ameke recommended Chol. as a remedy in
cancer of the liver. Chol. is the physiological opponent of Lee .. both seem to play some unknown
part in the growth of tumors. Benign tumors,
uterine fibroids. Gallstones. Chronic jaundice.
Obstinate hepatic engorgements. Opacities
of the vitreous. Insomnia.
MIND -Irritable. Delirium. Moody.

holds his hand on side.

Ameke claimed to have derived great advantages from its use in cases diagnosed as cancer
of the liver, or in such obstinate engorgements
that malignancy was suspected.
Clarke cured a case in the last stage of liver
disease. He had been given up by his medical
attendant, who ordered him to make his will
without delay.
Burnett claimed to have twice cured cancer
of the liver with it and "in hepatic engorgements
that by reason of their intractable and slow
yielding to well-selected remedies make one
think of cancer."
In such conditions, where the diagnosis is in

to repeated attacks of biliary colic, Chol., he

even striking. It has been used with success in
the removal of opacities of the vitreous.

substantial doses. He commended it in "obstinate hepatic engorgements, which by reason of
their obstinacy make one think interrogatively
of cancer."
Also in "cases in which there appears to be a
semi-malignant affection involving the left lobe of
the liver and what lies between it and the pylorus
and the pancreas." In such cases Burnett gave
alternately Chol. 3x and Iodoform 3x.

Chrysophanicum acldum
A. B. Norton used it successfully internally

G. C. McDermott confirmed this. Used locally

increased by a throbbing sensation synchronous
with the pulse. This was accompanied with
phosphorescent flashes of light.
On forcing eyes to look at objects, retinal
impressions remained some time after closing them. Swelling of lids and irritation of skin
around. After lasting a week there was marked
improvement and a second, milder application
completed the cure.

Paris, so the treatment could not be followed up.
Dr. H. Von Musits treated a case of acute
meningitis in J. N. R., 43, male, married, a user
of alcohol and tobacco, bookkeeper.
After the intense summer heat, symptoms
developed including convulsions, distortion of
limbs, head turned backward. Trismus. Froth
from mouth. Biting of the tongue. Oppression of
breathing. Entire loss of consciousness and of
power of swallowing. Convulsions, followed by
complete exhaustion. Stupor. Swelling of face.
Inability to move the tongue. The whole body
seems to be of enormous size.
The patient had three convulsions during
twenty-four hours, followed by the swelling of
the tongue and body. Extreme trembling of the
hands. Articulation difficult.
Next day, profuse watery diarrhea stools,
worse by any noise, sudden entrance of any
person into the room or loud talking. Better by
rest and in a dark room. Several times previously
he had symptoms of nervous exhaustion. His
brother, a physician, died the previous spring
from paresis in consequence of excessive use
of alcohol and drugging.
After two doses of Cic.200c there were no more
convulsions and the patient was perfectly cured
in two weeks. There was no relapse.
Banerjee recorded the case of "A lad, aged
five years, had an attack of cholera three days
before my visit. Had been treated by a homeopath from beginning of attack. The patient was
suffering from convulsions, when I first saw him
on the fourth day. The convulsive fits were very
severe since the third day of the attack of cholera.
"The symptoms were: eyes half turned, head
drawn toward the left side and the hands and
feet of the same side were contracted. He was
given Bell., Hyos., Cina and Bryonia without
effect. Cicuta virosa was then given.

CIMEX LECTULARIUS
(Bedbug)
PHARMACY - cimx. Cimex lectularius. Bedbug.
Acanthia lectularia. N. 0 . Hemiptera. Tincture or
trituration. Planets: Mars. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL- Chill. Colic. Constipation. Contractures.
Cough. Fever. Hamstrings. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Intermittent, fever. Liver, pain. Muscle,
contractions. Seminal, emissions. Skin, disorders.
Tendons, disorders. Yawning.
HOMEOPATHIC - Cimex is an ancient remedy for
intermittent fever. Nash recorded the following
cure by Dr. Brewster of Syracuse. After driving a
fractious horse that tried to run away over a very
rough road, a man was so bruised and sprained
about the buttocks and legs that he was confined
to the house for a long time.
It settled finally into what appeared likely to
be permanent contraction of the lower limbs. No
remedy relieved until Dr. Brewster remembered a
case of intermittent fever that he had cured twenty
years before, being guided by this symptom.
Cimex 600c (Jenichen) promptly cured.
Characteristic weariness and inclination to
stretch. The flexors are most affected, pains in
all joints as if tendons were contracted and
too short, every motion or stretching of arms
or legs causes tightening pain in them. Hamstrings feel too short (Am-m.). Sensation of
retraction of arm tendons. The whole right side
is especially affected.

Clove oil

HERBAL- Forover2,000 years, Indian and Chinese
traditional medicine has made extensive use of
cloves and clove oil. Arabic traders brought the
buds to Europe in the 4th century. During the
7th and 8th centuries in Europe, cloves became
popular as a food preservative.
Cloves have been well known as an all around
healing herb and it is not just digestive problems
that cloves are reputed to help with. In fact, they
are used in tropical Asia to treat conditions such
as scabies, cholera, malaria and tuberculosis.
The essential clove oil, the most popular clove
product, is extracted from the flower of the clove.
Clove oil constituents include eugenol, eugenyl
acetate, caryophyllene and iocaryophyllene.
Cloves are high in vitamins, minerals and
fiber. However, the component responsible for
clove's powerful effects and odor is a substance
called eugenol. Eugenol is toxic against harmful
organisms, including fungus, and has analgesic
and anesthetic effects.
One of the medicinal benefits of cloves is that
it is very effective against a variety of digestive
problems. Thus cloves are used in the natural
treatment for indigestion, loose stools, flatulence
and nausea. In fact cloves are also effective in
gaining relief from vomiting, gastric irritability
and diarrhea.
Clove oil offers a powerful action against
gas and bloating. It reduces gas pressure in
the stomach, aiding in the proper elimination of
food and toxins. It also relieves the discomfort
of peptic ulcers and is effective against nausea,
hiccups, motion sickness and vomiting.
Clove oil is used in connection with respiratory ailments such as asthma and bronchitis,
muscle aches, sprains and strains, arthritis and
rheumatism. Many individuals use clove oil for
its analgesic effects for body pain.
Clove oil, which encourages healthy teeth and
gums, is a traditional remedy for relieving toothache, sore gums and oral ulcers. Dental clove oil
is also commonly used on account of its properties
as an anesthetic, analgesic, antibacterial and for
its anti-inflammatory properties as well.
Clove oil is considered by many to be an effective antibiotic, antiseptic, antiviral, analgesic,
antioxidant,carminative, expectorant, antifungal,
anti-parasitic, spasmodic, and stimulant.

Coca etythroxylon
A striking case was recorded in the British
Medical Journal of December 13, 1890. At a
meeting of the Paris Academie de Medecine
on December 2nd, M. Hallopeau presented a
communication after distinguishing two forms
of cocaine poisoning: the acute in which the
symptoms are produced immediately after a dose
and speedily pass off, and the chronic in which
they are due to the prolonged use of the drug.
He then related a case that in his opinion
showed that the poisonous effects,while coming
on acutely, might last for aconsiderable time. On
March 7, 1890, aman had about eight milligrams
of hydrochlorate of cocaine injected into his gum
as apreliminary to the extraction of a tooth. Toxic
symptoms at once supervened.
There was intense precordial oppression with
thready pulse and extreme excitement and loquacity.The patient walked about the room, hitting
out at random with his fists and crying out that
he was dying. In ten minutes he became quiet
and the tooth was extracted after which he was
able to walk home, but arrived there in a state
of extreme prostration.
Then ensued a train of nervous symptoms,
such as continual headache, intractable sleeplessness, a bad taste in the mouth with attacks of
excitement accompanied by giddiness, faintness,
and a sense of impending death.
All brain work was impossible, the patient
could not do the simplest sum in arithmetic and
was in a state of profound depression. A sense
of formication and numbness in the hands and
forearms was almost incessant.
This condition lasted four months. It was
two months after the injection before the least
improvement was observed, and then progress
towards recovery was very slow.
M. Hallopeau thought the symptoms indicated
.a poisonous action of cocaine on the nervous
centers and especially the brain. As it is impossible to suppose that so small a quantity of the
drug should have remained in the circulation, he
was driven to conclude either that it was stored
up in the cells of certain nervous centers or that
it produced in them persistent lesions.
Among other effects observed from its use in
dentistry are "mental depression and drowsiness
and intense oppression in chest, dilatation of
pupils, acceleration of pulse and breathing and
mental excitement."

Kunkel recorded the case of a man, 75, who
suffered from nocturnal bedwetting up to the age
of seven. When almost 20 he frequently passed
large quantities of uric acid and at the same time
he began to have symptoms of chronic catarrh of
the colon, frequent scanty stools, much mucus,
cross humor, itching anus, threatening of hemorrhoids but no bleeding.
Insomnia soon followed. Coc-c. 2c and 3cwas
given without benefit. Aqua calcis did some good,
but not much. In three successive years he was
sent to Carlsbad with good results to the intestinal
catarrh, the sleeplessness was untouched.
Gradually all kinds of arthritic symptoms
developed, especially in knees. There was occasionally a considerable flow of urine and the
more copious it was the better the patient slept
and the less pain in the joints. The same relief
followed an attack of diarrhea.
Four weeks at Assmanhausen caused the
excretion of large quantities of uric acid one year,
but had no effect the next and the knee got worse.
Wiesbaden helped one year but not the next.
Half a tumbler of Kronenquelle water drunk
every morning helped the knee and enabled
him to walk better than he had for a long time.
In three or four years, the excretions of uric acid
had ceased and the patient's grew worse, insomnia recurred , diarrhea became more frequent.
A fortnight previous to such attack, the patient
noticed he had great aversion to butcher's meat.
Coc-c. 30c morning and evening was given.
Gradually sleep returned. There was almost daily
excretion of uric acid, sometimes in the form of
large shot, the diarrhea ceased and the patient
went about his work with pleasure.

Coconut oil
Cooking, oil-Doesnotform harmful by-products
when heated to normal cooking temperature like

HERBAL - The roasting of coffee develops certain
vitamin-like substances. The roasting process of
coffee beans reduces amounts of the chemical
chlorogenic acid. Therefore. green coffee beans
have a higher level of chlorogenic acid compared
to regular. roasted coffee beans.
While roasting green coffee beans removes its
naturally bitter taste. it also removes a significant
portion of chlorogenic acid. Hence. green coffee
beans remain one of the best natural sources for
chlorogenic acid.

HOMEOPATHIC - Colchicum is best known as a
remedy for gout and rheumatism. It markedly
affects muscles,fibrous tissue,serous membranes,
and joints, especially the small ones.
Colch. relieves gouty paroxysms. Red, hot
and swollen parts. Tearing pain, worse in the
evening, at night, and from touch. Stubbing the
toes hurts exceedingly.
Many joints are affected at the same time.
Small, rapidly shifting areas of severe pain, but
little swelling. Pains are tearing,digging,drawing.
Tingling, crawling. Stitching,jerl<ing,drawing pains
in muscles, periosteum and joints. Pains worse
from mental exertion, emotions, slightest touch
and vibrations.
There is the irritability and aversion to touch,
common in gout. Pain in small joints and especially the great toes. Affects the periosteum
and synovial membranes of joints.
The stomach is acutely disordered, nausea and
vomiting. Nausea at thought, sight or smell of
food, especially of cooking.
Dysentery. Uric acid diathesis, pale yellow
sediment like fine flour. Urine black as ink. Urine
loaded with albumen and casts.

CONCHIOLINUM
(Mother of Pearl)
PHARMACY -conch.Conchiolinum. Motherofpear1.
Mater perlarum. Triturations. Planets: Moon. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.
CLINICAL- Bone, disorders. Fever. Lung, disorders.
Osteitis. Pyemia.
·
HOMEOPATHIC - Conch. has a wide range of action in disorders of bones, especially when the
growing ends are affected. Calc-p. and Calc. are
its nearest analogs.
Observations made on workers in mother-ofpearl factories showed that inhalation of the dust
produces catarrh of the respiratory organs and,
later on inflammation of the ends of bones. This
begins in the diaphyses, but may spread to the
epiphyses. It attacks young subjects.
First there is a more or less intense pain in
the bone, comes suddenly, at first continuous,
later intermittent.

c

Conchiolinum
Soon after the appearance of the pain there
is fever, thirst, loss of appetite, sleeplessness,
dark-colored urine with sediment. Then swelling
occurs, developing on one or the other end of
a diaphysis, never in the middle of it nor in the
epiphysis. The swelling has a clear, sharp margin.
Swelling is very painful to the slightest touch,
at first soft, elastic and slightly fluctuating. It may
become as hard as a bone. Suppuration may
occur. The bones that have been affected are
lower jaw, scapula, humerus, radius, ulna, tibia,
fibula, tarsal and metatarsal bones.
COMMENTS - Clarke cured with Conch. 3c a
delicate boy who at three different times had had
pain in his left knee. The left inner condyle was
swollen and tender. The cure was rapid and the
general health much improved at the same time.
REFERENCES - Clarke.

CORIANDER
(Coriandrum Sativum)
PHARMACY - Coriandrum sativum. Coriander.
Cilantro.Chinese Parsley. Dhania. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Alzheimer's disease. Anemia. Arthritis.

HISTORY-The use of coriander can be traced back to
5,000 BC, making it one of the world's oldest spices.
II is native to the Mediterranean and Middle Eastern
regions and has been known in Asian countries for
thousands of years.
Coriander was cultivated in ancient Egypt and
given mention in the Old Testament. II was used
as a spice in both Greek and Roman cultures, the
latter using it to preserve meats and flavor breads.
The early physicians, including Hippocrates, used
coriander for its medicinal properties, including as
an aromatic stimulant.

c

Coriander
The Russian, India, Morocco and Holland are
among the countries that commercially produce
coriander seeds. Coriander leaves (cilantro) are
featured in the culinary traditions of Latin American,
Indian and Chinese cuisine.
HERBAL- Coriander is considered both an herb and
a spice since both its leaves and its seeds are used
as a seasoning condiment. Fresh coriander leaves
are more commonly known as cilantro and bear
a strong resemblance to Italian flat leaf parsley..
Anemia ·In addition, cilantro provides health
benefits to the persons who are suffering from
anemia. Coriander contains high amounts of iron,
which is essential for curing anemia.
Antioxidant • As an antioxidant cilantro is
able to help reduce inflammation. In this capacity it fights free radicals that destroy cellular
structure. Phytonutrients in coriander such as
elemol, camphor, borneol, carvone, quercetin,
keampferol and epigenin, give protection from
free radical damage.
Anti-bacterial- Cilantro contains an antibacterial compound called dodecenal, that may prove
to be a safe, natural means of fighting Salmonella,
a frequent and sometimes deadly cause of food
borne illness.
Bad, breath - Chewing cilantro keeps the
mouth and breath fresh . Chewing coriander
after eating onions or garlic masks their smell.
Brain, fog - Many people who have suffered
from mercury poisoning and the "brain fog" it
causes have reported fairly rapid relief by the
consistent consumption of cilantro over a period
of just a few weeks. Many people believe that
chewing on a pinch of cilantro every day will
help keep the mind clear and the breath crisp.
Cholesterol -Coriander lowers levels of total
and LDL (the "bad" cholesterol), while actually
increasing levels of HDL (the "good" cholesterol).
Cilantro essential oil - The essential oil
of cilantro is extracted from the leaves of the
plant by a steam process. Analysis shows that
it is comprised mainly of aldehydes. Cilantro oil
has a positive effect the inner digestive tract of
most people. II assists the digestive system in
production of digestive enzymes that stimulate
digestion through peristaltic motion.

669

Coriander
Detox • Cilantro has been found to chelate
(remove) heavy metals like mercury, aluminum,
and lead from the body. Cilantro has been specifically used to remove heavy metals that are
in the brain and spinal cord. Cilantro has been
used for heavy metal detoxification in combination with chlorella, a green algae superfood, and
garlic extracts.
Diabetes • Coriander is good for diabetes
patients. When coriander was added to the diet,
it helped stimulate their secretion of insulin and
lowered their blood sugar.
Digestion • A very good food for digestive
system. Promotes liver functions and bowel
movements. Add cilantro into a stir-fry, toward
the end of cooking to maintain the fresh flavor
and oils that can stimulate digestion and minimize
gastric distress.
Eyes • Another important health benefit of

Cranbeny
HERBAL - Cranberries are small, red berries, and
mainly grow in the cooler regions of the world such
as Canada, the United States and Europe. They
have a tart taste to them, but they are loaded with
antioxidants and many essential nutrients.
Cranberries are also called "bounce berries"
because they bounce when ripe. The name cranberry cx>rnes from "crane berry": before the flower
expands, its stem, calyx, and petals look like the
neck, head, and bill of a crane. In north-eastern
Canada cranberries are sometimes called moss
berry.
Many cranberries are water-harvested. Waterharvesting means that the cranberries are grown in
bogs and floated in watertoallowforeasy harvesting.
The North American cranberry has a long and
distinguished history. The healthy giving properties
of this fruit were recognized by Native American
Indians. Native peoples used cranberries as food,
in ceremonies and medicinally.
Early New England sailors are said to have eaten
the vitamin C-rich wild cranberries to prevent scurvy.
Revolutionary War veteran Henry Hall planted the
first commercial cranberry beds in Dennis Massachusetts in 1816.
For many years, researchers believed that the
ability of cranberries and cranberry juice to help
prevent urinary tract infections was partly related to
the strong acidity of the cranberries. Research has
shown that irs not the acidity of the cranberries, but
the unusual nature of their proanthocyanidins that
is related to prevention of urinary tract infections.
These condensed tannins or proanthocyanidins
from the cranberry fruit prevent Escherichia coli
(E.coli), the primary bacteria responsible for UTis,
from attaching to cells in the urinary tract. Thus,
the bacteria are flushed from the tract rather than
being allowed to adhere, grow and lead to infection.
Cranberries are an excellent source of antioxidants which may protect against cancer, heart
disease and other diseases.
Cranberries are a rich source of the flavonoid
quercetin which can inhibit the development of both
breast and colon cancers. Quercetin decreases
production of cavity and plaque producing bacteria
in your mouth. Also found to reduce the bacteria
associated with peptic stomach ulcers.
Cranberries have antioxidant, diuretic and antibacterial effects.

Antioxidants -Cranberries contain significant
amounts of antioxidants and otherphytonutrients
that may help protect against heart disease,
cancer and other diseases. Anthocyanins,
compounds that give cranberries their red color,
are powerful antioxidants that may be as strong

Anti-aging - The antioxidants contained in
cranberries will help your body to get rid of all
the free radicals which contribute to the aging
process. They will not only help your skin to look

to function longer without problems.
Bladder, infections - Cranberries contain
citric acid and nutrients that can prevent and
treat bladder problems. Cranberry juice can
help block urinary tract infections. It contains
proanthocyanidins, which help to prevent E. coli
bacteria from sticking tothe walls of the uterus and
bladder. One to three glasses of juice a day is all
you need to prevent and heal bladder infections.
Cancers - Cranberry contains proanthocyanidins. These compounds inhibit the growth
of various cancer cells. Proanthocyanidins can
stop micro-tumors from developing in the blood
vessels necessary for their continued growth.
Chemicals in cranberries also prevent multiplication of breast cancer cells. Other cancers
that may be prevented by using cranberries are
colon, prostate and lung.
Cholesterol- Drinking cranberry juice can help
lower your cholesterol. Cranberries have been
linked to producing HDL (good cholesterol) as well

benefits can be attributed to the presence of
polyphenols in cranberry juice.
Colds - Fresh cranberry juice is effective at

Dental - Consuming cranberries on a regular

Eyes- Cranberries are especially beneficial to
the eyes. They significantly improve symptoms
of cataracts, macular degeneration, and diabetic
retinopathy.

capsules, extracts, and herbal teas.
When you choose fresh cranberries look for
bright red, hard. and plump ones; stay away from
soft, dull, or wrinkled berries.
Fresh cranberries health benefits along with their
distinctive flavor and bright color, make these little
red berries perfect to be used in fruit or green salads,
sauces, snacks, and juice blends.
For optimum health benefits consume fresh
cranberries and make your own juice at home with
a juicer, or opt for unsweetened, 100 percent pure
cranberry juice.
Irs very easy to juice fresh cranberries at home
with just about any juicer. If the juice is too tart,
sweeten it with fresh apple juice at a ratio of 1 part
apple juice to 3 parts cranberry juice. Cranberries
and apples are a great mix. Sweeten the juice with
organic maple syrup to enhance the cranberries
health benefits.
Cranberries are high in vitamin C, and fiber
with only 45 calories per cup. Raw cranberries
and cranberry juice are abundant food sources of
flavonoids such as proanthocyanidins. flavonols
and quercetin. Cranberries have high content in
vitamin A,carotene,thiamine, riboflavin,niacin, large
quantities of vitamin C and antioxidants (phenols).
Cranberries also contains a high content of
minerals (sodium, potassium,calcium,magnesium,
phosphorus, copper, sulphate, iron) and organic
acids (quinic, malic, benzoic, and citric).

crataegus oxyacantha.

Teste, who was among the first to use Croto-t.
homeopathically, gave a very interesting account
of it. He quoted Trousseau and Pidoux as saying
that it often happens that eruptions are developed
on parts not touched by the remedy in those who
have been engaged in making Croto-t. ointments
on patients.
The face and the scrotum especially have
been thus attacked. The itching which it causes,
according to Teste, is at first more tingling than
burning (the contrary taking place with Rhus-t.).
The itching changes to burning {like Rhus-!.).
Teste recorded the case of a delicate, cachectic, psoric girl of four who had suffered for two
years without interruption from a fetid discharge
from the nose, less in winter, more in summer.
Before this, she had a vesicular eruption on chest
and neck, which disappeared by itself, followed
in three or four days by the discharge.
After the failure of Sulph., Mere., Calc., on the
indication of the previous eruption. Teste gave
Croto-1., and in less than a fortnight the disease
lost three-fourths of its intensity, although it was
in mid-summer. Six months completed the cure,
the only other remedies given during the time
were Lob. and Kreos.
A second case from Teste records a man of
forty, very fleshy, who for fifteen years had been
subject to attacks of gout returning every spring,
except on two occasions when a most fatiguing
and obstinate rash appeared instead.
This consisted of an intense redness of the
whole body, accompanied with a burning itching, especially in the hollow of the hands, at the
chest, and behind the ears.
These parts were the seat of a yellowish, plastic
exudation, emanating from a multitude of small
vesicles in close contact with each other. They
were only distinctly perceived in places where
they were less numerous and where a greater
degree of resistance on the part of the epidermis
imparted to them a certain persistence.

Croton tiglium
Each time this eruption broke out, it lasted three

patient, he had neithergout nor eczema, but adry,
racking, almost convulsive and unceasing cough.
Skin was rather hot, there was thirst, a little

few days, he showed a tendency to syncope.
At the end of three weeks, having received no

"Syrup of White Poppy," at bedtime. The cough
ceased entirely for some hours and then returned

But during the intermission the malady had
come out on the skin, and at daybreak the patient
found himself covered from head to foot with his
old horrible eczema.
He was almost unrecognizable and in a state
of the deepest anxiety and despair. He expected
three or four months of it.
Teste then gave Croto-1: The itching disappeared the same day. Within five or six days
there remained not a trace of either cough or
eruption. As the patient left Paris, Teste was
not able to follow the case in subsequent years.

HERBAL-Cucumber(Cucumissativus) is avegetable
that belongs to the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae,
which includes gourds, melons, and squashes.
There are two types of cucumbers: slicing cucumbers and pickling cucumbers.The pickling varieties
tend to be smaller, thicker, and have bumpy skin
with black-<totted spines.
The cucumber is believed to be native to India,
and evidence indicates that it has been cultivated
in Western Asia for 3,000 years. The cucumber
is also listed among the foods of ancient Ur
and the legend of Gilgamesh describes people
eating cucumbers.
· The cultivation process started in France in the
~th century, then in England in the 14th century
and finally in North America by the mid 16th
century. The Romans introduced cucumbers
to Europe.

HOMEOPATHIC · The proving was done by Joseph

Cystisus Laburnum,or wild laburnum, is a member ofthe leguminosae family.CystisusAubour is a
shrub or small tree,growing naturally or cultivated
as an ornamental plant with trifoliate leaves.
It has pale, yellow flowers which hang in
clusters with long pods and which are hairy
when yellow.
All parts of this well-known ornamental tree
are poisonous, especially the flowers and seeds,
owing to the presence of cytisin. This oxygenated,
unsaturated alkaloid is toxic to the glands, which
it first arouses and then paralyzes. It causes
convulsions and can lead to death by asphyxia.
The toxicity of cytisin is allied to that of nicotine.
Knowledge of it is derived chiefly from the
accidental poisoning of children who have eaten
the pea-like seeds and pods.
A typical case can be seen in that of W. G.,
et. 10, who ate eight to ten seeds. Five or ten
minutes later, began to sweat, but soon became
cold and shivering, skin pale, pulse scarcely
perceptible, general collapse.

HERBAL - Dandelion has a rich history. It was first

Dandelion as a medicine was first mentioned in
the works of theArabian physicians of the tenth and
eleventh centuries, who speak of it as a sort of wild
Endive, under the name of Taraxcacon.
The Greeks referred to it as "taraxos" "akos·,
which translates to "disorder remedy."
The French gave this herb its common name
calling it "dent de leon", which translates to "teeth
of the lion."They associated the saw-tooth shape of
the leaf as lion's teeth. Down through the centuries
the leaf and root have been used for the medicinal
properties.
European herbalists use dandelion for fever,diarrhea and diabetes. Dandelion is cultivated largely in
India as a remedy for liver complaints.
In traditional Chinese medicine, it is commonly
recommended for digestive problems and to improve
milk production in breast-feeding women.
Dandelion can also be used as a vegetable and
is a good source of fiber. It promotes digestion. In
old days it was also used to treat scurvy, due to
presence ofvitamin-C in it. II also has healing effects
on dyspepsia, infections in the stomach, intestines
and urinary system.
Dandelion leaf also serves to protect the liver
from damage. Many people use the herb to cleanse
their liver after drinking excess amounts of alcohol
or after eating unhealthful foods.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dioxins are a group of highly toxic
chemical compounds that are harmful to health.
They can cause problems with reproduction,
development, and the immune system. They can
also disrupt hormones and lead to cancer.
Over ninety percent ofhuman exposure to dioxins
comes through food, mainly animal products, such
as dairy, meat, fish, and shellfish.When dioxins enter
the food chain, they are stored in animal fats. Once
consumed, dioxins can stay in the body for a long
time, up to seven to ten years.
Short-term exposure of humans to high levels
of dioxins may result in skin lesions, such as
chloracne and patchy darkening of the skin, and
altered liver function.
Long-term exposure is linked to impainnent
of the immune system, the developing nervous
system, the endocrine system and reproductive
functions.

HERBAL- Dragon's blood has a long history of indigenous use in the rainforest and in South America.
The earliest written reference dates Dragon's blood
use to the 1600s, when Spanish naturalist and
explorer P. Bernabe Cobo found that the curative
power of the sap was widely known throughout the
indigenous tribes of Mexico, Peru, and Ecuador. Its
Peruvian name, sangre de grado, means "blood of
the dragon" (in Spanish).
In Ecuador, it's named sangre de drago (which
means "dragon's blood" as well). When the trunk
of the tree is cut or wounded, a dark red, sappy
resin oozes out as ifthe tree is bleeding, earning
this local name.

Dr. Serrand of Paris maintained that Dros. has
an important place in the prophylaxis of tubercle.
He noted that sheep eating Drosera leaves
acquire a nocturnal cough and die, and that the
pleura of cats to which Drosera had been administered were found studded with tubercles. He
commended it in cases of declared tuberculosis
as well. He gave it in the low potencies.

Buchmann of Alvensleben agreed with Hahnemann that Dros. in high potency should not
be often repeated. Buchmann had a bronchial

and fall, characterized by a violent tickling cough,
which almost drove him to distraction at night.
Buchmann cured himself with Dros. 1x. and
tincture. A single dose as soon as the tickling in
the larynx commenced sufficed to allay it at once
and allowed him to rest and it was only repeated

COMMENTS - George Royal wrote of his experiences with Echi-p. He used it for furuncles
with a dry skin. Small boils ("cat-boils"), very
sensitive and seemed to come in crops, more
about the neck and shoulders. Carbuncles with
profuse sanguino-purulent discharge, marked
large sloughing, coming in crops mostly about
the neck, sometimes on perineum.
Royal would usually give such patients five
drops of the 1st every three hours and apply a
hot solution of 1 part of the tincture to 9 of water;
changing the application often. He noted that it
could be used in a similar manner to treat bruised
or lacerated wounds.
It cured a case of a strumous, young bricklayer
whose hand and fingers were to be amputated
because of symptoms of sepsis (i.e.,enlargement
of the glands under the arms and temperature).
Echinacea 1c internally and tincture locally
checked the sepsis and saved the fingers. In
this case the skin and muscles were brought
as nearly as possible to normal position and
the Echinacea applied and changed every hour
for 48 hours.
Royal used it successfully, only once, for suppurative appendicitis, i.e., after pus had formed and
evacuated into the intestines. Mere. and Hepar
had both failed, but Echinacea 1c, five drops
every night and morning for three weeks, cured.
Used with success in recurring attacks of
chronic inflammation about the cecum, and in a
few cases of typhoid when the tired feeling was
the ranking symptom.

The toxicity of ergot has been known for a long
time, manifested by the medieval epidemics of
Saint Anthony's Fire due to the consumption
of contaminated fiour. Its oxytocic and abortive
powers are also well known.
The insoluble polypeptide alkaloids are
stimulants of smooth tissues, especially uterine
and vascular. Affects the sympathetic system,
counteracts the effects of adrenalin. Ergotinine,
the extract of ergot of rye, is used in allopathic
medicine, as a constrictor of blood vessels to
encourage hemostasis, as in uterine and pulmonary hemorrhages.
Ergot. acts by causing contraction of the arterioles and its effect is produced most promptly when
it is administered by subcutaneous injection. Its
homeopathic use are in the main identical with
those of Sec., but Ergot. will sometimes succeed
when Sec. fails.

W. K. Leonard reported the following case of
a young Methodist minister, apparently healthy,
who was just over his twelfth attack of kidney colic.
The attacks had recurred at intervals of two
to four weeks and lasted from one to three
days. They were so weakening as to keep him
incapacitated in the intervals.
He had old-school treatment including morphine and quinine, without benefit. The attacks
were accompanied with severe nervous chills
and it was for these that the quinine had been
prescribed. Ery-a. tincture, five drops three times
a day, put an end to the trouble.

EUPHORBIA AMYGDALOIDES
(Wood Spurge)
PHARMACY - euph-a. Euphorbia amygdaloides.
Wood spurge. Euphorbia sylvatica. N. 0 .
Euphorbiacae. Middle and Southern Europe.
Tincture of plant. Planets: Moon. Historical dose:
All potencies.
CLINICAL - Antrum, pain. Anus, spasms, prolapse.
Debility. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hemorrhoids. Skin,
eruptions.Smell,illusion.Spleen disorders. Throat,
soreness.
HOMEOPATHIC - Produces irritation and burning
sensations of the intestinal tract with vomiting and
diarrhea. Dark brown, watery, mucus stools.
sometimes mixed with solid feces. Sometimes
offensive with blood, mostly in afternoon. Diarrhea, stools difficult with painful anal spasm.
If stool lasts two or three days there is prolapse
returning very gradually, if replaced within half
an hour the bowel generally prolapses again. If
the diarrhea lasts longer, external hemorrhoids
appear, not returning with the prolapse.
Rheumatic pains come on when heated. Malaise, tired weak feeling during and after walking.
Restlessness all night, turning about half awake
and half asleep. Pain in antrum. Sense of taste
blunted. Cold water relieves burning in back of
throat (Caps., burning worse from cold water).
Skin disorders. Symptoms go from right to left.
Abdomen - Tightness, stitch in region of
spleen. Sensation as if a long worm writhing
in region of transverse colon or duodenum.
Throbbing in groins.
Liver - Severe stitches in liver, when walking
up a hill.
Lungs- Heat in chest, radiating from stomach.
Feeling as if lungs remained partly inflated.
Hoarseness.
Modalities - Better after eating. Worse evening. Worse from walking.
Rectum - Feeling or action of the liver, followed by griping and passing of offensive flatus.
Offensive diarrhea, followed by slight prolapse
rendering sitting uneasy,going offgradually. Stool
difficult from painful spasm of anus, continued
after the evacuation.
Sensations -Illusion of smell, "odor ofmice."
Seething sensation in the head and thigh.

PHARMACY-fagu. Fagussilvatica. Beechnut Fagus

and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Convulsions. Epilepsy. Headaches.
Hydrophobia. Rabies. Vertigo.
HOMEOPATHIC-Knowledge ofthis remedy is derived
from the ill effects of eating the nuts, among which
are dread of liquids and salivation, suggesting its
use in hydrophobia or rabies. It is said that the nuts
would disorder the head like darnel;hogs grow stupid
and drowsy by feeding on them.
Trembling, convulsions with periodic spasms,
stiffness and coldness have been observed,
pointing to nerve irritation. Swelling of the mouth
and headache were noted in one case. In some
instances, death has resulted from the effects
of the nuts.
COMMENTS - Dr. E. Berridge contributed a case in
wh1ch "a boy aged 13 had eaten four days ago a
large quantity of beech nuts. I found him in great
pain,languid and terrified.Aiso,with apprehensions
of present death. Pulse very unequal, sometimes
extremely quick, sometimes languid and intermittent, skin burning violently, mouth fiowing with froth
and saliva.
"Intolerable thirst, entreating for drink, but so
soon as any liquid was brought he seemed to
shudder with equal horror, as if he had been
eating unripe grapes. Soon after eating the nuts
he had been seized with torpor, gloominess and
dread of liquids. He had not been bitten by any
rabid animal.
"Next day, early in the morning, he was the
same, but seemed to talk more in his wildness
and perturbation of mind and his mouth fiowed
with foam more abundantly, the urine he had
voided by night was red and fiery, depositing a
copious turbid white sediment, resembling an
emulsion of beech nuts, subsiding as deep as the
breadth of the finger at the bottom of the vessel.
"A few hours before he died he vomited a porraceous bile after which he died quietly.

FELDSPAR
PHARMACY - feld. Feldspar. Mineral varieties,
containing alumina, silica and oxygen. Planets:
Moon. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Arteriosclerosis. Fainting. Otosclerosis.
Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC -It is a silicate compound containing potassium, sodium and aluminium. Kaolin is
a disintegrated feldspar which has lost its potassium and sodium but has retained the silicate of
aluminium. It is not similar to feldspar in its use.
The chemical composition suggests a use
in arteriosclerosis and those illnesses showing
sclerosis and fibrosis of the tissue.
COMMENTS - Two cases of otosclerosis were
cured clinically, both occurring in patients fortyone years old. Both were nervous, disposed to
tremble, and complained of weakness.
One said he felt if he had been struck on the
head and was about to faint. He had sensations
of heat on hands and feet. His head pained on
moving.
Both cases recovered after many weeks of
treatment. These symptoms are common to
silica and the kalis, hence, the weakness is
characteristic of Feld.
A woman age 38, had had varicose veins
for many years. Her skin injured easily. Under
Feld. she was freed of the pains in the legs. The
tendency of the skin to injure disappeared at the
start of treatment, the varicose veins remained.

818

A woman age 48, was given Feld. for retinal
hemorrhages five months after the attack. At
times she showed glycosuria and was very nervous. After two months treatment, the nervousness and eye affects improved fifty percent, and
she experienced a feeling of general well being.
A woman age 53, received Feld. for fainting
spells resulting from an arteriosclerotic heart.
She suffered from incipient arcus seniles; by
resting in bed she regained normalcy, at least
concerning her domestic work.
A man age 70, with an arteriosclerotic kidney,
suffered from hematuria. Under Feld. he was on
his feet again as an ambulatory patient.
Awoman age 84, with marked arteriosclerosis,
cardiac decompensation and edema received
Feld. and a decoction of Apoc. The dropsy
disappeared.
Several weeks later the dropsy returned,
gangrene of the foot developed, and she died.
A man age 70, with severe dropsy of both
feet, received Feld. and Apoc. He recovered in
two months. We can only guess what the future
holds in store for him.
A woman age 50, with high arterial pressure,
spells of weakness. and nervous exhaustion,
received Feld. in a series of doses. Her complaints disappeared. Chronic cases improve
slowly, quick results should not be expected in
these cases.

Ever since ancient times, fennel has enjoyed
a rich history. As far back as Hippocrates can its
employment be traced. ln most of the old books

use as a modifier and corrective of cathartic
infusions, to prevent bloating, and flatulence.

of increasing the secretion of milk, (galactagogue.) The infusion of the seed can be used
without limitation. Herbal formulas are used
combining the fennel with anise seed, parsley
root, licorice root, etc.

appetite, breast enlargement, promoting menstruation, improving digestive system, increasing
breast milk flow and urine flow.
Rich in phytoestrogens. Fennel ·is also used

Fennel is also commonly used to treat heartbum, high blood pressure and to boost sexual

prevents formation of gas in the intestinal tract.
Fennel has anti"acidic and anti-spasmodic properties, it relieves intestinal spasms or cramps.
Fennel relaxes the smooth muscle lining the
digestive tract, makes it an antispasmodic. It is a
remedy for gas,acid stomach, gout, cramps, colic

after radiation and chemotherapy treatments to
help rebuild the digestive system.

(Trigonella foenum graecum)
PHARMACY -trig-f-g.Fenugreek. Trigonella foenum
graecum. Foenumgraecum officinale. North

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Baldness. Beriberi.

lmpotence.lndigestion.lnfections. Leg, edema.

HERBAL-Fenugreek is native to southem Europe,
the Mediterranean region and Western Asia.
Fenugreek seeds contain a high percentage of
mucilage, a natural gummy substance present
in the coatings of many seeds. Although it does
not dissolve in water, mucilage forms a thick,
gooey mass when exposed to fluids.
The resulting soft mass is not absorbed by the
body, but instead passes through the intestines
and also triggers intestinal muscle contractions.
Both actions promote the emptying of intestinal
contents. Therefore, fenugreek is a mild but
effective laxative.
In addition, fenugreek seeds contain chemicals
that slow down the time that food takes to go
through the intestinal tract. As one result, sugars
are absorbed from foods more slowly and blood
sugar levels may not rise as high or fluctuate as
much as usual.
Fenugreek may further affect blood sugar
levels by decreasing the activity of an enzyme
that is involved in releasing stored sugar from
the liver into the blood.

Fenugreek
Fenugreek lowers cholesterol levels as well as
blood sugar levels. It may reduce the amounts of
calcium oxalate in the kidneys. Calcium oxalate
often contributes to kidney stones.
Fenugreek also appeared to lessen the chance
of developing colon cancer. It may have some
ability to protect the liver against damage from
alcohol and other chemicals.
Fenugreek is also used for hair care as it

natural color.

Cured a case of compound capsular cataract

In the second, Ferr-ma. was given at once and
the effect was speedy and marked.
Teste noted the case of a patient who had a
very unpleasant experience with the medicine.
He suffered from a mercurial neurosis and was
very sensitive to medicines. Teste was led to
give the medicine due to a painful contraction
of the posterior cervical muscles, against which
no remedy he had tried had produced any effect.
Teste gave Ferr-ma., four globules in a tumbler
of water, two tablespoonfuls every day. The first
tablespoonful, taken in the morning, seemed to
produce a sensible improvement.

A quarter of an hour after the second dose,

This lasted one hour and did not pass off entirely

he uttered heart-rending cries."

HERBAL - Flaxseed is known in many parts of the

sold in the United States is not food grade and is sold
instead for use as a wood finish and preservative.
Flaxseed is the seed of the flax plant, which
may have originated in Egypt. A rich source of
healing compounds, flaxseed has been cultivated
for more than 7000 years.
This plant has served not only as a food source
and source of linen, but also for the creation of
sails on sailing ships, bowstrings,and body armor.
In the 8th century, King Charlemagne believed
so strongly in the health benefits of flaxseed
that he passed laws requiring his subjects to
consume it. Now, thirteen centuries later, some
experts say we have research to back up what
Charlemagne suspected.
The most common herbal use of flaxseed is
as a laxative; it is also used for hot flashes and
breast pain.
Flaxseed oil has different traditional uses,
including treating arthritis. Both flaxseed and
flaxseed oil have been used for high cholesterol
levels and in an effort to prevent cancer.
Flaxseed oil and other omega-3 fatty acids
are helpful in treating a variety of conditions.
Omega-3 fatty acids have been shown to reduce
inflammation and help prevent certain chronic
diseases, such as heart disease and arthritis.

Prostate-Fight prostate problems,male infertility

Sjogren's syndrome -Sjogren's syndrome is an

attacks glands in the body that produce moisture,

Sjogren's syndrome.
Skin -Treat acne, eczema, psoriasis, sunburn

rosacea often respond to the Essential Fatty Acid's
anti-inflammatory actions and overall skin-soothing
properties. Sunbumed skin may heal faster when
treated with the oil as well. In cases of acne, the
EFAs encourage thinning of the oily sebum that
dogs pores.
Women- Treat menopausal symptoms, menstrual cramps, female infertility and endometriosis.
Because the hormone-balancing lignans and plant
estrogens (phytoestrogens) in flaxseed oil help
stabilize a woman's estrogen-progesterone ratio,
they can have beneficial effects on the menstrual
cyde,and relieve the hot flashes of perimenopause
and menopause.
COMMENTS - Flaxseed oil is available in liquid and

The highest quality flaxseed products are made
using fresh pressed seeds, bottled in dar1< containers, and processed at low temperatures in the
absence of light, extreme heat, or oxygen.
Flaxseed oil comes from the seed of the flax
plant. It contains 50 - 60% omega-3 fatty acids in
the fonn of alpha-linolenic acid (AlA). Flaxseed oil
contains both omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids,

FRAXINUS EXCELSIOR
(European Ash)
PHARMACY - frax-e. Fraxinus excelsior. European
ash. Common ash. N. 0 . Oleaceae. Tincture of
the leaves. The fresh leaves are pounded to a pulp
and macerated with two parts by weight of alcohol.
Planets: Satum. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Gout. Joint, disorders. Joint,
pains. Rheumatism.
HERBAL -Ash leaves were highly recommended by
the medical alchemist Dr. Rademacher and were
extensively used in Germany on his suggestion. In
the Union Med1cal for Nov. 27, 1852, two French
physicians, Drs. Pouget and Peyraud, detailed
several case of gout and rheumatism cured by an
infusion of ash-leaves in boiling water. Dr. Peyraud
himself was one of those relieved.
A commercial traveler, who had been gouty
for twenty years and had saturated himself with
the syrup of Boubee and other vaunted specifics,
consulted Dr. Pouget. At this time he was almost
constant prisoner in his room successive attacks.
After eleven days' use of the infusion he was
able to walk two kilometers (one and a quarter
miles), in fifteen days he resumed his journeys
and was able to travel without suffering from
Bordeaux to Quimper.
Acute and chronice painful gout and rheumatism. Joint rheumatism in numerous instances.

F

Fraxinus excelsior

COMMENTS - Anshutz recorded the case of Dr.
Peyraud. In 1842, Peyraud had his first attack of
gout, which was severe and lasted for twenty-frve
days. During the three following years the attacks
increased in frequency and severity.
Having derived little benefit from the remedial
means that he had resorted to, he listened to the
suggestion of one of his patients, an inhabitant
of the department of Dordogne in France, who
advised him to try an infusion of ash leaves.
Informing Peyraud, at the same time, that his
forefathers had been cured by this prescription
and that many of the country people got rid of
"their pains" by employing it.
Dr. Peyraud took the infusion of ash leaves
and from 1845 to 1849 had no fit of gout. He
then had an attack, which yielded in five days
to the infusion of ash leaves, used under the
observation of Dr. Pouget.
Dr. Pouget recalled that when he was a physician at Soreze in 1824, the peasants of that place
had spoken to him of the great power which an
infusion of ash leaves had in driving away pains.
He afterwards discovered that it had been used
forty years ago as a gout specific by the peasants of Auvergne .

HERBAL -Allium sativum,commonlyknown as garlic,
is a species in the onion genus, Allium. Garlic has
been used as a condiment from ancient times and
also as a remedy against wonns and fevers. It has
a reputation of lowering the blood pressure.
Garlic has a history of human use of over 7,000
years, it is native to central Asia, and has long been
a staple in the Mediterranean region, as well as a
frequent seasoning in Asia, Africa, and Europe.
Garlic has been known as a universal savory
ingredient, even a food in its own righ~ ever since
the ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans ate the
pungent bulb in large quantities.
Hippocrates, the father of natural medicine
used garlic in infectious diseases and particula~
prescribed it for intestinal disorders. The wor1<ers
building the Egyptian Pyramids were fed garlic,
onions and leeks, and garlic was an essential part
of the rations for Roman legions.
12th century Gennan mystic Hildegarde von
Bingen recommended simmering garlic in water for
twenty minutes and drinking the "tea" for bronchial
problems like asthma. This treatment is still in use
in many cultures. Three doves of garlic in boiling
water is also used as a topical cure for athlete's foot
Additionally, garlic was used extensively in the
battlefields during World War I {1914-1918) to treat
and dress wounds and infections. Being a natural
antibiotic and widely available, it was the most effective antiseptic available at the time.

HERBAL-Gent-q. is a pleasant bitter and appears,

has a popular reputation in Ohio and other parts of
the United Statesas an anti-periodic and tonic.Valuable tonic forold cases ofdyspepsia and torpid liver.
Dr. Yelvington of Susquehanna, who said he
learned its value from a tribe of Native Americans,
said it has succeeded in obstinate intermittents
where quinine and other anti-periodics had failed.
He used the decoction of the herb, but a fluid
extract or the saturated tincture is a better form
for administration in fever.
Yelvington also used it in casesof infantile fever
and cholera infantum. "As a tonic in enfeebled
patients and in chronic diseases, it is a remedy
par excellence, appearing to exert an action
over organs of nutrition and assimilation, as well
as being a stimulant to the excretory organs."

Ginger, tea • Make with fresh ginger root Grate

HERBAL - Graviola is a rainforest plant that has
been part of the natural and traditional medicine
of Central and South America and the Caribbean
for centuries. It has an extremely wide range of
medicinal properties, which are distributed through
the different parts of the plant.
The Graviola bar1<, leaves and roots can be made
into a soothing medicinal tea, taken as a sedative
or an antispasmodic. The bar1< can also be used
to treat fever, and the leaves are used topically to
speed the healing of wounds.
The Graviola fruit or juice is taken to reduce fever,
counteract diarrhea and dysentery, and kill wonns
and other parasites. The unripe fruit is especially
prized as a digestive aid.
Antiviral, antibacterial,anti-fungal properties.The
Graviola seeds are also a potent anti-parasitic and
are used traditionally as a remedy for lice.
In the Amazon region, the bar1<, leaves and roots
are used by diabetics to stabilize blood sugar. In the
Andean mountain ranges of Peru, graviola leaves
arebrewedtodischargemucusandsootheinflamed
mucous membranes.
The leaf tea is taken as a heart tonic in Guyana,
a liver remedy in Brazil,and atreatment for asthma,
coughs and flu in the West Indies. It is also used
for arthritis and rheumatism, and some mothers
eat and drink the graviola fruit to increase lactation.
Anti-inflammatory- Graviola has been used to
relieve pain and lnflammation.Anti-inflammatory
activities of the ethanol extract from Graviola
leaves were investigated!. These results suggest that Graviola maybe an active source of
substances with anti-inflammatory activities.
Arthritis • Mixtures made with the graviola
leaf were often used externally to ease the pain
of arthritis, rheumatism and neuralgia.
Cancer· The large,dark leaves are commonly
used in various home remedies for treating depression and cancer.Annonaceous acetogenins
found in graviola leaf and other parts of the graviola plant have the ability to destroy cancerous
cells without affecting healthy ones.Acetogenins
and other secondary metabolites, including
alkaloids, of this plant possess demonstrable
ability to decrease the growth of cancer.
Blood, pressure· Research also bears outthe
traditional use of graviola tea as a hypotensive,
a remedy for high blood pressure.
