HERBAL - Camellia sinensis is the species of plant
whose leaves and leaf buds are used to produce the
popular beverage called tea. White tea, green tea,
oolong, pu-erh tea and black tea are all harvested
from this species, but are processed differently to
attain different levels of oxidation.
Green tea has been used as both a beverage
and a medicine in most of Asia to help everything
from controlling bleeding and helping heal wounds
to regulating body temperature, blood sugar and
promoting digestion.
Alzheimer's disease - Both green and black
tea were effective in improving memory and slowing the development ofAlzheimer's, though green
tea was found to be more effective than black.
Antioxidants - The polyphenols present in
green tea may help prevent and repair damage
from sun exposure by fighting free radicals that
damage cells. UV radiation can damage DNA.
which can then cause immune system suppression, which may create a risk for developing
skin cancer.
Anti-aging - Regular consumption of green
tea can effectively delay symptoms of aging.
The free radicals are responsible for corroding
the body, i.e. foraging and the related symptoms.
The catechin polyphenols present in green tea
are mainly responsible for the anti-oxidizing effects, the most powerful among them being the
epigallocatechin gallate.
Asthma - The leaves have been used in
traditional Chinese medicine to treat asthma.
Astringency- This is yet another benefit from
green tea. It triggers contraction in muscles and
tissues and tones up muscles and skin. Even if
you do not drink green tea, a mere mouthwash
with this daily will cause contraction in gums to
keep them firm and tight on teeth and thus prevent
loosening and falling of teeth for long. Wash your
hair with it and see them grow stronger each day.
Bones- Green tea has been found to improve
bone mineral density and strength. Studies have
found that epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG), a
component of green tea, blocks the activity of two
molecules, IL-6 and cyclooxygenase-2 (Cox-2),
which play a role in breaking down bone. Habitual
green tea drinkers have stronger, denser bones.

Antioxidants - Hawthorn berries contain flavonoids such as quercitin,and oligomeric procyanidins.
Exposure to radiation, cigarette smoke, air pollution
and some medications can increase the amount of
free radicals 1n the body. Hawthorn berries' antioxidants can prevent damage from these free radicals,
thus protecting against cancers and heart disease.
Anti-aging -Free radicals are known tocontribute
to the aging process as well as the development of a
number of health problems including heart disease.
Antioxidants found in hawthorn can neutralize free
radicalsand may reduce or even help prevent some
of the damage they cause.
Anxiety - Hawthorn tea is helpful for dealing
with anxiety. The main symptoms of anxiety which
hawthorn efficiently treats are chest tightness as
well as heart palpitations.
Arteriosclerosis - Hawthorn berries said to
have a solvent power upon calcareous deposits in
arteries. This herb has antioxidant properties that
help protectagainst the formation of plaques,which
leads to atherosclerosis. Plaque buildup may cause
chest pain (angina) and heart attacks while plaque
buildup in the arteries that supply blood to the brain
may result 1n stroke.
Blood, pressure -A specific use for hawthorn
berries is the treatment of orthostatic hypotension,
a sudden loss of blood pressure caused by moving from a seated position to a standing position.
Orthostatic hypotension can cause temporary loss
of consciousness, and is a common complication
during the first few weeks of medical treatment of
high blood pressure with beta-blockers.
Blood, pressure, low-Hawthorn berries are also
good for low blood pressure. Shortness of breath,
worse exertion. Weak heart and poor circulation
can cause low blood pressure

vascular insufficiency, blood clots (embolism,
phlebitis). Dilates coronary vessels to restore the
heart muscle wall.
Chest, pain -Hawthorn berry preparations have
been shown to combat chest pain, a health problem
caused by insufficient blood flow to the heart. Hawthorn improves the blood flow to the heart allowing
one to exercise for longer periods of time without
suffering from chest pain.

Burnett noted "On July 3, 1880, a young
lady, age 15, came under my observation with
an exostosis on her right os calcis. somewhat
smaller an a little flatter than half a walnut shell.
It was at times painful.
"Patient was in other respects in good health
and well nourished, but her teeth were not very
sound. She goes blue in winter, and suffers also
very badly from chilblains both on hands and
feet, worse on hand.
"Hecla lava 2c given six grains three times a
day. July 17th.The exostosis is decidedly smaller;
it never pains now. September 25. The exostosis
has entirely disappeared; the two heels being
compared, no difference between them now
can be discovered."
Burnett stated "I have cured several bony
tumours of the jaws with the same remedy, and
that very promptly: they were all of recent origin."

and where one desires to work without having the

Cooper, who studied the Hellebores very

sensation" more intensely than any other drugs.
The winter aconite (Eranthis hyemalis), a close

HELICOBACTER PYLORI
(Ulcer Bacteria)
PHARMACY - Helicobacter pylori. (H. pylori). A
digestive tract bacteria. "Helico" means spiral,
which indicates that the bacteria are spiral shaped.
Planets: Moon, Jupiter. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Abdominal, pain. Anemia. Anorexia.
Belching. Bloated. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Fainting.
Fatigue. Fever. Gastritis. Halitosis. Heartburn.
Hypotension .Indigestion. Nausea.Peptic ulcers.
Stomach, cancer. Stomach, pain. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weight loss.
HOMEOPATHIC - H. pylori is a type of bacteria that
grows in the digestive tract and has a tendency to
attack the stomach lining. Infection with H. pylori is
common. It was discovered in 1982 by two Australian researchers who also found that it causes
peptic ulcers.
About two-thirds of the world's population has it
in their bodies. For most people, it doesn't cause
ulcers or any other symptoms.
H.pylori infection comes from food,water, orutensils. It's more common in countries or communities
that lack clean water or good sewage systems. You
can also pick up the bacteria through contact with
the saliva or other body fluids of infected people.
Symptoms of H. pylori infections are excessive
burping, feeling bloated, nausea, heartburn, fever, lack ofappetite, or anorexia and unexplained
weight loss. The pain is usually described as a
gnawing pain, and it may come and go.
H. pylori enters your body and it attacks the lining
of your stomach. Which usually protects you from
the acid your body uses to digest food. Once the
bacteria have done damage, acid can get through
the lining, which leads to ulcers.

961

Helicobacter pylori

These may bleed, cause infections,or keep food
from moving through your digestive tract.
Symptoms of a stomach ulcer might include a
dull or burning pain in the upper belly area. The
pain is sometimes worse at night or when the
stomach is empty. There may be temporary relief
from taking an antacid, but the pain comes back.
Symptoms of gastritis often include upper belly
pain, nausea, and vomiting. These complications
require immediate medical attention.
Possible warning signs include:severe stomach
pain, black or tarry stool, stool with bright red blood,
vomit with bright red blood, vomit that looks like
coffee grounds, feeling weak or short of breath,
feeling dizzy or faint, chills or fever
COMMENTS- There is no known way to prevent H.
pylori infection, but experts recommend: Washing
hands before eating and after using the restroom.
Eating food that has been handled and prepared
safely. Drinking only clean, safe drinking water.
RELATIONS- Compare: (1) China off. Nux vomica.
Arsenicum alb.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

Belden described it as "an ugly, disagreeablelooking creature, the head long and blunt, eyes
black and bead-like, tail half the length of the
body, thick-set and club-like. The entire body
cased in athinly coated armor, marked curiously
with yellow and black." Its skin is studded with nail
or tuberde-like heads.
The venom is alkaline in reaction. A number
of cases of bites are on record. A dog bitten in
the nose "uttered fearful howls and when after
great difficulty, he was released, had symptoms
like 'blind staggers,' began turning around in a
circle and died in twenty minutes."
Ayoung miner bitten in the leg, through in robust
health at the time, at once began to lose flesh,
became melancholic and died in a few months
like a person with rapid tuberculosis.
A Native American woman bitten in the leg
survived, but the leg shriveled and she became
a semi-idiot, though she lived over thirty years
after. The writer of an article quoted by the
Recorder from the New York Sun related her
case, describing the effect as:
"Where the person survives an hour or two
after the bite, the agony is described as awful
to witness. The poison goes through the human
system with rapidity and causes unspeakable
pain and excruciating agony from head to foot.
Though paralyzed, every muscle, bone, sinew
and nerve is keenly alive to intense pain. The
sufferer's head seems as if it would split open.
Very few persons bitten can speak after the first
fifteen minutes, but unconsciousness seldom
comes until a few minutes before death."
Belden noted its reputation of being fatal to
drinkers and to affect non-drinkers less severely.
This is borne out somewhat by the recovery of
Mr. Vail of Tucson, a man of temperate habits,
after a bite: and the death of a man bitten while
drunk, after lingering several months.
This lingering nature of the poison is markedly
different from snake poisons, which generally kill
quickly, if at all.
Mr. Vail said his suffering was intense. the
pain proceeding from the wounded part to the
head and back. Immediately after receiving the
wound, which was on his index finger, both wrist
and finger were tightly bandaged.

Marvin A. Custis reported a case. "Mrs. L,
28, has two children, both living. Has prolapse
of uterus, ulceration of cervix, dark offensive
leucorrhea. Her system is worn out and her
expression one of great distress.
"Irritable, finds fault with every one and cannot bear contradiction. Restless, wants to move
around, as she feels better when mind and body
are employed.
"She had a severe backache and a sore and
heavy feeling in the womb, she said she was
always 'conscious of her womb.'
"Helon. 30c every three hours for two days,
and then every night, was prescribed with a
warm water injection night and morning. At the
end of three weeks the leucorrhea had almost
ceased, the womb was in the first position and
she 'forgets that she has such an organ.'"
L. L. Danforth treated Mrs. W., who had intense
pruritus, vulvar and vaginal, for several weeks.
"She could tear the flesh out" it was so intense.
There was vulvovaginitis, the labia and adjoining
skin were red, swollen and covered with thin
white, curdy deposits.
'
Further examination showed a thin, albuminous leucorrhea pouring from a congested cervix,
evidently the cause of the pruritus. The leucorrhea
coagulated on the vagina, forming small curds
covering the mucous membrane of vagina and
vulva. Helon.tincture on tablets speedily relieved.
S. A. Jones found that Helon. turned an alkaline urine acid, and increased the amount of
urea as well as the amount of urine secreted.
Jones considered this the result·of a condition
of debility, venous paresis, the result of previous
arterial tonic contraction.

HEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE
(Influenza Nosode)
PHARMACY-Hemophilus influenzae,type-b. (HIB).
Planets: Mars. Historical dose: Tincture and all
potencies.
CLINICAL - Arthritis. Back, pains. Breath, bad.
Cellulitis. Conjunctivitis. Convulsions. Coughs.
Diarmea. Endocarditis. Epiglottitis. Eye, swelling. Fevers. Headaches. Hearing, difficulties.
Hypotonia.lnfections. Meningitis. Nausea. Neck,
pains. Neck, stiffness. Osteomyelitis. Otitis media.
Pericarditis. Peritonitis. Pneumonia. Photophobia.
Respiratory, infections. Septicaemia. Sinusitis.
Sleep, problems. Sore throat. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The World Health Organization
estimates that Hib causes three million episodes
of serious disease and 400,000 deaths annually
worldwide.
Hemophilus influenzae type b causes pneumonia, septicaemia, meningitis, epiglottitis, septic
arthritis, cellulitis, otitis media. and purulent
pericarditis, as well as less common invasive
infections such as endocarditis, osteomyelitis,
and peritonitis.
Symptoms and signsofHib meningitis are indistinguishable from other causes of bacterial meningitis
and include fever, headache, photophobia, stiff
neck, vomiting and altered mental status.
Severe cases may present with convulsions and
coma. Infants often present with less characteristic
symptoms such as, vomiting, refusal to feed and
irritability. Severe cases may develop hypotonia,
a tense or bulging fontanelle, a high-pitched or
moaning cry and convulsions.
Septicaemia is the second most common
presentation, acoounting for around a quarter of
all confirmed cases of invasive Hib disease, and
can affect all ages.

from ear(s),loss of balance. hearing difficulties, ear
pain, nausea and vomiting, diarmea, decreased
appetite, congestion.

HOMEOPATHIC- "LiverofSulphur''isa name given
by the old alchemists to several sulphur compounds
whose color was supposed to resemble that of the
liver. Before Hahnemann's time, Hep., Sulfuret
of lime, was used as an external remedy for itch,
rheumatism, gout, goiter and scrofulous swellings.
Hahnemann prepared Hep. with oyster shells
instead of ordinary lime. As it is a chemical combination of Calc. and Sulph., it has some of the
properties of both, but is very different from either
and though 11 is useful to compare them, Hep.
must be studied as a separate entity.
Material doses were used in pellagra. The
higher potencies may abort the suppuration, the
lower promote it. If it is necessary to hasten it,
give 2x. Hep.; 1x will often start secretions and
profuse drainage in stuffy colds.
In 1794, Hahnemann proposed to use it
internally to arrest mercurial salivation. A few
years later it was tried for asthma and pulmonary
tuberculosis, with success.
It acts on the mucous membranes, causing
croupy, catarrhal process with a tendency to
hemorrhage and ulceration. Tendency to suppuration. Lesions spread by the formation of
small papules around the side of the old lesions.
The catarrh may be in the throat, stomach,
uterus, or urethra, and is characterized by
thick, yellow, acrid, ropy discharge. Mucus
in the stools, the urine, and is hawked up. Easy
perspiration with mucus. Infected sinus with
pus formation .

P. Foster distinguished between Hep., Cale-s.

whole was absorbed without breaking.

Herpes simplex

HERPES SIMPLEX
(Herpes Nosode)
PHARMACY- Herpes simplex virus. Planets: Venus.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Cold sores. Fatigue. Fever. Fever
blisters. Fevers. Genital herpes. Glands,swelling.
Headaches. Mouth, sores. Viral infections.
HOMEOPATHIC - The herpes simplex virus, also
known as HSV, is an infection that causes herpes.
Herpes can appear in various parts of the body,
most commonly on the genitals or mouth. There
are two types of the herpes simplex virus.
HSV-1: primarily causes oral herpes,and isgenerally responsible for cold sores and fever blisters
around the mouth and on the face.
HSV-2: primarily causes genital herpes, and is
generally responsible for genital herpes outbreaks.
Some of the symptoms associated with this virus
include:blistering sores (in the mouth or on the genitals) pain during urination,(genital herpes) itching.
You may also experience symptoms that are
similar to the flu. These symptoms can include:
fever, swollen lymph nodes, headaches, tiredness, lack of appetite.
RELATIONS- Compare: (1) Nat-m. Rhus tox.
REFERENCES - Murphy.
HERPES ZOSTER
(Shingles Nosode)
PHARMACY - Herpes zoster. Planets: Venus. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bell's palsy. Blisters. Encephalitis.
Eye, infections. Facial paralysis. Fatigue. Fevers.
Headaches. Hearing loss. Itching. Nerve pains.
Neurological problems. Photophobia. Pneumonia.
Postherpetic neuralgia. Rash. Shingles. Skin
infections. Viral infections. Vision loss.
HOMEOPATHIC - Shingles is a viral infection that
causes a painful rash. Shingles is caused by the
varicella-zoster virus. The same virus that causes
chickenpox. After you've had chickenpox, the virus
lies inactive in nerve tissue near your spinal cord
and brain. Years later, the virus may reactivate as
shingles.

977

Herpes zoster

Thesigns and symptoms of shingles usually affect
only a small section of one side of your body. the
shingles rash develops as a stripe of blisters
that wraps around either the left or right side of
your torso. Sometimes the shingles rash occurs
around one eye or on one side of the neck or face.
These signs and symptoms may include:
Shingles can be very painful. Pains are burning,
numbness or tingling. Sensitivity to touch. A red
rash that begins a few days after the pain. The
pain and rash occur near an eye. If left untreated,
this infection can lead to pennanent eye damage.
Skin infections.Before the rash appears,people
often have pain, itching, or tingling in the area
where it will develop.This mayhappen several days
before the rash appears. Fluid-filled blisters that
break open and crust over. Itching. Some people
also experience: Fevers, headaches, sensitivity to
light and fatigue. If shingles blisters aren't properly
treated, bacterial skin infections may develop.
Complications from shingles can include:
Postherpetic neuralgia. For some people,
shingles pain continues long after the blisters have
cleared. This condition is known as postherpet1c
neuralgia,and it occurs when damaged nerve fibers
send confused and exaggerated messages of pain
from your skin to your brain.
Vision loss. Shingles in or around an eye (ophthalmic shingles) can cause painful eye infections
that may result in vision loss.
Neurological problems. Depending on which
nerves are affected, shingles can cause an inflammation of the brain (encephalitis), facial paralysis,
or hearing or balance problems.
COMMENTS -Afewpeople who get shingles develop
pneumonia, hearing loss,or encephalitis a disease
that causes the brain to swell. Shingles can cause
Bell's palsy, in which a facial nerve is paralyzed.
RELATIONS- Compare: (1) Nat-m. Rhus tox.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

HERBAL - Hibiscus tea is a tisane or "herbal tea'
consumed both hot and cold by people around the
world.The drink is an infusion made from crimson
or deep magenta colored calyces (sepals) of the
Hibiscus sabdariffa flower.
Hibiscus tea is made from the part of the
hibiscus plant called the calyx, the green layer
that protects the petals while they are budding.
Hibiscus tea has a tart, cranberry-like flavor,
and sugar is often added to sweeten the beverage. The tea contains vitamin C and minerals
and is used traditionally as a mild medicine. The
tea is red colored, and has a fruity, tart flavor
similar to cranberry. It is often served cold, and
usually with a generous dose of honey or sugar.
North Africans have used hibiscus internally
for supporting upper respiratory health including the throat throat and also use it topically to
support skin health
In Europe, hibiscus has been employed to support upper respiratory health, alleviate occasional
constipation, and promote proper circulation.
Hibiscus tea has been a traditional cure for
nervous restlessness and in occasional difficulty of
sleeping.Helps support memory and concentration.
Hibiscus tea is rich in vitamin C, minerals and
antioxidants. Antispasmodic, anthelmintic and
antibacterial. Diuretic, cholerectic, febrifugal
and hypotensive.
Acne - The red hibiscus flowers have skin
benefits at the same time. It is often used as a
natural cure for acne. If you want to fight acne,
soak the hibiscus flowers in water for a few hours
and then grind them into a paste. Mix with honey
and apply on the acne skin.

HOMEOPATHIC - Hippoz. is a powerful nosode

noticeable, the skin being chiefly affected with
deposits in the lungs. Homeopathic preparations
of both have been made.
In horses, glanders affects the lungs and the
upper respiratory tract, causing coughs and disseminated ulcerations and deposits throughout
the lungs. Mallein, atoxin prepared from glanders,
was used in veterinary practice as a test injection for deciding whether a horse suspected of
glanders actually has the disease or not. If the
horse reacts it is concluded there is glanders.
In a number of cases in which animals reacted
to the first injections, repetition of the test has
failed to elicit reaction, thus suggesting that Mallein is curative as well as diagnostic.
The nosode has been used by homeopaths, at
the suggestion of Wilkinson, on the phenomena
of the disease as guides. It has been used in a
large number of cases involving low forms of
suppuration and catarrh.

COMMENTS - Burnett had a case of persistent
bleeding from the rectum, the blood was watery
and all the usual hemorrhagic remedies failed
to arrest it. Burnett thought that Hir. might prove
a similar remedy. He had a tincture made and
attenuated, gave the 5c potency and cured
the case.
To make Hir., macerate the end of a leech's
head for twenty minutes in a mixture of sand and
a physiological serum. Centrifuge the liquid and
a green liquid residue is obtained, which is dried
after the addition of thymol.
The substance obtained forms the stock for
the preparation of the potencies. W. Schwabe
of Stuttgart, who prepared this stock, called it
"Hirudin."

Holy basil
Holy basil acts as a powerful adaptogen, assisting the body in maintaining health when faced
with stress, whether physical, psychological, or
environmental.
The medicated oil is used as drops, in the ears
in earache and purulent discharges, and into the
nose in ozaena. The leaves, with lime juice, are
rubbed over ringworm.
The seeds are mucilaginous and used as a
diuretic in scanty urine and cough. The leaves
are expectorant, and given, sweetened with
honey, in chronic cough, especially in children.
The expressed juice of the herb has traditionally
been administered to children who are attacked
with catarrh, cough with fever and constipation,
with very gratifying and beneficial results.
Adaptogen - Holy Basil offers protection from
the many diseases caused by stressors. Basil
leaves are regarded as an 'adaptogen' or antistress agent. Even healthy persons can chew
121eaves of basil, twice a day, to prevent stress.

and free radical scavenging protection. Neutralizes dangerous biochemicals that contribute
to premature aging, cancer, and degenerative
diseases.
Anti-aging - Slows the biological aging process by reducing the impact of physiological
aging factors- such as stress, free radicals and
decreased immunity.
Anti-inflammatory. Reduces the painful and
dangerous inflammation that plays a key role in
various forms of arthritis, cancer and degenerative neurological disorders.
Bronchitis. Holy basil promotes the removal
of the catarrhal matter and phlegm from the
bronchial tube.
Cardiovascular. Lowers dangerous cholesterol and stress-related high blood pressure,
protects the heart and blood vessels, and has
mild blood thinning qualities, thereby decreasing
the likelihood of strokes.
Children. Common problems like cough cold,
fever, diarrhea and vomiting respond favorably
to the juice of basil leaves. If pustules of chicken

taken with saffron will hasten them.

PHARMACY- hydr-s. Hydrazinum sulphuricum. Hydrazinesulphate.Planets: Jupiter, Moon. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC- Dr. Joseph Gold, in 1968, wrote a
paper for the Oncology Journal called "Aproposed
treatment of cancer by inhibition of gluconeogenesis" inwhich he noted that Hydr-s., dramatically
reverses cachexia, the wasting-away process
that kills many cancer patients.
"This inexpensive chemical, with little or no
side effects, also has a clinically documented
anti-tumor action. It causes malignant tumors
to stop growing, to reduce in size, and, in some
cases, to disappear.
"A number of cancer patients diagnosed as
terminal have experienced tumor stabilization
and remission through hydrazine sulfate therapy.
About half of all patients who take hydrazine
sulfate experience weight gain, restored appetite,
extended survival time, and a significant reduction
in pain and suffering.

1007

Hydrazinum sulphurlcum

H

"Many patients report an increase in vigor and
strength and the disappearance of symptoms
of the disease, along with feelings otwell-being
and optimism.
"The common types of cancer most frequently
reported to benefit from hydrazine sulfate therapy
are recto-colon cancer, ovarian cancer, prostatic
cancer, lung cancer, Hodgkin's disease and
other lymphomas, thyroid cancer, melanoma.
and breast cancer. Some rare types of cancer
also benefit.
"Hydrazine sulfate is known to produce excitement. lethargy, convulsions, hypotension.
arrhythmias, fatty changes in the liver, hypoglycemia and weight loss.
"Toxicity. If inappropriately high doses of hydrazine sulphate are taken. numbness, nausea,
vomiting, drowsiness and nerve inflammation
may occur. Side effects may include nausea,
some pruritus, diuiness due to low blood sugar,
or peripheral neuritis.
"The following toxic symptoms have been
reported: nausea, vomiting, anorexia, abnormal
sensations affecting both upper and lower limbs,
impaired fine motorfunctions (writing), confusion.
abnormal electromyograms."
COMMENTS - In one case, a sixty-two-year-old
woman with widely disseminated cancer of the
cervix, in a very debilitated condition. was put
on Hydr-s.
After one week, a secondary tumor the size of
an orange had completely disappeared, much
to the amazement of the woman's doctors, and
her neck nodes had become markedly smaller.
After three weeks on the therapy, the patient
had gained weight and was active and in good
spirits. The woman was discharged from the
hospital a short time later.

COMMENTS - A. H. Croucher cured a boy, 3 1/2, of
convulsions with Hydr-ac. The first attack occurred
six months previously. His father's sister had died
of epilepsy.
Before the fits came on he could walk well, but
could not afterwards. The fitsoccurred at intervals
of about three weeks when a succession ofthem
occurred, each lasting about five minutes during
two or three days. During the intervals between
the fils he would generally scream.
In the morning on awaking, the patient cried
out, then convulsions occurred, body and limbs
convulsed, eyelids twitched but remained open,
eyeballs turned up and to right. Seemed quite
unconscious.
Hydr-ac. 2x, one drop three times a day increased afterwards to two drops and continued
for a fortnight. No more convulsions, but three
months later a rash developed all over him.
The characteristic blue tint of Hydr-ac. is apparent after death in some poisoning cases. Livid
spots on limbs,nails violet. In one case there was
a brilliant violent hue all over. The heat is greaUy
disturbed, blueness and coldness of surface.
Marble coldness within and without.
It acts on the medulla and through the vagus
nerve on heart and respiration. Irregular and
gasping breathing. Dry tearing cough, worse at
night. Cough in tuberculosis. The pulse is feeble,
imperceptible. The patient clutches at the heart
as if in distress. Profound prostration.
Persistent and tonic tetanic spasm,without
any reflex excitability (unlike Nux-v.). Paralysis
attacks first the lower, then the upper limbs.Acts
powerfully on the muscles offace,jaws and back.
Pronounced risus sardonicus. Lividity, frothing.

HYDROGEN
(The Element)
PHARMACY - hydrog. Hydrogen. The element.
Planets: Moon. Historical dose: All potencies.
CUNICAL - Acidosis. Alkalosis. Aphthae. Backaches. Congenital deformities. Cystitis. Diarrhea.
Fainting. Fistula. Headaches. Hemorrhoids.
Insomnia. Nevi. Rash. Sprains. Stomach, pains.
Ulcers. Weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC-Hydrogen was the first elementto be
fanned.This primordial element begins Mendeleev's
Periodic Table. It has a positively-charged proton
as tts nucleus and a negatively-charged electroncloud around it.
Hydrogen was proved by Jeremy Sherr and his
team of provers in England. They used modem
hydrogen with its increased tritium content as
it is now.

One patient, a clever lawyer. suffered from
a nervous breakdown and had to abandon his
business entirely. He then had a kind of fit and
became cold and senseless, his face working
much. After that he fell asleep, and had another
attack an hour and a half later.
After this he was suspicious and said that his
wife was poisoning him. He took a single dose
of Hyos. 1,OOOc, given in food or drink without
his knowledge. It was repeated once a week.
He began to improve and in a few months was
restored to health, though some other medicines
were given later on.

W. J. Guernsey related the case of a nine-yearold boy who was bitten by a pet rat on the first
finger of his left hand. Nothing was observed at
the time, but some time after, he became ill and
his state was alarming.
The boy could talk with great difficulty, teeth
firmly locked, conscious, neck so stiff the head
could scarcely be moved. There was more tenderness about the wound than the appearance would
indicate, hence Hyper. was preferred to Led.
It was given (8 p.m.) in the 500c, dissolved in
water, at first every fifteen minutes, later every
two hours. At3 a.m. there was improvement, he
fell asleep and the next morning was practically
convalescent.
Gilchrist said Hyper. 3x, given at intervals of
twenty minutes for twelve hours or longer, seems
to control perfectly the pain following laparotomy.
Roehrig considered Hyper. externally and
internally the nearest thing loa specific in bleeding
hemorrhoids. He gave it to pneumonia patients
who have hemorrhoids, it cured the pneumonia
and prevented the arrest of the flux.
Usher confirmed this, ·pain, bleeding and
tenderness" were his indications. "It seems to suit
the plethoric with great soreness." He used the 1x.

HOMEOPATHIC- Hypothalamus glands are made
up of pure hypothalamic hormones, (vasopressin and oxytocin, combined with a transporting
protein). These hormones are liberated in their
active form, under such stimuli as pain and
modifications in the blood biochemistry, as well
as changes in the volume of the blood.

Hypothalamus gland
The posterior hypophysis is therefore subject
to a direct nervous control. The blood irrigation
of this gland is assured by the vessel gates
which form in the median protuberance and
which traverse the pituitary stem to flow into the
sinusoid of the anterior hypophysis.
Neurons, notably those from the median protuberance, secrete substances which travel down
from the neurons and accumulate at the end ofthe
tissues. When the cells of the median protuber,ance are stimulated, these agents penetrate the
vessel gates and the sinusoid and instigate the
liberating ofthe anterior hypophyseal stimulants.

HERBAL- The smell from spathe and lctod. flowers

the odor of asafetida.
An acrid principle resides in the root, even
when perfectly dry, producing an effect like that
of the Arum and the Ranunculi. When chewed
in the mouth, the root is slow in manifesting its
peculiar taste, but after some moments apricking
sensation is felt, which soon amounts to a disagreeable smarting and continues for some time.
This acrimony is readily dissipated by heat
and the decoction retains none of it. The distilled
water is impregnated with it, if the process is
carefully conducted, but loses it on standing a
short time. To insure a tolerably uniform activity
of this medicine, the root should be kept in dried
slices and not reduced to powder until it is needed.
The bruised leaves are frequently applied to
ulcers and recent wounds with good effect.
They are also used as an external application in
cutaneous disorders and the expressed juice has
been successfully applied to different species of
herpes. The leaves are used to dress blisters
with the view of promoting their discharge.
The Treasury of Botany explains the traditional
uses of this plant in medicine: "The roots in
cases of asthma, the leaves as an application
to.ulcers. The seeds are also considered to be
anti-spasmodic and useful in coughs."

HOMEOPATHIC - This pancreatic hormone plays an
important part in the process of sugar metabolism
in the body. Its capacity to bum sugar into carbon
dioxide and water, thereby helping the body with fat
combustion, has made it very useful in the hands
of the allopathic school saving patients from death
in cases of diabetic acidosis.
If Insulin. is administered at suitable intervals in
diabetes mellitus, the blood sugar is maintained at
a normal level and the urine remains free of sugar.
Restores the ability to oxidize carbohydrates and
to store glycogen in the liver.
It was proved by Dr. William F. Baker, and Dr.
S. K. Ghosh of Calcutta. Some use of Insulin.
homeopathically has been made by Baker,
showing its applicability in acne, carbuncles,
and erythema with itching eczema.

Iris tenax

In the female prover, it produced a strange
sensation in her mind: she though some of her

The most remarkable symptoms were the
"fearful pain in the ileo-cecal region and the hard

The first case concerned Miss A., a schoolteacher, who had for several years a pain beginning in right eye, extending to the right half of
her head. When the pain was most severe, she
vomited a quantity of green bile. When she did
not vomit she had nausea and chill between 2
and 3 p.m. The pain passed off in sleep at night.
It always began on Saturday, before rising.
lris-1. 30x every six hours commencing on

Iris., Aloe. Cimic. and Kali-bi. had failed to give
much relief. The relief from Iris-I. was so marked
the patient thought she had received morphine.
The second case concerned Mr. E., who drank
a large quantity of buttermilk while in a state
of perspiration after walking thirty miles over
a mountainous country in August. Four hours
after, he was taken with fearful pain in ileo-cecal
reg1on. This caused a deathly sensation at his
epigastrium. Finally he vomited much dark green
bile without relief.
An old school doctor was called in and diagnosed obstruction with probable death in four
days. He lingered three weeks and was brought
home to Portland where Dr. Wigg saw him and
diagnosed typhililis, badly treated. Pressure
on the ileo-cecal region caused the death like
sensation at stomach pit. Pain continued until
he vomited a cupful of dark green bile. He was
somewhat constipated.
Under lris-1. 15x every three hours he commenced to improve at once and in two weeks
was back at his business.

Jab. has been used as a remedy for baldness

the popular hair restorer tonics. In a number of
patients taking it, white hair and blonde hair have
been observed to tum black.
Jab. has a reputation for stimulating breast
secretions. A case is quoted from the Lancet in
which a woman whose milk had ceased for a
fortnight received ten drops of the fluid extract
every four hours. The secretion of milk was reestablished, but the patient began to suffer from
extreme nervous excitement accompanied by
a fixed idea that she should murder her family
with a hatchet.
The drug was stopped and these symptoms
disappeared, and with them, the activity of the
breast glands.
Bell commended it in diarrhea with gushing,

is scanty or profuse.

in hot water.

for increased eye-tension which rapidly disappeared. The patient noticed that she passed the

This was followed by extreme coldness of the

The attacks recurred every quarter of an hour

immediately and repealed every half hour. After
the second dose the attacks ceased and he was
able to take bread and milk without sickness. He
had a good night's rest and was perfectly well
the next day.

COMMENTS· The ancient jade carved in China was
what we today call nephrite jade: an amphibolite
mineral. In the 19th Century , it was discovered
that the material from the new world was not the
same mineral as the jade from China.The mineral
from Central America, a pyroxene, was called
jadeite to distinguish it from the original nephrite.
Because of its smooth even texture, jade has
long been a preferred material for carving. The
most common shape is the flat donut-shaped disc
called a pi, which is commonly worn as a necklace. The Emerald Buddha, the sacred image
that is enshrined at Wat Phra Kaeo in Bangkok,
Thailand , is actually beautiful green jadeite.
Good fortune, prosperity. A peaceful stone for
centuries of primary importance to the people
of the Orient (where it is considered to be one
of the most importance symbols of purity and
serentiy). The Chinese referred to jade as the
musical stone, because of the melodic tones it
makes when struck.
For centuries, jade was thought to be a single
gemstone,but in 1863 two types were recognized:
jadeite and nephrite. Jade, Venus: Chinese Stone
of Heaven. Since at least 2950 BC, jade has been
treasured in China as the royal gemstone, yu.
The character for jade resembles a capital! with
a line across the middle: the top represents the
heavens, the bottom the earth, and the center
section, mankind.
The word yu is used in Chinese to call something precious, as in English we use gold. Jade
was thought to preserve the body after death
and can be found in emperors' tombs from
thousands of years ago. One tomb contained
an entire suit made out of jade, to assure the
physical immortality of its owner. For thousands
of years, jade was a symbol of love and virtue
as well as a status symbol.

behind the ear, itching is intense at night so that

Clotar Muller, who experienced the axillary
skin symptoms in his own person, had never
suffered from a skin affection before. One of
the provers was cured of an itching eruption of
the legs from which he had suffered in winter for
four years, the itching commencing as soon as
he began to undress.
Many of the symptoms closely resembled
syphilis and the affection of the cheek in one of
the provers was actually diagnosed as syphilitic
by a doctor who saw him in Muller's absence.
The left side of head, face and abdomen were
mostly affected. Axillary symptoms proceed
from right to left.
In one case, a nurse poisoned her left arm
some years before from septic and possibly
syphilitic cause, inflammation of the axillary
glands ensued, first of the left then of the right,
leaving an eczematous itching condition. The
glands of the groin also became affected.
Elaps. 200c relieved the bulk of the conditions,
but there was still a little irritation in the axilla and
Jug-r. 2c three times a day was given.
Five days after beginning the Jug-r., an eruption of minute vesicles appeared on her back,
itching a great deal. It extended up the center
of her back from sacrum to mid-dorsal region,
spreading out below, tapering above. She had
scratched holes in two places.
The rash was worse afterwashing.AII soreness
and irritation had gone from the arms and axilla.
The rash was antidoted with Rhus-t. 2c. She had
no more trouble with her glands.
Muller observed, "In the digestive organs it
causes derangement and irritation, which simultaneously call forth abnormal symptoms in other
organs, especially in the head. After this action,
which is brief, appear various exanthematous
symptoms, which appear late and run a chronic
course."

COMMENTS - Cases of Kali-ar. poisoning with massive doses present nothing to distinguish them from
cases of other arsenical preparations, but Kali-ar.
has had a short proving and a number of cases of
allopathic provings are on record.
Jonathan Hutchinson recorded a number of
cases of right-sided herpes. One of his patients
observed that, while taking Kali-ar., her sclerotics
became thick and yellow instead of clear and
bluish. The iris, which was blue, became more
gray. Her skin, instead of being fair and florid,
became muddy and older looking.
This was a mystery to Hutchinson as he usually gave Kali-ar. to make the skin clearer, but
he was compelled to record the fact, though he
did not apparently perceive the homeopathic
solution of the mystery.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-bi., with the other chromium preparations, Chr-ac. and Chr-ox., was
introduced into the Materia Medica by Dr. J.
Drysdale. All chromium salts are derived from
potassium bichromate, which is manufactured in
large quantities from chrome-iron-ore. The association of chromium with ferrum is noteworthy.
The bichromate is largely used in dying,
calico-printing, wood staining, photography and
as a solution for producing the current in electric
batteries. Many symptoms were obtained from
workmen engaged in the preparation of the salt,
some of which had been noted before Drysdale
studied the drug.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-c. is potassium carbonate,
sometimes called "vegetable alkali," and existing
inall plants. It was originally obtained from the ashes
left after burning wood and vegetable structures,
although it is not limited to vegetable structures.
Kali-c. is typical of the Kali group of remedies. The
potassium salts have an affinity for solid tissues
and blood corpuscles.

HOMEOPATHIC · Schussler introduced Kali-m. into
homeopathy. His account of it is "it is contained in
nearly all the cells and is chemically related to fibrin.
It will dissolve white or grayish-white secretions of
the mucus membrane and plastic exudations."
When the cells of the epidermis lose molecules
of Kali-m. due to a morbid irritation, the fibrin
comes to the surface as a white or whitish-gray
mass. When dried, this forms a mealy covering. If the irritation affects the tissues under the
epidermis, then fibrin and serum are exuded,
causing the affected spot on the epidermis to
rise in blisters. Similar processes may take place
in and below epithelial cells.
Useful in catarrhal disorders in the sub-acute
innammatory states, fibrinous exudations and
glandular swellings. Whiteness of secretions,
exudations, eruptions of tissues. Tough, fibrinous exudations and discharges. Milky white,
viscid, sticky, thick, slimy or lumpy discharges.

expectoration of thick, white phlegm.

hard swellings. Hard deposits. glandular swelling.

patellar. Crawling and numbness. Crosswise

J. C. Nottingham considered a leading

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-s., introduced by Schussler,
affects respiration, mucus membranes and skin
where it causes desquamation. Schussler explains
that Kali-s., in reciprocal action with iron, effects the
transfer of the inhaled oxygen to all the cells and is
contained in all the cells containing iron.
When a sulphate and any oxide of iron come
into contact with decomposing organic substances they surrender their oxygen and form
sulphate of iron. With more oxygen added, this
may be further decomposed into sulphuric acid
and an oxide of iron.
A deficiency of Kali-s. causes a sensation of
heaviness and weariness. vertigo, chilliness,
palpitations of the heart, anxiety, sadness, toothache, headache and pain in the limbs. Symptoms
are worse in a warm room and towards evening,
better in open, cool air.
Catarrh of larynx, bronchi, nostrils, etc., with
yellow discharges. Catarrh of the stomach where
the tongue has a yellowish mucus coating. Profuse and deep yellow discharges, thin or sticky.

serous discharges, profuse and intermittent.

wandering rheumatism (Puis., Kali-bi.).
Torpid processes. Lack of reaction. Warmblooded. Oxaluria. Facilitates the formation of
new epithelium. Epithelial cancer. Interrupted

HERBAL - Kalmia is the name of a genus of heath
worts native to North America. Kalmia latifolia,
which has large and showy nowers, is found in the
northern parts of the United States.
Its nowers yield a honey said to be deleteri·
ous, and its leaves and shoots certainly are so
to cattle. Dr. Meadows says cattle eat Kalmia in
the latter part of the winter when they are inwant
of something green.
K. angustifolia, probably for the same reason,
has the name of lamb-kill. The powdered leaves
are used as a local remedy insome skin diseases.
The hard wood of K. latifolia is used in the
manufacture of various articles. The Treasury of
Botany noted that the Canadian partridge is said
to become poisonous to humans after feeding
on Kalmia berries.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hering introduced Kalm. into
homeopathic practice, and he, and some friends,
completed the first proving. The head, including
the eyes and face, shows the majority of its
action, followed by the heart. A number of skin
symptoms confirm the popular use of the leaves,
among them a stiffness of the skin, especially
of the eyelids.
A heart, nerve, circulation and rheumatic
remedy. In small doses, it accelerates the heart's
action, in larger doses, it moderates it greatly.
Nausea and slow pulse frequently accompany
conditions.

Karaka
HOMEOPATHIC - The Treasury of Botany noted
that karaka seeds contain a tasteless farinaceous
substance and are eaten in times of scarcity. The
raw seeds are poisonous and produce spasmodic
pains, giddiness and partial paralysis. To render
them edible, they are steamed for twenty-four
hours and then either buried in the ground or
allowed to soak in water for some days.
G.Bennett recorded a few symptoms observed in
the case of a Maori chief poisoned with the seeds.
Spasm with pains. Violent pain lasting a week.
Partial paralysis. Heat anesthesia, when warm
water was applied he did not feel any warmth
from it. Violent spasms and convulsions of whole
body, arms and legs stretched violently and rigidly
out. Permanent rigid distortion.
COMMENTS - C. F. Fischer proved Kara. and used
it clinically in cases of convulsions. He recorded
an account of its effect from the proceedings of the
New Zealand Institute.
"Violent spasms and convulsions of whole
body, arms and legs stretched violently and
rigidly out, great flushings of heat, protrusion of
eyes and tongue, gnashing of jaws. The poison
proves rapidly fatal if the patient is not attended
to immediately and the limbs are permanently
and rigidly distorted if they are not fixed in proper
positions until the crisis is passed.
"The general treatment is to bind the patient
(generally a child) with the limbs in right positions,
dig a pit and place him in it, standing, buried up
to the chin with a gag in his mouth.
"The writer described a youth, age 12, who
had recovered after being poisoned, but whose
limbs had not been properly secured and were
ever after absolutely useless.
"One leg was curved up behind his loins, the
other bent up with the foot outwards. One arm
inclined behind his shoulder, the other slightly
bent and extended forward and all, as to muscles
inflexibly rigid. He could not move himself or even
drive away the flies."

HERBAL - The plant Karwinskia belongs to the

or oblong, rounded at the end, the flowers are

limbs. which becomes generalized and can
terminate in death. They contain a fatty acid,
a yellow substance and a glucoside, which is
the cause of the paralysis of the motor nerves.

HERBAL -.Kava kava is a tall shrub in the pepper

Kavakava

Piper is Latin fOf "pepper". methysticum is Greek
word for "intoxicating". The natives use ~as a stimulant, either chewing the root or drinking a beverage
madeof~befOfeundertakinganyimportantbusiness

or religious rites.
Kava causes exaltation of the mind. lively and
inclined to work. Faculties sharpened, capable
of working more without fatigue or brain-fag.
From increased doses, there is intoxication of a
sorrowful, silent and sleepy character, different
from that produced by alcohol.
Captain James Cook is credited with introducing kava to the West after a voyage through the
South Pacific from 1768 through 1771 .
In former times, the islanders prepared the
ceremonial kava beverage by first scraping
the root. then chewing pieces of it and spitting
them into a bowl to which coconut milk or water
was added.
Next, they stirred the mixture until it took on
a muddy, opaque appearance, then strained it
into another bowl. During ceremonies, a cup of
the beverage was first presented to a special
guest, who was expected to down the contents
without stopping. Then others attending the
ceremony imbibed.
Islanders take moderate amounts of the beverage to achieve a state of tranquility, happiness,
and contentment, but without the unpleasant
side effects of alcohol, such as hangovers or
boisterous behavior. Overindulging can lead to
loss of muscle control and a strong urge to sleep.
The islanders have also used kava as medicine
for centuries, brewing decoctions made from its
rootstock to treat gonorrhea, urinary infections,
menstrual problems, migraine headaches,
insomnia, and other conditions.
It is the kavalactone constituents that offer
many of the actions attributed to Kava. They
leave the mind sharp while your body relaxes.
Besides the popular use of Kava for muscle
relaxing, soothing anxiety and tension, other uses
can relieve headaches, hyperactivity in children,
insomnia and aid in the treatment of depression.
Kava kava has been used for alcohol and drug
abuse. It also helps with the cravings for alcohol
and drugs. Anti-inflammatory and analgesic.
Sedative and relaxant.

kill many potentially harmful microorganisms.

Kombucha starts out as a sugary tea, which is

HERBAL - The flowers of Kousso are a favorite

that purpose has led to the observation of the
few recorded symptoms, among which thirst,

To use as a vermifuge, take a quarter of an
ounce of the dried flowers and boil in four ounces
of distilled water. Infuse for fifteen minutes without
straining. The powder is to be taken with the
infusion in the morning, fasting. Two such drafts
may be g1ven. It is best to g1ve a purgative before
and an hour or two after the draft.

HERBAL - The Kudzu plant is a creeping vine that
is native to Japan, throughout most of China
and the southeastern United States. The word
"kudzu" comes from the Japanese word "kuzu"
which means vine.
Kudzu was introduced to the United States in
1876 at the Centennial Exposition in Philadelphia,
Pennsylvania. Countries were invited to build
exhibits to celebrate the 1OOth birthday of the U.S.
The Japanese government constructed a
beautiful garden filled with plants from their
country.

Kudzu vine
The large leaves and sweet-smelling blooms
of kudzu captured the imagination of America~
gardeners who used the plant for ornamenta
purposes.
Kudzu now is considered a very invasive plant.
But kudzu grows better in the South than it does
in its native lands. Its natural insect enemieS
were not brought to the U.S. with it. That's why
visitors to the South are sometimes awe-struck
by scenic vistas which reveal miles and miles of
seemingly endless vines.
The Kudzu root is used in Traditional Chinese
Medicine and modern herbal products. It has
been used in Chinese medicine since at least
200 BC. As early as 600 AD, it was used to treat
alcoholism.

The modality "alternation ofsides" once led
Clarke to the cure of an eczematous condition
of the eyelids in a child . The child's aunt, who
brought her to him, causally remarked that it
often left one side entirely and went to the other
and then back again. Lac-c. cleared it up in a
very short time.

Laccaninum

E. T. Balch asked for advice in the case of
Maud. age 10, a brunette of healthy parents.
She had fallen forward and hurt her chest while
playing one and a half years earlier.
Nothing was thought of it at the time, but when
brought to Dr. Balch, she was pale, emaciated,
capricious, with no desire for play.
Her sleep was disturbed by frightful dreams.
During the day, piteously begged her mother to
take her, she was so afraid. She felt as though
snakes were on her back. In response to advice,
Balch gave one dose of Lac-c. 50,000c. dry,
and in twenty-four hours the child became more
lively and cheerful and very soon all abnormal
sensations disappeared.

HOMEOPATHIC - lachesis was first introduced to
homeopathy by Dr. Hering. His first experiments
were made when he was studying the botany and
zoology of the Upper Amazon for the German
government. With the exception of his wife, all
those around him were natives, who told him so
much about the dreaded Surukuku that he offered
a good reward for a live specimen.
One was brought in a bamboo box. Those who
brought it immediately fled, along with his native
servants. Hering stunned the snake with a blow
on the head as the box opened, then, holding
its head in a forked stick, he pressed its venom
out of the poison bag upon milk sugar.
Handling the venom and preparing the lower
potencies threw Hering into a fever with tossing
delirium and mania, much to his wife's dismay. He
slept through the night and woke with a dear mind.
He drank a little water to moisten his throat
and asked his wife "What did I do and say?" His
wife remembered and the symptoms were written down as the first installment of the proving.
The natives crept back one by one next day and
were astonished to find Hering and his wife alive.
The snake grows up to seven feet in length.
It has fangs nearly an inch long, with a reddish
brown skin marked along the back with black
brown rhomboidal spots. Nearly alithe provings
of lachesis were made with the 30c and higher
potencies.
like other snake venoms, it decomposes the
blood, rendering it more fluid. It has a marked
hemorrhagic tendency. Hemorrhages are
thin, containing dark particles like charred straw.
Vicarious hemorrhages, nosebleed, bloody
urine etc. Hemophilia. Small wounds bleed a
great deal.

COMMENTS - Characteristic aggravation from
sleep. Nash noted the case of an old, syphilitic
patient who suffered from obstinate constipation
and was taken with severe attacks of colic. The
pains seemed to extend all through the abdomen
and always came on at night.
The man was not making any progress when,
one day, he remarked to Nash, "Doctor, if I could
only keep awake I would never have another attack." And in response to an inquiring look from
the doctor, he added, "I mean that I sleep into
·the attack and waken in it." One dose of Lach.
200c cured the colic and the constipation too.

HOMEOPATHIC - Lachnantes grows in sandy

they feed on Lachnantes, while the black varieties
eat it without inconvenience.

Lachnanthes tinctorla

Arthur Dalzell reported the case of Mrs. B.,
43, who had fibroid tuberculosis of both lungs,
collapse of right lower lobe. Great prostration
and night-sweats. The bowels were alternately
relaxed and confined. Pain and stiffness in the
back, bruised all over, dry cough, roughness of
throat, weak heart-sounds. Bad sleep owing
to a cough.
Lachn. tincture, three drops every four hours,
was given. In three days the prostration was
diminished and the cough was much better,
night-sweats and bruised feeling gone. From this
time an emulsion containing cod-liver oil, liquor
pancreaticus, eggs, cream, hypophosphites and
eucalyptus oil were given in addition. The case
went on to recovery.
Dalzell also recorded the case of Mrs. R., 45,
who was in the last stage of tuberculosis.
Right lung consolidated, left in cavities. This
patient had circumscribed flush on face, brilliant
eyes, throat felt rough, overall bruised feeling.
Remittent fever. Skin dry, except at night, when
she had profuse perspiration. Constant dry
cough. Muco-purulent expectoration.
Lachn. tincture, five drops every three hours,
relieved all the symptoms and procured euthanasia, the patient dying quite easily twelve days later.

LAETRILE
(Amygdalin)
PHARMACY -laetr. Laetrile. Amygdalin. Pangamic
acid. Vitamin 8-17. Anti-cancer drug. Planets:
Moon. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Anemia. Cancer. Cyanosis. Dizziness.
Fatigue. Hair. loss. Headache. Hypotension.
Liver, damage. Muscular, weakness. Nausea.
Ptosis. Rheumatism. Tumors. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - Laetrile formula is laevo·D·
mandelonitrile-8-glucoronide. Laetrile is a
decomposition product resulting from the hydrolysis of amygdalin. This compound is chemically
related to amygdalin, a substance found naturally
in the pits of apricots and various other fruits.
The term "laetrile· was first proposed by Ernest
T. Krebs, Jr. in 1949. Most proponents of laetrile
for the treatment of cancer use the terms "laetrile"
and "amygdalin" interchangeably. Amygdalin
is one of the first and best known cyanogenic
glycosides. Neither amygdalin nor laetrile contain
free cyanide.

L

Laetrile
Amygdalin is a herbal constituent derived
from the kernels of various fruits of the Genus
Prunus (synonym amygdalus) , which includes
the plum, prune, cherry, peach and apricot. It is
among the most ancient herbal remedies used
against cancer.
Apricot kernels have been in medical use

HERBAL- As the common name of Lapsana would

Three ounces of the green plant (or four of

One patient who was cured in this way said
he had no swallowed the draft more than a few
minutes before he felt his stomach as warm as
if he had drunk hot brandy and water.
Only three doses were ordered and the patient
was told, if not cured , to wait a fortnight before
repeating the treatment.

HOMEOPATHIC - Lathyrus is a vetch, a member
of the Leguminosae family that grows in India.
Lathyrus contains variable amounts of a toxin
that, when ingested, may cause lathyrism, a
paralytic affection. Produces a perfect picture
of certain spinal affections.
In Christison's Toxicology, it is stated that Lath.
causes paraplegia, dragging gait, turning-in of the
toes, stiffness and semi-flexion of the knee joints.
The clinical record of Lath. indicates that it may
prove useful in numerous cases of bedridden
paraplegias and infantile spinal paralysis, as
well as in certain fonnns of myelitis.

one of rheumatic paralysis with stiff knees.

COMMENTS - The two varieties of Lathyrus that
have occasioned poisonings are Lath. sativus
and Lath. cicera. The peas are very alike in
appearance. Those of Lath. cicera are rather
smaller than Lath. sativus. more square, and are
a lighter brown. Except for this brownish color
they could easily be mistaken for ordinary peas.
Lath. cicera has red flowers, Lath. sativus, bluish.
Both are cultivated for food and are sometimes
cut green for fodder.
Polio (Gels.). Post-polio neuralgia syn·
drome (Rhus-!, Gels.). Guillain-Barre syn·
drome, ascending paralysis. Multiple sclerosis.
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
Characteristic increased reflexes. Weak
and lame joints. Severe muscle cramps in the
calves. Pain induced by touch. Emaciation of
the paralyzed muscles (Pib., Caust.).
In the British Journal of Homeopathy there is
an account of a wheat famine in India, where the
peas of the plant were substituted for wheat and
used as a food. Those who subsisted on it were
taken, even during sleep, with sudden paralysis
of the lower limbs. Th1s occurred without warning
in young men more than in young women, and
was never recovered from.
Another observer recorded fifty cases of people
who had eaten the lathyrus bread and all stated
that they became paralytic during the wet season
of the country. They went to bed quite well and
woke with stiff legs, unsteady gait and aching,
but no severe pain. The upper limbs were free.
Another saw the disease in Algeria and de·
scribed the symptoms in ten cases. Symptoms
came on suddenly in damp weather with some
pains in the loins, trembling, motor paralysis
and exaggerated reflexes. He attributed these
phenomena to an acute transverse myelitis with
degenerative changes in the cord.

Uthyrus sativus
Never well since an influenza or a viral
infection. Symptoms may be brought on or
be made worse by cold or damp wind. Burning
heat, better uncovering. Burning pain on the
tip of the tongue. Weak bladder with sudden
urgencies to urinate.
O'Connor found that marked benefit followed
its use in old cases of myelitis with marked
spastic symptoms. Bartlett recommended Lath.
for excessive knee jerk and rigidity.
Hart spoke of it as a remedy for locomotor
ataxia, but the absence of sensory symptoms
and the presence of exaggerated reflexes would
seem to contraindicate it in this disease.
He also spoke of Lath. in spinal anemia, giving as symptoms "numbness, followed by pain
in the lower limbs, sensation of a band around
the body, unable to step or distinguish one limb
from another."
In a case related by Bojanus, the general
symptoms were the same. Lath. was the cause
of the trouble, arising during the great Russian
famine. Horses fed with Lath. along with oats
manifested symptoms of paralysis of the limbs
and also of the throat and wind-pipe, setting
up the condition called "roaring." Some died of
suffocation.
Clarke relieved several cases of spastic paralysis, including Miss R., 25, who had been ill
four years with the usual symptoms of spastic
paralysis. Excessive constipation and violent
urging to pass water, if she attempted to retain
it, it passed of itself. The muscles were hard
and unyielding.
She was heavily drugged under allopathic
treatment before coming under his care. Hyper.
was first given with considerable benefit. As the
improvement went no further, Lath. 1c and 30c
were given and then the improvement was much
more marked.
W. A. Dewey recorded a cure with Lath. 3x in a
case of spastic paralysis in a man of twenty-eight.
The attack had been coming on six months. The
patient was a hunchback, having been deformed
since the age of five, but this had given no more
than the usual inconvenience.
On admission to the hospital {December 1,
1898), he was unable to make the slightest
movement of the lower limbs, even of the toes.

Lathyrus sativus
The adductors were in a constant state of
irritable contraction, so that the thighs were
constantly crossed. Reflexes greatly exaggerated. No pain. Spine not tender. General health
was normal. The only other symptom was a
girdle sensation, as if he had a cold, damp doth

Three weeks after commencing Lath., there
was slight lessening of rigidity. On AprilS. 1899,
he could raise his limbs and move his toes. On
July 2nd he walked out of the hospital without
difficulty, the abnormal irritability of the musdes

HOMEOPATHIC- Lat-k. is a venomous spider found

symptoms recorded are the effects of bites.The seat
of a bite becomes immediately painful and swelling
occurs. In some cases, the swelling does not come
on until some days after the bite.
In one case, five days after the bite, a scarlet
papulous rash appeared on both limbs, burning
like fire. The symptoms were somewhat slow
in evolution. In a fatal case, that of a girl bitten
on the abdomen, death did not occur until six
weeks after the bite.
lassitude, faintness, twitchings and trismus.

E. Wigg related the case of MayS.. 7, who

After ten minutes she began to twitch and jerk.
Wigg was sent for and found her inthis convulsed

and heaviness of the tongue. The mind was clear.
Recognizing the action of Laur., Wigg antidoted
it with camphor, and later a cup of coffee, and
symptoms ceased in a few hours. She had no
more of the cough.

COMMENTS - Bay Laurel is the source of the bay

HERBAL-Lavender Oil. The word lavender comes
from the Latinword "lavare" which means to wash.
Historically, lavender has been used not only
for its fragrance but also as a disinfectant, vulnerance (useful for healing wounds), sedative,
stimulant, tonic and ca1minative (a medicine that
expels flatulence). The herbal h1story of lavender
can be traced back to anc1ent Greece.
Dioscorides mentioned French lavender, which
seems to have been used only medicinally by
the Greeks. He attributed to it certain laxative
and invigorating qualities and recommended its
use in a tea-like infusion for chest complaints.
The Romans used lavender to perfume their
public baths. Roman soldiers carried their own
first aid kits of herbs, and whenever the armies
settled herbs would be grown, including lavender.
The Romans were aware of lavender's healing,
soothing and insect repellent properties, and used
its oil in massage. Galen (129-199 AD) added
lavender to the time honored antidotes, theriac
and mithridate, and Nero's physician used it for
anti-poison pills and in uterine disorders.
Abbes Hildegarde (1098-1180) from a monastery in the diocese of Malinz in Saxony, made
some of the earliest mediaeval references to
lavender in her writings. She realized its practical
effect in getting rid of lice and prescribed it for
cleaning eyes. She also thought it could drive
away evil spirits.

Lavender
Lavender oil has been used through the years
as a detoxifier, antidepressant, as an antibiotic,
a natural antiseptic as well as a sedative. Antibacterial. Disinfectant. Anti-inflammatory.
Acne • Lavender oil is considered one of the
best home remedies for treating acne. Lavender
oil has antibacterial properties and can be used
in the treatment of acne. It inhibits the bacteria
that cause acne and helps to rebalance the oversecretion of sebum, which the bacteria thrive on,
and reduce scarring". Simply mix 3-4 drops of
lavender oil with 10 ml of carrier oil and apply
on the affected area daily. Add a few drops of
lavender oil to a plain cream sold by chemists
and use as a moisturizer or cleanser.
Alopecia • In one study of people with alopecia areata, those who massaged their scalps
with lavender and other essential oils daily for
7 months experienced significant hair regrowth
compared to those who massaged their scalps
without the essential oils.
Anti-bacterial • French studies showed that
lavender is a powerful antibacterial in dilutions
of 5 per cent or less it is lethal to bacteria that
cause typhoid, TB &diphtheria.
Anxiety • Keep a spritzer of Lavender mist
hydrosol to spray on your face, or apply lavender
oil to your temples.

is almost immediate, and burn usually heals
without scarring.
Cuts. Apply lavender oil to sooth pain, prevent
bacterial infection and aid scar-free healing.
Dandruff • Steep lavender as you would to

Disinfectant. Lavender is a good household

HERBAL- Lemons are thought to have originated
in India. and were later introduced into Assyria,
where they were discovered by soldiers serving Alexander the Great, who took them back
to Greece
It is believed to have been introduced into
southern Italy around 200 C.E.; and was being
cultivated in Egypt and in Sumer, the southern
portion of Mesopotamia a few centuries later.
The lemon later reached the Mediterranean
after the Romans discovered a direct sea route
from the southern end of the Red Sea to India.
The Arabs were largely responsible for the cultivation of the fruit in the Mediterranean region.
In the 18th Century, The Royal Navy used lemons to fight scurvy (Vitamin Cdeficiency). Lemon
juice and citric acid are traditional remedies for
and preventives of sea-scurvy. It can be used
as a local application (in one part of citric acid
to eight of water).

used in many cuisines worldwide for its navor.

health benefits. A study of the genetic origin of
the lemon reported that it is a hybrid between
sour orange and citron.

used for centuries in order to cure many ailments.

A. E. White wrote that it has a popular repute

in camp life, and also as an application to nongranulating ulcers. For this purpose the root is
to be chewed and then applied.
White was invited to chew a piece, which he
did. In six or eight hours he had three successive calls to stool, very urgent, a little griping in
lower back and some straining at stool. He has
confirmed its use in camp diarrhea, but says
it acts better if Sulph. or Mere-c. is given first.
White reported the case of Mr. X, 56, who
had chronic diarrhea since the war. He had tried
treatment of all kinds, homeopathic included.
He had twelve to sixteen stools a day and had
loss much weight. He was run down and had
made up his mind he had only a short time to live.
He was given Sulph. 30x two doses, one each
night, then Mere-c. 3x, a dose each night for five
nights, then Uatr. 1x, four pellets each nightforfive
weeks, by which time he was completely cured.

HERBAL- Liquorice his one of the most commonly
used herbs in herbal medicine and has a very
long history of use, both as a medicine and also
as a flavoring to disguise the unpleasant flavor
of other medications.
Liquorice was known to the ancients as far back
as the third century B. C. for its efficacy in the
case of dry coughs. The Greeks, recommended
it for the treatment of gastric and peptic ulcers.
Later, Arab physicians used Licorice to relieve
coughs and side effects associated with laxatives.
It is a very sweet, moist, soothing herb that
detoxifies and protects the liver and is also powerfully anti-inflammatory, being used in conditions
as varied as arthritis and mouth ulcers.
The root is alterative, antispasmodic, demulcent, diuretic, emollient, expectorant, laxative,
moderately pectoral and tonic. The root has also
been shown to have a hormonal effect similar to
the ovarian hormones.
Liquorice root is much used in cough medicines
and also in the treatment of catarrhal infections of
the urinary tract. It is taken internally in the treatment of Addison's disease, asthma, bronchitis,
coughs, peptic ulcer, arthritis, allergic complaints.

HERBAL-Matthew Lobe, whose name is given to
this family of plants, was a physician and botanist
attached to the court of James I. There are two
British species, Lobelia dortmanna, found in
shallow lakes, and Lobelia urens, which grows
in healthy places.
Lobelia inflata, the North American variety, is
the most important medically.According to Hale,
this plant was used by the Indians as an emetic
detergent in the same way as Vera!. was used
by the ancients to produce "Helleborism."
Samuel Thompson of New Hampshire, who
founded the modem Botanical School, used
chiefly lobelia, cayenne pepper and the vapor
bath. Often the acetum lobelia acts better than
any other preparation.
In veterinary practice, it is said to have proved
curative in the tetanus of horses, a disease it is
also said to produce.
Lobelia probably obtained the name of"lndian
Tobacco" from the similarity of its action to that
of tobacco in producing intense nausea, vomiting, profound depression at the epigastrium
and collapse.
Treatment should always begin with a single
dose if the symptoms permit, as in some cases
it produces violent depression.
It must be kept in mind when studying lobelia
that the herbalists used it in two forms: the
decoction to produce emesis and through which
they seem to have obtained its antidotal action or
by virtue of which they aborted acute gout, and
the acetum tincture, which they gave in chronic
diseases and in moderate doses."
HOMEOPATHIC-Lobelia is avaso-motor stimulant
increases the activity of all vegetative processes:
It spends its force mainly upon the pneumogastric
nerve, producing a depressed, relaxed condi~ion with oppression of chest and epigastrium,
Impeded respiration, nausea and vomiting.

moments had come. By the bedside stood my

Palmer said there was no pain, he was in no

LOMATIUM DISSECTUM
(Indian Carrot)
PHARMACY -1om-d. Lomatium dissectum. Indian
carrot. Biscuit-root. N. 0 . Apiaceae. Tincture of
fresh plant. Planets: Mercury. Historical dose:
Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL-AIDS. Bacterial, infections. Bronchitis.
Candida. Chronic fatigue. Colds. Coronavirus.
Coughs. Epidemics. Hepatitis. Herpes. HIV.Immune, weakness. Influenza. Lung, disorders.
Pneumonia. Respiratory, diseases. Sinusitis.
Sores. Tuberculosis. Viral, infections. Wounds.

L

Lomatium dissectum
HERBAL-Botanists named it Leptotaenia dissecta
until 1942 when it was renamed Lomatium dissectum, a slightly different classification. One
of the many Lomatium species is often called
"Biscuit-root", as the pulp was pounded into
cakes. Its large taproot and its kinship with common carrots, also gave it the name "Indian Carrot.·
The root of the Lomatium dissectum plant is a
natural medicine with extensive traditional use
by the Native Americans of the Pacific Northwest
and Northern Nevada where it grows.lt was used
primarily for upper respiratory infections, colds,
and influenza although a great many other uses
have been noted.
Anti-microbial especially in the lungs and
upper respiratory tract. Traditionally used to
treat all cases of colds and flus. It can be employed for quick acting relief in all cases of viral
or bacterial infection, particularly where there
is a large amount of thick or sticky mucus and
where infection is deep seated and persistent.
Specific for pneumonia, infective bronchitis
and tuberculosis. Some research has indicated
a greater activity against gram positive bacteria.
It's action of limiting infection makes Lomatium
valuable as a mouth wash and gargle for oral and
throat infections. As a douche for bacterial and
viral infections as well as for candida.
Also used as a skin wash for infected cuts or
wounds, and in many other 'first aid' situations.
The anti-viral and anti-bacterial properties of
Lomatium dissectum have attracted the interest
of herbalists and Naturopathic physicians who
are utilizing it in the treatment of today's most
difficult viral diseases.
It can be part of a protocol in the treatment
of Hepatitis-C. Influenza, HIV, AIDS, Chronicfatigue, Pneumonia, Bronchitis, Herpes simplex,
Sinusitis, and common Colds.
COMMENTS - When the influenza epidemic hit
Northern Nevada in 1918, Ernst Krebs MD
of Carson City was surprised to see the local
Washoe people recovering, and he inquired
as to their medicine. They called it "Toh-sa" or
"Do-sa". Dr. Krebs called it Balsa mea, due to its
biting odor of balsamic resins.
The Native Americans gather this root in the
late fall, November being considered the proper
month for gathering.

1249

Lomatium dissectum
The root is used in the fresh or dry state. It is
cut up and a decoction is made by boiling the
root in water. skimming off the top and giving
large doses of the broth.
Apound of root is considered about the proper
dose to treat a case offever for three days, which
is the longest time needed to break up a fever
due to inOuenza or apulmonary disease. although
the Washoes used it as a panacea.
Whether a coincidence or not, there was
not a single death in the Washoe tribe from
influenza or its complications, although Indians living in other parts of the State where the
root did not grow died in numbers. It was such
a remarkable coincidence that the ·root was
investigated by a practicing physician who saw
apparently hopeless cases recover without any
other medication or care of any kind.
A preparation was prepared and employed in
a great many cases, from the mildest to the most
virulent types ofinfluenza.and it proved, among
other things, that it is the nearest approach we
have today to a specific in epidemic influenza
and the accompanying pneumonia. Where
used early it proved itself to be a reliable agent
in preventing pulmonary complications.
Other physicians were induced to give it a
trial, with the same results. It is beyond the experimental stage, as its therapeutic action in this
direction is established and beyond any doubt.
The cases in which it has been used run into
the hundreds. There is probably no therapeutic
agent so valuable in the treatment of innuenza
pneumonia and, as far as being tried, in ordinary
lobar pneumonia if started early.
REFERENCES - Krebs. Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC-The victim is often not aware of the
spider bite until two to six hours later, unless, and
this is rarely the case, he witnesses the spider in
the act. The first symptoms after the bite include
a stinging sensation with mild to intense pain.
The immediate local effects of envenomation are
a transient erythema, which produces a dusky
or mottled appearance to the skin. Sometimes
a blister quickly follows.
During the first several hours the dusky hue
expands, traveling downward from the site of the
bite, along the forces of gravity. The pathologic
process is fully established within six hours. and
within 24 hours the area where necrosis is taking
place is indeed striking.

L

Loxosceles reclusa
The zone of erythema is replaced by violaceous
discoloration, and subsequently an irregular zone
of necrosis develops ranging in measurement
from a few centimeters to more than 30 em.
Aseptic necrosis proceeds to dry gangrenous
slough and black eschar formation. Open ulcers
form as the necrotic area breaks away from surrounding healthy tissue. Thus the venom diffuses
through subcutaneous tissue until the supply is
exhausted. In some cases it extends through
the fascia, exposing the underlying muscles.
Healing of such ulcerous wounds can require
months, and often a sunken scar endures. If the
quantity of venom is small, no necrosis occurs
and only the local erythema appears.

According to Menuret, skin diseases are
frequently influenced by the moon. He noted
a case of eczematous affection which increased
with each waning moon and was at its maximum
intensity at the new moon when it covered the
whole face and chest and was accompanied

improvement and the face became smooth,
but scarcely had the full moon passed when all
began again.
Moritz Hoffmann observed a young girl

swelling disappearing as the moon waned.

that with weakly persons' excitability is most
pronounced at the new moon and the full moon.

He was put in a private asylum. Although his

can he lie down and go to sleep. ln the morning he
remembers nothing. At full moon the symptoms
are still more extraordinary."

Dr. Herbert H. Roberts, published provings
made by himself, two with the 3x and two with
the 30x tinctures. "The original tincture was
made from the thoroughly ripened fruit, great

seeds as well as the pulp.· The rheumatic and
congestive symptoms were mostly produced by
the 3x, the nervous symptoms mostly by the 30x.
Roberts remarked that the natives of Mexico
and California eat quantities of the ripe fruit to
prevent rheumatism. The right deltoid was very
markedly affected and should make Lycpr. a
companion to Sang. in shoulder pains.
Headaches were intense and characteristic
in some, great soreness remained after the
pain had gone.
The first case concerned a widow, 50, dark
complexion, large, stout, gray eyes. Sudden attack of grip. Very severe aching pains all over, up
and down back, limbs, head. Beating, throbbing
in head, beginning in occiput. spreading all over
head, settling with great violence in temples.
Excruciating pain back of eyes and in balls as if
they would burst with the pressure. Light causes
pain. Delirium. Severe, deep, racking cough.
Thirst for large quantities. Pupils contracted.
Lycpr. 3x every hour cleared away the fever
and acute symptoms by the following morning
and rapidly cured the remaining cough.
The second case was a man, 40, dark complexion, black hair and eyes, tall, thick-set. Severe
bursting, throbbing pain beginning in occiput
and settling with great force in temporal and
frontal regions, eyes painful, worse from light,
pupils contracted. Thirst for large quantities.
Temperature 104" F. Pulse full flowing.
Lycpr. 3x every hour given in evening removed
the headache before midnight. The next day, the
right tonsil was swollen and inflamed, sore on
swallowing, feeling of a lump there. Temperature
101". He recovered rapidly.
