HOMEOPATHIC- The Lycopodiums stand between
the mosses and the ferns. Fossils show that in past
eras they occupied an important place in the world's
vegetation. This remedy is inert until the spores
are crushed. The spores from which the potencies
are made have been called "vegetable sulphur"
(probably on account of their use for producing
stage-lightning at theaters).
In the old school the function of Lye. has
dwindled into its use as an "inert" coating for
pills and an "inert" powder dusting on excoriated
surfaces. Earlier practitioners did not consider it
by any means inert.
Lye. ranks with Sulph. and Calc. in the central
trio around which all the rest of the Materia Medica
can be grouped. Teste puts Lye. at the head of
a group containing Nat-m., Viol. tric. and Ant-c.
Lycopodium is adapted more especially to
gradually developing ailments, functional power
weaken1ng with failures of the d1gestive powers, where the function of the liver is seriously
disturbed. Deep seated, progressive chronic

experience of Clarke's seems to confirm.
Miss S., 25, came to him in October, 1899.
About three years ago she had the first symptoms
of exophthalmos, which was ascribed by her
mother to a prescription of Macrin. in low potency,
taken for pains in the eyes and continued for a
long period.
The first symptoms were sore throat with
ulcerations, then the goiter appeared and the

After a course of Thyr. and later of Thuj. 30c

Attacks of influenza complicated the case and
other remedies had to be given. The patient then
did well under Spig. 30c, as far as the heart is
concerned, though no impression was made on
the goiter, which was small. The heart sounds
were normal.
Characteristic shifting symptoms. Pains shift

HERBAL- Maca is an annual plant which produces a
radish-like root. The plant is cultivated in the Junin
plateau of Peru's Central Highlands, and was highly
revered by the Inca. Maca roots can be gold or
cream, red, purple, blue, black or green.
Native Peruvians traditionally have utilized maca
since pre-lncan times for both nutritional and medicinal purposes. It is an important staple in the diets of
these people, as it has the highest nutritional value
of any food crop grown there.
In Peruvian herbal medicine today, maca is
reported to be used as an immune-stimulant; for
anemia, tuberculosis, menstrual disorders, menopause symptoms, stomach cancer, sterility and to
enhance memory.
To the Andean indigenous peoples, maca is a
valuable commodity. Because so little else grows
in the region, maca is often traded with communities
at lower elevations for such other staples as rice,
com, green vegetables, and beans.
Maca is known for normalizing the male and
female hormones like testosterone, progesterone,
and estrogen. Therefore it has facility to forestall
the hormonal changes of aging.
Maca does not contain hormones itself, only
healthynutrients.ltprovidesthenutrientsthatdirectly
feed the endocrine system and help the glands to
produce vital hormones in dosages predetermined
by one's own body.

COMMENTS - The root of maca is typically dried
and stored, and will easily keep for seven years.
The whole powdered or sliced root in either raw
or roasted form.
In Peru. maca is prepared and consumed invarious ways,although traditionally it is always cooked.
The freshly harvested root can be roasted in a pit,
which is considered a delicacy.
The fresh roots are considered a treat and are
baked or roasted in ashes in the same manner as
sweet potatoes.
The dried roots are stored and, later, boiled in
water or milk to make a porridge. They also are
made into a popular sweet. fragrant, fermented
drink called Maca chicha.
In Peru even maca jam, pudding, and sodas are
popular. The tuberous roots have a tangy, sweet
taste and an aroma similar to that of butterscotch.
It is enzyme-rich, with a pleasant malty taste.
Maca is rich in sugars. protein, starches, and
essential nutrients (especially iodine and iron). The
tuber or root is consumed fresh or dried.

HOMEOPATHIC -The ancient reputation of Mag-s.
as a "refrigerant cathartic" under the familiar name
of "Epsom Salts," or "salts" par excellence, has
overshadowed its homeopathic uses.
Recently old-school authorities have discovered in this "cathartic" a remedy for dysentery.
It is the chief ingredient in many laxative mineral
waters and popular saline aperient mixtures.
Mag-s. has therapeutic value in gallstone
colic. The physiological dosage from 2 to 4
teaspoonfuls in glass hot water taken at onset
of a colicky attack may abort or stop the colic.
Epsom salts is one of the most active saline
cathartics, operating with little pain or nausea,
especially if pure.

M

Magnesia su/phurica

Mag-s. action causes a rush of fluid into the
intestine, which by producing a distention of the
bowel produces evacuation.
It causes little or no irritation in the intestine.
In common with the other salines, it is the classical evacuant to be employed in connection
with mercurials and anthelmintics and in cases
of poisoning.
Mag-s. usually acts within from one to two
hours, more quickly if taken in hot water and in
the morning before breakfast.
The ordinary dose as a mild laxative is a
heaping teaspoonful, as a cathartic, two to four
teaspoonfuls. The taste may be improved, if
necessary, by the addition of a little lemon juice
and sugar. Use on compresses saturated with
solution.
Magnesium sulphate is used to a considerable
extent externally in saturated solution as an
poutice and anti-itching in erysipleas, poison ivy
poisoning, cellulitis and other local inflammations.
Percy Wilde noted that the purgative action of
Mag-s. is not a quality of the drug, but a quality
of its physical state, which renders its absorption
impossible. The properties inherent in the substance itself can only be discovered by potency.

COMMENTS-The effectoflhe magnet as awhole and
of each pole separately was tested by Hahnemann,
and the symptoms are mainly from his pathogenesis.
He said he did not expect "ordinary mechanical,
materialistic and atomistic heads" to be able to
regard diseases as "immaterial alternations of
the vitality or pure dynamic derangements of our
state of health and medicinal powers as merely
virtual, almost spiritual, forces."
Hahnemann asked how they can reconcile
with their materialistic notions the fact that "a
single imponderable spark from a Leyden jar
gives a shock to the strongest man and yet to
ascertainable ponderable substance is communicated to his body?"
Clarke's experience with magnetism is confined to M-ambo. 2,000c, but that is sufficient
to give him confidence in prescribing potencies
of these remedies when their indications arise,
particularly burning lancinalions throughout
the body, pains as if broken in joints, where
cartilages of two bones touch, shootings and
jerkings, disturbed sleep, headache as if a nail
were driven in.

Magnetis poli ambo

Hahnemann said the symptoms ·occurred from
various powerful magnets brought in contact with
various sensitive individuals without distinction
of the poles.
'They were observed in experiments conducted for half a year for the purpose of ascertaining
the proper and most efficacious mode of stroking
the steel with magnets in which a horse-shoe
magnet, capable of lifting a weight of twelve
pounds, was held in the hands, which were held
in contact with both poles for an hour at a time."
Additional symptoms came from Andry, Thouret,
Unzer and De Harsu.
Hahnemann noted that "Although each of the
poles presents something peculiar in its power
of altering the human health, yet each of them
seems, when applied twice of oftener to produce
alternating actions which resemble those of the
opposite pole."
For curative purposes, Hahnemann recommended a much milder application of the
magnet. The popular use of magnetic rings for
rheumatism is analogous to this. The method
of attenuating media saturated with emanations
from the magnet does not seem to have occurred
to Hahnemann.

MAITAKE MUSHROOM
(Grifola Frondosa)
PHARMACY· Grifola frondosa. Maitake. Hen of the
Woods. Dancing Mushroom. King of Mushroom.
Sheep's Head Mushroom. Signorina mushroom.
Planets: Moon, Mars. Historical dose: The whole
mushroom.Added to cooking, teas, tinctures,powders, encapsulations. Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Blood pressure. Blood sugar. Cancer.
Chemotherapy. Constipation. Diabetes. Fatigue.
Fibroids. Hair, loss. Hepatitis. HIV. Hypoglycemia.
Immune, weakness. Indigestion. Influenza.
Obesity. Tumors. Viral, infections. Weight, loss..
HERBAL- Maitake literally means "Dancing Mushroom"ln Japan. Ancient folklore has it that when
the Japanese found Maitake deep in the mountains,
they began dancing for joy.
Historically, Maitake has been used as a tonic
and adaptogen. Maitake is known as the king of
mushrooms for both its taste and health promoting
benefits. It was used as a food to help promote
wellness and vitality. Anti-tumor, anti-diabetic, and
anti-viral properties.
Most or maitake's health benefits seem to come
from one main source. They contain beta-glucan,
a polysaccharide compound thought to help the
immune system by activating effector cells like
macrophages, natural killer cells, and T cells.
In addition to their role in general immunity, these
types of antibodies also act against cancer. Maitake
also has very strong antiviral properties and has
been shown to kill HIV virus in lab experiments. It
has also been used to treat hepatitis and chronic
fatigue syndrome.
The mushroom has also been used to reduce
pain, nausea, hair loss and other negative side
effects of chemotherapy. Maitake mushrooms can
promote weight loss and decrease obesity when
combined with light exercise.
Beta-glucan • The mushroom's beta-glucan
content works to promote important immune
system functions, effectively activating white
blood cells that fight off microorganisms that
cause disease,including cancer. The beta-glucan
polysaccharide is also thought to be the source of
the mushroom's ability to control blood sugar to
help manage diabetes and improve weight loss.

M

Maitake mushroom
Blood, pressure ·Research on animals suggests that maitake may help lower blood pressure
in people. One study gave hypertensive rats a
5% maitake mushroom powder and observed a
reduction in blood pressure. In an unpublished
trial on humans, eleven patients with hypertension took 500 mg of maitake mushroom pills twice
a day. A decrease in diastolic blood pressure of
approximately and a mean decrease in systolic
blood pressure were reported.
Blood, sugar • The consumption of maitake
mushrooms may regulate blood sugar levels and
blood lipid levels. The polysaccharide compounds
that promote the strength of the immune system
are also effective in helping to regulate blood
pressure, glucose. insulin and lipids. This effect
is especially beneficial for people with diabetes
or hypoglycemia.
Cancer • Maitake mushrooms are highly
sought after for their anti cancer properties.
They are abundant in polysaccharides and
polysaccharide-protein complexes that the body
uses to fortify the immune system. Maitake mushrooms enhance the activity of cells, inducing the
production ofinterleukins and other lymphokines
that have chemo protective effects, slow tumor
growth, and help to inhibit the spread of cancer.
Chemotherapy· The mushroom has also been
used to reduce pain, nausea, hair loss and other
negative side effects of chemotherapy.
Cholesterol-In one study on hyperlipidemic
rats, maitake changed lipid metabolism through
inhibiting the aggregation of liver lipids and the
raising of serum lipids. Similar results were seen
in rats fed a high-cholesterol diet. In another study,
rats given powdered mushroom preparations
saw a drop in both total cholesterol and very
low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol.
Diabetes • People with Diabetes may also
benefit from maitake mushrooms. Scientists have
studied a specific, high-molecular polysaccharide
in maitake called the X-fraction. Research results
suggest that maitake mushrooms can reduce
insulin resistance and increase insulin sensitivity.
Digestion ·Aiding digestion by regulating the
stomach and intestines and helping eliminate
food stagnation.

Immunity • One active constituent in Maitake for enhancing the immune activity is a
protein-bound beta-glucan compound. Regular
consumption of maitake enhances the immune

its beta-glucan, a polysaccharide compound
that boosts the immune system through the
activation of macrophage cells, natural killer

MALARIA CO. NOSODE
(Malaria Nosodes)

MALARIA OFFICINALIS
(Decomposed Vegetable Matter)

PHARMACY - malar-co. Malaria co. nosode.
Combination of the nosodes from all four types
of malaria.(Plasmodium falciparum, Plasmodium
malariae, Plasmodium vivax, and Plasmodium
ovate). Planets: Mercury. Historical dose: All
potencies.
CLINICAL- Ague. Bilious, fever. Cachexia. Chills.
Diantlea.Emaciation. Fatigue. Fever. Headaches.
Intermittent fever. Liver, disorders. Malaria. Nausea. Spleen, disorders. Sweats. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC - The first episode of symptoms
usually occurs about 8 to 30 days after the
mosquito bite. Headache, fatigue, and nausea.
Hard, shaking chills with feverfor 12 to 24 hours.
Rapid breathing. Heavy sweating, accompanied
by a drop in temperature.
Episodes may recur every 2 or 3 days until
the disease is treated. Without treatment, the
disease can continue for years. Generally worse
in crowded or unsanitary living conditions. Hot,
humid climates. Malaria is endemic in Latin
America, Asia and Africa.
COMMENTS- Malaria is an infection caused by a
single-cell parasite, which is transmitted by the
bite of an anopheles mosquito. Malaria affects
the blood cells, blood vessels, liver, central
nervous system.
There are four types of malarial parasites,
they are transferred from person to person by a
mosquito bite. The mosquito becomes infected
with malaria after biting a person with the disease. The organism multiply in the mosquito,
then enter the bloodstream of the next person
the mosquito biles.
Once in a person's bloodstream, the parasites
travel to the liver, where they thrive and multiply
rapidly. After several days, thousands re-enter
the bloodstream and destroy red-blood cells.
Some parasites remain in the liver, continue to
multiply and are released again at intervals into
the bloodstream.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

HERBAL - The mandrake does not derive its name
from the shape of the human body which the root
of the plant sometimes takes, but from the name by
which it was known to the Greeks,Mandragora, and
which signifies injurious to cattle. It was used by the
ancient Egyptian physicians for many conditions.
The mandrake figures largely in legend and
poetry. It is said to be the "insane root" spoken
of by Macbeth and it is mentioned by name
in Antony and Cleopatra and in Romeo and
Juliet. Mandrake must not be confounded with
Podophyllum or Bryonia dioica, which are also
sometimes called "Mandrake" in this country.
HOMEOPATHIC - Dufresne experimented with
Mand. on himself and another by repeatedly
smelling, at short intervals, the expressed juice
of the plant, "which has a nauseating odor
like adder's flesh."

There are two varieties of Mand., the vernal
and the autumnal: Dufresne used the vernal.
The symptoms were very similar to those of
Belladonna, to which it is botanically closely
related. Mand. is like a cooled or attenuated Bell.
Restless excitability and bodily weariness.
Great desire for sleep. Striking tiredness, exhaustion, collapse. Depressive condition.

HOMEOPATHIC- Manganese was isolated in 1774
and was introduced into the Materia Medica by
Hahnemann, who made provings of the acetate
and carbonate. The symptoms of the two have not
been kept separate.
Manganese is a metal having a remarkable
affinity for and in some respects a close resemblance to iron,of which it is an extremely frequent
associate. Its medicinal as well as its physical
relationship with iron is very close.
Symptoms of chronic manganese poisoning,
according to Professor von Jaksch, were involuntary laughter,weeping and walking backwards.
Exaggerated reflexes and physical disturbances, evidenced by men making fun of each
other's gait. Paraplegia progressive, wasting,
feeble and staggering gait. Anemia with destruction of red blood corpuscles.
Affinity for the inner ear, larynx, . trachea,
periosteum of shinbone, joints, ankles and lower
limbs. Asthmatic persons who cannot lie on
a feather pillow. Pain extends to ear from other
parts. Everything affects the ear. Yellow-green
lumpy or bloody discharges. Great accumulation of mucus.
Bones are very sensitive. Painful, deep
soreness of the whole body, every part of the
body feels sore when touched, ears,joints, skin.
Weak joints. Growing pains. Diagonal pains.
Wants to lie down in bed which improves all
the troubles. Chronic arthritis with infiltrated,
glistening joints.
Cellulitis, sub-acute stage, promotes suppuration and hastens regeneration. Suppuration
of skin around joints. Necrosis and decay of
bones. Malignant ulcers with blue border, following slight injury. Inflammation of bones or joints
with nightly digging pains.

convalescence.
Syphilitic and chlorotic patients with general

HERBAL- The mango is the national fruit of India,
Pakistan and the Philippines.!! is also the national
tree of Bangladesh. Mango cultivation spread
first to Malaya, eastern Asia and eastern Africa

around 1880.
Mango was introduced to Africa and Brazil
by the Portuguese explorers. Mango cultivation
started in Hawaii and Florida in around 19th
century.The mango originated in southern Asia,
especially Burma and eastern India almost 4,000
years back.
Many stories in Indian mythologies have the
mention of mango plant; Buddha was known to
meditate in a mango grove. According to Indian
concept, mango symbolizes life and is used in
every pious ritual. Mango leaves are used for
festival and wedding decorations.
The 'chutney' made by Indian mangoes is
the original chutney that has become popular
universally. Today India is the world's major
producer of mangoes; Thailand, China, Brazil
and Mexico are the other producing countries.
In China, mangoesare sweet and sour and offer
a cooling energy. The tonic made from mangoes

is used to treat bleeding gums, anemia, cough,
constipation, nausea, fever, sea sickness and
cures weak digestion.

HERBAL - Matcha is a fine ground, powdered, high
quality green tea and "not the same as" tea powder

Preparation and consumption of powdered tea
was formed into a ritual by Zen (Chan) Buddhists.
The earliest Chan monastic code in existence,
entitled Chanyuan qinggui (Rules of Purity for the
Chan Monastery, 1103), describes in detail the
etiquette for tea ceremonies.
Zen Buddhism and the Chinese methods of
preparing powdered tea were brought to Japan in
1191 by the monk Eisai. Powdered tea is no longer
popular in China, but in Japan it continued to be an
important item at Zen monasteries. and became
highly appreciated by others in the upper echelons
of society during the 14th through 16th centuries.
The Japanese tea ceremony centers on the
preparation,serving, and drinking of matcha.Blends
of matcha are given poetic names called chamei
("tea names") either by the producing plantation,
shop or creator of the blend, or by the grand master
of a particular tea tradition.

powerful green tea catechins.lt boosts the metabolism and bums calories. Detoxifies effectively and

COMMENTS -Tea leaves. Powder. Tea bags. The
highest grades of matcha have more intense
sweetness and deeper flavor than the standard or
coarser grades of tea harvested later in the year.
Matcha is made from shade-grown tea leaves also
used to make gyokuro. The preparation of matcha
starts several weeks before harvest up to 20 days,
when the tea bushes are covered to prevent direct
sunlight. This slows down growth, turns the leaves
a darker shade of green and causes the production
of amino acids. The shade increases the amount
of chlorophyll content in the leaves, which is what
makes them bright green and full of nutrients. Only
the finest tea buds are hand picked.
After the leaves are laid out flat to dry, they will
crumble somewhat and become known as tencha.
Tencha can then be de-veined, de-stemmed, and
stone ground to the fine,bright green powder known
as matcha. It can take up to one hour to grind only
30 grams of matcha. Only ground tencha qualifies
asmatcha.
Matcha is also used as flavoring in many
chocolates, candy, and desserts, such as cakes
and pastries, cookies,pudding, mousse, and green
tea ice cream.
The use of matcha has also spread to North
American cafes, which introduced "Green Tea
Lattes" ·and other matcha flavored drinks. As in
Japan, it has become integrated into lattes, iced
drinks, milkshakes, and smoothies.

The only negative side effect reported from

less caffeine than coffee: there are approximately
thirty to sixty mg. of caffeine in six - eight ounces
of tea, compared to over one-hundred mg. in eight

19, tall, blonde, for several years had severe,
nervous and congestive headaches. The attacks
recurred two to four times a month and were so
severe that they compelled her to keep to her
bed twenty-four hours.
The pain, mostly in temples and forehead,
was a congested, full sensation with flushed
face, drowsy, stupid feeling and sometimes
much nausea.
Trivial things seemed to provoke the attacks.
Spectacles had been supplied by oculists and
teeth freshly stopped by dentists, diet, rest
from study and outdoor exercise had all failed
to relieve.
Meli. 4x was given and she had only two attacks
in six months and those very slight.
A writer in Hom. News tells of a Frenchman
who came to him complaining of an incessant
headache so bad that he thought he would die.
A dose of Meli. was given on the spot and the
doctor, thinking Nux-v. indicated, went into the
next room to get it.
He returned in five minutes and found the
patient on his hands and knees shaking his head.
The doctor, thinking him crazy, asked what he
was doing. He replied that the pain was entirely
gone and he was only trying various attitudes
and motions to make sure.

HOMEOPATHIC -There was a fitness innaming this
metal after the mutable planet Mercury. It provides
us with weatherglasses and thermometers and
likewise it turns those who are under its influence
into weatherglasses and thermometers.
Hahnemann invented Mercurius solublis in his
pre-homeopathic days in response to a general
desire for a mercurial preparation which should
be at once soluble and non-corrosive and it at
once took its place in the pharmacy, a place it
has never lost.
The method of developing the medicinal power
of metallic mercury by graduated trituration was
a later discovery, through there was a suggestion
of it in the well-known Hydrargyrum cum creta.
Although Hahnemann proved Mercurius
solublis, he recommended the use of triturations of the pure metal in practice as being the
simplest mercurial preparation and more easily
obtained and equally available with Mere. The
potencies are prepared from soluble black oxide
of mercury, originally prepared by Hahnemann
from pure metallic mercury.
There is no difference between the symptoms
of these preparations, but it seems that when
Mere. solublis fails, when indicated, Mere. vivus
acts. Hahnemann recommended Mere. vivusas
a superior preparation for homeopathic prescribing in his preface to the proving. No pains have
been taken to keep distinct Mere. solublis and
Mere. vivus.
Mere. is Hahnemann's typical anti-syphilitic
remedy, as Sulph. is the typical anti-psoric and
Thuj. the typical anti-sycotic. Every organ and
tissue of the body is more or less affected by
this powerful drug.
It transforms healthy cells into decrepit,
inflamed and necrotic wrecks, decomposes the
blood, producing a profound anemia.

COMMENTS - To the symptoms of Hahnemann's
pathogenesis of Mere. solublisare added observed
effects of mercury in those engaged in working with
the metal, patients taking mercury, and the effects
on those applying mercurial inunctions to patients.
Many people have been severely affected by
absorbing it through their hands. An electrician,
who at one time was required to work with his
hands frequently in a trough filled with quicksilver.
thereafter could not bear the slightest shock of
electricity, though before he could stand very
strong ones.
There is no difference between these effects
and the symptoms of the proving so far as the
general characteristics are concerned, but in the
finer characteristics there must be differences.
The symptoms of the proving are in general
more particularly characterized than the effects
of Mere. vivus.
The symptoms of nosebleed and the more
finely characterized throat symptoms were
produced by Mere. solublis, as were the majority
of the symptoms in the male and female sexual
organs. Stitches on tonsils, stitches into ear
on swallowing, something hot rises into throat.

HOMEOPATHIC-There have been reports of allergies and/or sensitivities to MSG, sometimes
attributed to the free glutamic acid component.
It has been blamed for causing a wide variety
of physical symptoms including migraines,
nausea, stomach cramps, bloating, irritable
bowel syndrome. Extreme dryness of the
mouth, mouth lesions. Hives or rashes.
Alleric reactions and anaphylactic shock.
Numbness to the tongue and face, burning
sensation in the neck, facial pressure or tightness.
Drowsiness, msomnia, anxiety, panic attacks,
mental confusion.Asthma, runny nose, sneezing. Flushing, and heart palpitations.
MSG can affect human children's cognitive
skills and cause learning difficulties. MSG
has been shown to cause lesions on the brain,
especially in children. These lesions cause cognitive, hormonal and emotional abnormalities.
In children, excess glutamate affects the growth
cones on neurons. Growth cones are vital in
laying down chemical pathways in the brain to
enable the brain to operate effectively.
COMMENTS - MSG is made by either a bacterial
fermenting process, protein hydrolysis (a breaking of protein into its constituent amino acids),
or by synthesis.
When aproduct is 99%pure MSG, the product
is called "monosodium glutamate"by the FDA
and must be labeled as such.
However, when a hydrolyzed protein contains
less than 99% MSG, the FDA does not require
that the MSG be identified.
Many food products manufacturers advertise
"No MSG" on their food packages, but MSG
may be disguised as "hydrolyzed vegetable
protein," "glutamic acid." "enzyme modified,"
"natural flavor," "yeast extract," "maltodextrin,"
or "autolyzed yeast."
REFERENCES- Murphy.

Mucuna is an Ayurvedic remedy in nervous and

Mucuna pruriens, also known as Cow-itch. The
plant isinfamous for itsextreme itchiness produced

the seed pods. It has value in agricultural and horticultural use and has a range of medicinal properties.
Mucuna or velvet bean contains a very powerful
neurotransmitter pre-cursor L-Dopa. Studies show
L-Dopa also helps in the reduction of cholesterol
and blood sugar levels.
The mucuna seed has been used internally for
Parkinson's disease, edema, impotence, intestinal
gas, and worms. Externally it is applied to ulcers.

Cartier noted two cases in which he used
Myris. The first was a young girl who had had
her leg in a splint for inflammation of the knee
and doughy swelling of the entire limb for three
months. Cartier came to the conclusion that there
was pus in the joint.
Myris. 3c, five drops three times a day, was
given for three months. Five months later, the
swelling and inflammation were all gone, walking gave no pain, but the joint was anchylosed.
The second case was an old man, 87, who
was seized with sudden arthritis of the shoulder
with intense fever. Cartier was sent for and found
the shoulder quite full of pus with a particularly
painful spot on the scapula, at a point where the
bone was said by one authority to be attacked.
Myris. 3c, five drops three times a day, was
given. In ten days there was no longer suppuration, the size of the joint has become normal and
the tender spot was gone.

HERBAL-Myrrh is highly prized for its bitter,cleansing
perfume.The aromatic pale yellow,gum resin seeps
out from fissures in the bark.
Myrrh is a thorny shrub, myrrh thrives in the arid
regions surrounding the Red Sea. Red gum oozes
from cracks and fissures in the bark, which is collected and distilled to give a rich, amber colored
essential oil.
Myrrh comes from anArabic word "murr" meaning
"bitter". Myrrh was a vital ingredient of an Ancient
Greek aromatherapy perfume called 'megaleion'.
Myrrh has a long history of therapeutic and
medicinal use inAyurvedic medicine.lt is currently
used internally to treat mouth ulcers, gingivitis,
pharyngitis, respiratory conditions, stomatitis, several female complaints, and topically for
ulcers and gum conditions.
Myrrh was still being used in some hospitals
to treat bed sores. As a gargle it can help with
laryngitis and respiratory complaints; it is
both expectorant and a stimulant of circulation
and finds many uses in the treatment of the
common cold.

1404

Externally it is healing and antiseptic ~01
wounds and abrasions and can be applied
diluted with a carrier oil or used as a tincture.
The tincture is used for sore throats, ulcers
and thrush.
Myrrh is a useful agent for treating thrush.
(Candida albicans) and athlete's foot fungal infec·
lions. Mouthwash for infected gums or ulcerated
tongue. The dry, powdered resin is often added
to tooth paste formulas.
Myrrh is an excellent antiseptic, a slow and mild
stimulant, possessed of moderate astringency,
and acting as a stimulating tonic.
Myrrh diminishes mucus discharges. leaves
a sense of warmth in the respiratory passages.
arrests decomposition, and removes foul odors
from sores.
Herbalists indicates use of this aromatic herb
as a gargle to treat pharyngitis and tonsillitis. Its
use is also suggested externally for sinusitisand
skin inflammations.
Dr. Christopher also included instruction

He then tried the chekan on members of his own

COMMENTS - Naja. was introduced into homeopathy by Russell and Stokes. who made the
first provings along with some forty other provers
including Gillow, Pope and Drysdale. Provings
were made with low potencies.
Majumdar had no success with Naja. until he
obtained fresh venom from snake charmers and
made potencies. Previously the Naja. used by
Indian homeopaths had been re-imported into
India from England in the form of potencies.
Deane. in his experience in the plague epidemic
of1899-1900, found Naja. preparedfromthefresh
venom more efficacious than Lach.
Naja. has an affinity for the medulla oblongata
and cerebellum. Heart failure and distress. Weak
valves with regurgitations, stenosis, prolapse.

after infectious diseases.

NARCISSUS POETICUS
(Daffodil)
PHARMACY- narc-po. Narcissus poeticus. Daffodil.
N. 0 . Amaryllidaceae. Tincture of unexpended
blossom-buds, stem, leaf and flower. The young
buds, stems and leaves are macerated in two times
their weight ofalcohol. Planets: Mercury.Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea.
Whooping cough.
HERBAL - The name of the plant, Narcissus, is not
from that of the fabled youth who fell in love with
his own image reflected in the water, but is from
the Greek Narkao, "to be numb," on account
of the narcotic properties of the drug. The classic
Asphodel and the Narcissus are the same, from
which it may be seen that the plant dates back as
far as man's records go.
Dr. Charge's work, Maladies de Ia Respiration, quoted the great Laennec as an authority
in regards Narcissus.
Fernie, in his excellent Herbal simples, also
said "An extract of the bulbs applied to open
wounds has produced staggering numbness of
the whole nervous system and paralysis of the
heart. Socrates called this plant the 'Chaplet of
the Infernal Gods,' because of its narcotic effects."
He also noted that a decoction of the dried
flowers is emetic and when sweetened will, as
an emetic, serve most usefully for relieving the
congestive bronchial catarrh of children.
On the other hand, the alkaloid from the bulbs
after flowering produces copious salivation,
increases cutaneous secretion, contracts the
pupil of the eye, produces slight relaxation of the
pulse and slight faintness and nausea.
Daffodil bulbs contain an alkaloid the action
of which, according to authorities, varies as
to whether the alkaloid is extracted from the
flowering bulb or from the bulb after flowering.
The National Dispensatory noted that"The emetic
action of Narcissus has been used to break up
intermittent fever and relieve bronchial catarrh with
congestion or obstruction of the air tubes. Like Ipecacuanha, it has also been prescribed in dysentery,
especially of the epidemic form. Its influence upon
the nervous system is attested by the vogue it has
enjoyed in hysteria, chorea, whooping cough and
even epileps ."

HOMEOPATHIC . This acid (and more particularly its

Faculty of Medicine of Paris,as a "cure" for tuberculosis. The nature of this salt enables the patients to
take it in small doses. but it is not always harmless.
Cacodyl, which signifies evil-smelling. is like
Cyanogen. a compound radical. It was first
obtained by Bunsenis 1873 as di-cacodyl. It is
a clear liquid that refracts light strongly, heavier
than water, of insupportably offensive smell, its
vapor being highly poisonous.
Cacodylic acid is a crystalline arsenic compound, soluble in water, odorless and. though
containing 54.4 percent of metallic arsenic, not
an active poison.

Tuberculosis. Foul breath and mouth with bad
odor. Dry dermatitis of the skin of abdomen.

It corresponds to Hahnemann's sycosis

Grauvogl described the hydrogenoid constitution as the state in which there is extreme
sensitiveness to damp wetting, bathing,
watery foods and residence near fresh water,
especially standing water. Periodicity is also
another feature of this state. He considered this
constitution as providing the soil for gonorrheal
infection.
Schussler wrote, "The action of the Sodium
sulphate is contrary to that of the Sodium chloride.
Both indeed, have the faculty of attracting water,
but the end is a contrary one, Nat-m. attracts the
water destined to be put to use in the organism,
but Nat-sulph. attracts the water formed during
the retrogressive metamorphosis of the cells
and secures its elimination from the organism."

HOMEOPATHIC - Nectrianinum is a clear liquid of a

and Chausse. Two month old nectria cultures on

reduced to one-third of their original volume.
They were filtered through paper, and again
through porcelain. The liquid was then taken to

Observers said that Nectrin. caused · An arrest
or diminution of hemorrhages. Suppression of
fetid discharges. A tendency at times to epidermization of the neoplasm with a corresponding
well-defined arrest in its evolution."
The patients were worse when treatment was
discontinued and better when it was resumed. ln
very advanced cancer, reaction may not occur.

HERBAL - Neurolaena lobata is a member of
the Asteraceae family and a common Central
American plant. It has yellow flowers and
bitter-tasting leaves which contain a potent antiparasitic agent (sesquiterpene dialdehyde), that
is active against amoebas, candida, giardia and
intestinal parasites.
Atea made from the root is used to cleanse the
blood, and a leaf tea is used to treat intestinal
parasites, malaria, fungus and ringworm .
It is also topically to bate wounds to prevent
infection, and to use as a hair wash for ridding
the hair of head lice. Boiled and strained leaves
have been used as an insecticide for house and
garden plants.
There is some preliminary research that
indicates N. lobata helps regulate blood sugar
levels, which can ultimately help diabetics manage their condition. A subsequent animal study
showed that a tincture of this plant lowered blood
glucose levels in animals.

(Tobacco)
PHARMACY - nicot-r. Nicotiana rustica. Tobacco.

HERBAL-Tobacco refers to a genus of broad-leafed
plants of the nightshade family indigenous to
North and South America, or to the dried and
cured leaves of such plants. Tobacco leaves
are often smoked in the form of a cigar or cigarette, or in a smoking pipe, or in a water pipe
or a hookah. This could damage the lungs and
could also potentially cause lung disorders such
as asthma. Tobacco is also chewed, "dipped"
(placed between the cheek and gum), and sniffed
into the nose as finely powdered snuff.
Nicotiana rustica is a very potent variety of
tobacco. The high concentration of nicotine in
its leaves makes it useful for creating organic
pesticides. It is also used for religious purposes
by South American shamans.

N

Nicotiana rustica
Growing in the rainforest it contains up to
twenty times more nicotine than common North
American varieties such as Nicotiana tabacum.
HOMEOPATHIC - Richard Pitt conducted a recent
proving of Nicotiana rustica which was written
up in his book called Tobacco. Tobacco contains the nicotine, a powerful neurotoxin that
is particularly harmful to insects. All means of
consuming tobacco result in the absorption
of nicotine in varying amounts into the user's
bloodstream, and over time the development of
tolerance and dependence.
Nicotine is the key alkaloid found in tobacco.
Extremely addictive andpoisonous,one or two
drops of pure nicotine can be lethal. In some
varieties of Nicotiana rustica, the nicotine content
of the leaves can be as high as 20 percent.
Toxic effects of tobacco include perspiration,
light-headedness. general weakness, tremors,
convulsions and respiratory paralysis.
Interestingly, one of the keynote symptoms of
Tabacum is a sinking feeling, usually associated
with nausea. This was confirmed in the Nicotiana
rustica proving. but the feeling of sinking was
also seen in its psychological sensations,
making it a theme of the remedy. The sinking
was explained in different ways, from a falling
from a high place into the earth, a falling through
space. a general sinking feeling in the body. The
sinking feeling was confirmed in the stomach and
abdomen region.
The vertigo symptoms were confirmed and
also elaborated on with Nicotiana rustica. This
falling, sinking feeling was consistent throughout
the remedy picture, and more modalities were
confirmed than are currently found with Tabacum.
Physically, there were strong vertigo symptoms,
one prover experienced debilitating vertigo for
over 4 weeks.
There were characteristic headache symptoms, often described as being neuralgic in
nature, and also eye and face symptoms which
were neuralgic in nature. In the ear and nose
symptoms, there was a particular feeling of
"openness", which could parallel some of the
mental experiences, a sense of opening to other
dimensions, or like the earth opening up, creating
an abyss or chasm.

C~MMENTS- Tobacco smoking carries significant
nsks including the potential to develop various
cancers as well as strokes, and severe cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.
Significantly shorter life expectancies have
been associated with tobacco smoking. The
substantially increased risk of developing cancer
as a result of tobacco usage seems to be due
to the plethora of nitrosamines and other carcinogenic compounds found in tobacco and its
residue as a result of anaerobic heating, either
due to smoking or to flue-curing or fire-curing.
The above facts of the use of tobacco are
testament to the toxicity of tobacco and its
impact on societies throughout the world. It is
the most widely used drug known to man, having
spread originally from the Americas to the rest
of the world. Nicotiana plants were frequently
seen in cemeteries, reinforcing the connection
between tobacco and the other world.

In the store of Mr. Harold Woolley, in Manchester, a two-gallon bottle of nitric acid fractured.
Water was thrown upon the bottle and whiting
placed about it to neutralize the fumes which
issued from the fracture.
Mr. Woolley supervised the process and was
in contact with the fumes for two hours. This
happened in the afternoon. The next day, Mr.
Woolley complained of being unwell and although
medical aid was promptly summoned, he died at
5 o'clock in the afternoon. Death was attributed
to rapid congestion and inHammation of the lungs
in consequence of inhaling the fumes.
Burnett made a cure of actinomycosis with Nitac. 3x in a patient who had seen many London
consultants and had doubtless taken much Kali-i.
The localities in which the disease manifested
itself, the region of the mouth and anus, gave
Burnett his indication.
H. N. Coons recorded the case of an anemic
woman who, four weeks after miscarriage, had
constant pelvic hemorrhages, at times coming
with a gush, a constant heavy feeling, much
worse standing or walking. Nit-ac. 2x, 20 drops
in three ounces of water, a teaspoonful every
two hours, quickly arrested bleeding and cured.
W. M. James cured a case in which a girl
had frequent attacks of petit mal, sometimes as
many as fifty a day, between the periods. At the
beginning of menses she had spasms so violent
that they dislocated both humeri.
Giving Nit-ac. 200c persistently gradually put
an end to the attacks. The first few times after
beginning treatment, there were spasms but no
dislocation.
D. C. Perkins related the case of a woman who
said she was very ill, but could only describe her
illness by saying that she "felt like a pulp-mill."
Nit-ac. has "borborygmus as if a boiler was working in the bowels," and proved to be the remedy.
Mohr gave Nit-ac. 3x to a man who suffered
from liver cancer with bloody diarrhea, followed
by constipation, and violent pains in the stomach
and liver. He was unable to sleep or to take
any food without much pain, vomiting. Nit-ac.
removed the pain and relieved the constipation
entirely, and the patient died without an hour's
suffering from the time he received treatment.

COMMENTS - Stonham reported a case in which
a dark-haired young man ate two nutmegs one
moming.ln the afternoon, he was exhilarated,able
to do more than usual, to argue on any subject. AI
dinner, his mouth was dry, he had great thirst, felt
he could not drink enough to quench it
After dinner, his head felt strange, as Win a
dream, but he jointed a small musical party as he
had intended. He seemed to be two people. His
real, conscious self seemed to be watching his
other self playing. He could not play well and
had to stop.
He seemed lost and when spoken to would
come to himself with a start. He could hear distant
sounds much more acutely than usual.
A woman who ate several nutmegs in an attempt to bring on a miscarriage hallucinated that
she had two heads.
A. P. Williamson recorded one case of awoman
who took grated nutmeg for diarrhea. After the
second dose of half a nutmeg, her head felt queer
and dizzy, then her head felt large.
She could not reply to questions, although her
eyes were open and she seemed to understand.
Her pupils dilated, eyes starting, face pale,
respiration was labored.She was semi-conscious
and had to be shouted at, but relapsed into
semi-consciousness. Pulse was at first small or
rapid, but during the unconscious period it was
irregular, fuller and weak.
When consciousness first returned, she kept
her hands to her head "to prevent it falling off,
was obliged to move her head with her hands,
it being too large and heavy for her body.· Her
chest felt as if in a vice.
For some days she was unable to use words
properly, frequently obliged to stop in the middle of
a sentence and change it entirely from not being
able to use the appropriate words.

Nux vomica
HOMEOPATHIC - Strychnos nux vomica is a
moderate-sized tree, native to the Coromandel
Coast and Cochin China. The fruij is like an orange
in appearance and contains numerous seeds of
nattened circular outline, about the size of a half
penny,ashi)ray in color,covered with fine silky hairs.
The seeds are intensely bitter owing to the
presence of strychnia and brucea that exist
together with certain peculiar acids, but the
pulp is innocuous and is said to be eaten by
birds. If nitric acid is added to the seeds a deep
orange-yellow color is produced. The wood of
the tree is very bitter.
Nux-v. is used in India in cases of intermittent
fever and snakebites. The Treasury of Botany
noted that a decoction of the leaves is used
externally in rheumatism.
The difference in the character of lgn. and
Nux-v.proves the wisdom ofHahnemann's simple
methods of studying medicines. If there was
nothing more than the chemistry of the drugs to
go by lgn. and Nux-v might be used indifferently,
but with the knowledge of their characteristic
features, they are seldom even thought of in
connection with the same case.
Nux-v. is useful to those who lead a sedentary life doing much mental work, or to
those who remain under stress and strain of
prolonged office work, business cares and
worries. Generally thin, spare, quick, active,
nervous and irritable.
Firrn-tissued brunettes. Debauchees, much
drugged patients. Useful for the ill effects of
wine, women, rich food, tobacco and stimulative drugs.
Indulgences result in dyspepsia and irritable
temper. Irritable nervous system, hypersensitive and over-impressionable. Digestive disturbances, portal congestion and hypochondriacal
states. Dyspepsia. Zealous fiery temperament.

HERBAL - Nyctanthes is a small tree of the Jasmine
family, having brilliant, highly fragrant flowers, white
and yellow, which do not expand until evening and
which fall off about sunrise. During the day the tree
lose all its brightness and hence is called "The Sad
Tree." "Nyctanthes" means "Night-flowering."
S.C. Ghose gave an account of the medicinal
properties of this plant. He used it extensively in
cases of bilious and remittent fevers, rheumatism
and sciatica and the constipation of children.
Nyctanthes is "a bitter tonic and expectorant
and a mild purgative." In the fever there is thirst
before and during chills, and bitter vomiting at
close of chill. Not much sweat.

OnionS
The name also describes the onion bulb when
cut down the middle: it is a union of many separate. concentrically arranged layers.
Eaten and cultivated since prehistoric times,
onions were mentioned in first dynasty of ancient
Egypt, circa 3200 BCE, and have appeared in
tomb paintings, inscriptions and documents
from that time on. Some paintings depict onions
heaped onto banquet tables. both the robust bulb
onions as well as scallions.
Of all foods in the plant kingdom, onions set
the record for the most frequent appearance in
ancient Egyptian art. It certainly is no wonder
since they were the staple food of the poor
along with bread and beer. Egyptian priests were
prohibited from eating them.
In ancient Greece, athletes ate large quantities
of onion because it was believed to lighten the
balance of the blood. Roman gladiators were
rubbed down with onions to firm up their muscles.
In the Middle Ages, onions were such an
important food that people would pay their rent
with onions. and even give them as gifts. Onions
were considered so potent that in ancient times
celibate In France, newly weds were fed onion
soup in morning after their wedding night to
restore their libido.
For centuries.onions have been used to reduce
inflammation and heal infections. Doctors were
known to prescribe onions to facilitate bowel

ORCHITINUM
(Testes Extract)
PHARMACY - orch. Orchitinum. Testicular extract.
Sperminum.Asarcode.Trituration.Planets: Moon.
Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Debility. Hot flashes. Impotency. Menopause. Senility. Sexual, weakness.
HOMEOPATHIC - The use of a testicular extract in
cases of senile decay and nervous breakdown was
first proposed by Brown-Sequard, and formed one
of the examples by wh1ch he illustrated his doctrine
of "1nner secretions."
He maintained that the various glands of the
organism had, in addition to their obvious secretion or excretion, an additional secretion which
was not obvious,butwhich materially contributed
to the welfare of the organism.
The doctrine is now generally accepted and the
use of the sarcodes in general is based upon it.
Orch.has been used with success in the triturations in menopausal sufferings and in old-school
practice in the sequelae of ovariotomy in cases
of debility, sexual weakness, premature senility.
COMMENTS - Generally a remedy for men. Impotency (Sel.) and sexual debility. Weakness
in the testes, particularly before puberty. Hot
flashes. Senility.

HERBAL - Oregano grows wild in the mountains
of the Mediterranean region. The name is
derived from a Greek word meaning "joy of the
mountains."
It was used by Greek physicians for trauma,
wounds, headaches, lung disorders and venomous bites and was the traditional cure for
hemlock poisoning.
Over the centuries it gained widespread use for
lung conditions, asthma. pneumonia, bronchitis,
sinusitis, allergies, and cough.
Britain's Gerard, in his 17th century manuscript,
explained the use of oregano as a top remedy for
head colds. The 19th Century eclectic physicians
used oregano as a general tonic and a promoter
of menstruation (which is why it should not be
used during pregnancy).

antibiotics known.
Oregano oil is known to be a potent anti-viral,

OXYTOCIN
(Pituitary Gland Hormone)
PHARMACY - Oxytocin. Pituitary gland hormone.
Planets: Moon. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Anxiety. Autism. Breastfeeding.Depression. Hormonal, problems. Intestinal problems..
Irritable bowel. Prostate, enlargement.
HOMEOPATHIC -Oxytocin is a hormone secreted by
the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland. Oxytocin is
a hormone and a neurotransmitter that is involved
in childbirth and breast-feeding.
Oxytocin plays a role in the female reproductive
functions, from sexual activity to childbirth and
breast feeding. Stimulation of the nipples triggers
its release.
During labor, oxytocin increases uterine motility,
causing contractions in the muscles of the uterus,
or womb.As the cervix and vagina start to widen for
labor,oxytocin is released.This widening increases
as further contractions occur.
At present, the implications of having too much
oxytocin are not clear. High levels have been linked
to benign prostatic hyperplasia, a condition which
affects the prostate in more than half of men overthe
age of 50.This may cause difficulty in passing urine.
Similarly, it is not fully understood at present ~
there are any implications of having too little oxytocin
in the body. A lack of oxytocin in a nursing mother
would prevent the milk-ejection reflex and prevent
breastfeeding.
Low oxytocin levels have been linked to autism
and autistic spectrum disorders (e.g. Asperger
syndrome). Akey element of these disorders being
poor social functioning. Some scientists believe
oxytocin could be used to treat these disorders.
In addition, low oxytocin has been linked to
depressive symptoms and it has been proposed
as a treatment for depressive disorders. However,
there is not enough evidence at present to support
its use for any of these conditions.
RELATIONS- Sepia. Pulsatilla.
REFERENCES-Murph1

W. D. Gentry in June, 1895, sent Boericke
& Tafel specimens of Oxyt. and as this firm is
extremely careful about the botany of the plants
they make their tinctures from, Gentry made
these remarks concerning the plants he sent:
"My attention was first called to this plant last
winter during January. Soon after my arrival on
the territory, as it was almost the only green thing
showing itself above the snow. Which covered
the ground at that time for two or three days.
"Some cattle had been eating the weed and
as I approached them they tried to move away,
but in spite of their efforts they backed towards
me and in their efforts to escape made some
ludicrous maneuvers. I observed them closely
for more than an hour and was reminded most
forcibly by their actions of the symptoms of
locomotor ataxia."

Gentry's observation of loco-disease in winter
bears out what is said by other writers, namely,
that it is only in winter, when food is scanty, that
animals can be induced to commence eating the
weed and then they cannot leave off.

PARAQUAT
(Nitrogen Herbicide)

PHARMACY- paraq. Paraquat. Nitrogen herbicide
(1 ,1'-dimethyl-4,4'-bipyridinium). Planets: Moon.
Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL-Abdominal pain. Coma. Convulsions.
Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Eye, problems. Incoordination. Kidney, failure. Liver, problems. Lung,
problems. Lung, scarring. Nail, problems.
Nausea. Pulmonary, edema. Respiratory,
failure. Skin, problems. Tachycardia. Vomiting.
HOMEOPATHIC -Paraquat is aquaternary nitrogen
herbicide widely used for broad leaf weed control.
It is a quick-acting, nonselective compound ,
that destroys green plant tissue on contact and
by translocation within the plant. It is also used
as a crop desiccant and defoliant, and as an
aquatic herbicide.
Paraquat affects the lungs,heart, liver, kidneys,
cornea, adrenal glands, skin, and digestive
system. lt causes skin and eye irritation and also
has caused skin sensitization. Paraquat splashed
in the eye can irritate, burn, and cause corneal
damage and scarring of the eyes.
Direct contact with paraquat solutions or
aerosol mists may cause skin burns, dermatitis,
and damage to fingernails. After prolonged skin
exposure, workers get damaged fingernails as
indicated by discoloration, nail deformities, or
loss of nails.
Effects due to high acute exposure to paraquat
may include excitability and lung congestion,
which in some cases leads to convulsions.
incoordination, and death by respiratory failure.
If swallowed, burning of the mouth and throat
often occurs, followed by gastrointestinal tract
irritation, resulting in abdominal pain, loss of
appetite, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. After
a person ingests a large amount of paraquat,
he or she is likely to immediately have pain and
swelling of the mouth and throat.
The next signs of illness following ingestion
are gastrointestinal symptoms. such as nausea.
vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea (which
may become bloody). Severe gastrointestinal
symptoms may result in dehydration, electrolyte
abnormalities (not enough sodium and potassium
in the body), and low blood pressure.

1548

Paraquat

Ingestion of small to medium amounts of
paraquat may lead to development of liver.
kidney or heart failure. or lung scarring, within
several days to several weeks. Ingestion of
large amounts leads to pulmonary edema, lung
scarring, respiratory failure, leading to possible
death, heart injury, increased heart rate, confusion, seizures. or coma , within a few hours to
a few days.
Other toxic effects include thirst, shortness
of breath, rapid heart rate, kidney failure, lung
sores, and liver damage. Some symptoms may
not occur until days after exposure. Persons with
lung problems may be at increased risk from
exposure. Many cases of illness and/or death
have been reported in humans.
REFERENCES - Murphy.

COMMENTS - Experimental results have indicated the existence of a parathyroid secretion
whose action diminishes the level of calcium in
the blood. It was the clinical syndrome of the
primitive hyperparathyroid hormone which drew
Fouche's attention to establishing a homeopathic
symptomatology.
Primary hyperparathyroidism is explained by
an osseous syndrome whose clinical manifestation is expressed by pain in the bones,aggravated
by standing or walking and also expressed by
spontaneous fractures, swelling in the bones
and bone deformities.
In radiology, one can observe abnormal
transparency of the skeleton, the cortex of the
long bones is decalcified, the medullary canal is
enlarged and these signs are especially present
in the hands and jaws. Cavities can also be seen,
again, primarily in the hands and jaws, as well
as tumors, which enlarge the bones by pushing
back the periosteum.
The extra-osseous syndrome occurs in 40%
of the cases. It is characterized by its effects
on the urinary organs, polyuria, kidney stones
and nephrocalcinosis. Effects on the digestive
system with anorexia, post-prandial epigastric
pains and constipation. Gastric atony and ulcers
in the low duodenum.
Effects on the heart muscles with palpitations, tachycardia and shortening of the Q. T.
interval on the electrocardiogram. Effects on the
muscles with asthenia and muscular hypotonia.
Psychological effects with depressive tendency
and mental confusion.
The syndrome is characterized by an increase
of calcium and reduction of phosphorus in the
blood, as well as an increase of phosphates in the
urine and an increase of the alkaline phosphateliberating enzymes.
Fouche noticed that the removal of the parathyroid gland improved the condition of patients
with chronic ankylosing rheumatism, but only
temporarily.

1549

Parathyroidinum
Secondary hyperparathyroidism can occur as a
defense reaction by the organism, which aims to
maintain the normal level of calcium in the blood.
The level can become reduced as a result of
a diminution in the calcium deposits in the bone
or disorders of alimentary deposits or because
of absorption complaints.
It can also be reduced from destruction of
the skeleton following osseous carcinoma or
myelomas, or from kidney infections, kidney
malfunctioning, glomerulonephritis, tubular
nephritis, idiopathic increase in the level of
calcium in the urine.

Harmine, which is being used in research into

HERBAL- Throughout the Aztec empire, avocado
was used as both a food and medicine. All parts
of the tree was used for medicinal purposes. Native Guatemalans have long used the avocado
to stimulate hair growth, repel worms, and treat
diarrhea.
The fruit is highly nutritious, containing calcium,
phosphorus, iron, and vitamins. Avocado is rich
in potassium and vitamins B6 and E, which can
help in relieving stress and sexual problems,
such as infertility and impotence.
Although many believe that avocados are
fattening, they contain a high amount of monounsaturated fats, particularly oleic acid, making it
a powerful antioxidant foot. The oleic acid offers
protection against heart disease, strokes, and
cancer. There is some evidence to suggest the
fruit can help lower cholesterol.
The fats are also easily digestible and contain
anti-fungal and antibacterial actions that, when
pureed, make an excellent food for invalids,
convalescents and sick children. In some parts
of Africa, the fruit pulp is used as a baby food.
Externally, the fruit soothes the skin, helps heal
wounds, and stimulates hair growth. Avocado oil
nourishes and softens rough, dry, or flaking skin.
Stimulates the production of collagen, helping
reduce the appearance of wrinkles.

HOMEOPATHIC - Phosphorus was discovered in
1673 by Brandt, an alchemist of Hamburgh, and
shortly afterwards by Kunkel in Saxony. According
to Teste, attempts were made to use it in medicine
immediately after discovery. Kunkel made it into his
"luminous pills," and Kramer claimed to have cured
with it diarrhea, epilepsy and malignant fevers.
Teste offered a list of old-school cures, which
included continuous, bilious and intermittent
fevers, general edema, measles, two cases of
pneumonia of the left lung with ataxic symptoms, chronic rheumatism of the legs, strokes.
hydrocephalus, periodic headaches, catalepsy,
epilepsy, and chronic lead poisoning.
Hahnemann's provings have been added to by
later provings, by numerous cases of poisoning
and by the effects on workers in match factories,
most notably, necrosis of the lower jaw.
The vapor given off by unignited phosphorus is
phosphorus oxide. The jaw affection, called "the
phossy-jaw" by the workers, is accompanied by
profound adynamia and frequently ends in death.
The form of the disease differs according to
whether the upper or lower jaw is attacked. ln the
former case, it generally pursues a chronic and
mild course, end in in exfoliation, scars and cure.

Phosphorus

In the latter, the necrosis may be either acute
or chronic, but is always severe and the patients
usually die of "tuberculosis" fever.
Phos. irritates, inflames and degenerates
the mucus membranes. It inflames the serous
membranes, the spinal cord and nerves. It causes
paralysis and destroys bone, especially in the
lower jaw and tibia. It disorganizes the blood,
causing fatty degeneration of blood vessels and
every tissue and organ of the body.
It gives rise to hemorrhages and hematogenous jaundice. Phos. produces a picture of
destructive metabolism.lt causes yellow atrophy
of the liver and sub-acute hepatitis.
Ill effects of iodine and excessive use of salt.

A man, 48 inhaled the vapor of burning Phos.
Among his symptoms was a sensation as if
something twitched under his skin or was creeping between skin and flesh. Twitching of single
bundles of tissues at different times like playing
on a piano. Tongue often refused to move when
speaking so that he stammered.
E. R. Heath had some decidedly "phosphorescent" symptoms. Darting, cutting pains,
causing much distress, starting from different
points and flashing over the whole abdomen.
He imagined an aurora borealis and seemed
to distinctly hear voices shouting "Beautiful, oh!
was not that splendid?" as the pains became
more severe and lasting.
He sprang from the bed and tried to collect his
thoughts, had numbness all over with sensation
of myriads of needles slightly pricking him.Throat
dry and parched, aflame seemed to pass through
him. Feet seemed glued to the floor.
With great difficulty he reached the vessel and
as soon as the bowels began to act the pains
changed to cramps. Stools were like scrapings
of intestines. They were almost constant, with
tenesmus, for over two hours. He lay down in bed
after, weak, sore, and almost helpless.
Clarke reported a case of spinal decay with
paralytic symptoms in a woman aged 67. She
had a history of a strained back thirty-five years
before, and of lumbago and sciatica five years
before he saw her. Pains in the scapula and
chest, she could not walk unless supported about
the waist. She was cured with Phos. 1,OOOc, the
curvature remained, although the decay and
paralysis were removed. The Phos. caused
dryness of her mouth, lips and throat.
W. A. Nicholas reported the case ofT. B., 51,
whom he saw after a four months' illness. The
case began with congestion of the brain on the
sudden death of his wife and was followed by
bronchitis. During all this time he was heavily
drugged. A rather long walk brought on a severe
attack of angina pectoris. Bell. 1x gave much
relief. Nicholas noticed he put his hand to the
back of his neck. Phos. 1c relieved entirely.
Hansen cured a case of purpura in a girl of
10. The disease began with loss of appetite and
pains in the stomach, but as soon as the purpura
spots appeared, the pains ceased and the appetite returned. The inner thighs were affected.
Phos. 2c cured.

HERBAL- Calabar is the type of a genus of Leguminosae of the tribe Phaseoleae. It has flowers
very like Phaseolus except that its beardedstyle is
terminated by agreat oblique hood, covering the
blunt stigma. lt is this hood that distinguishes the
genus and gives it its name. It is a great twining
climber and has purplish flowers.
Physostigma is the "ordeal-bean"of old. The
seeds are very poisonous and are used by the
Calabari to determine guilt and innocence. When
ingested, the person either vomits or dies, if they
die they are considered guilty, if they vomit, they
are innocent.
Observed cases showed twitchings, especially in the back, and death in thirty minutes. In
poisoning cases, the most notable feature was
complete muscular prostration.
A group of children in Liverpool ate beans
that they found among the sweepings of a ship
from Africa. Forty-six were admitted to a hospital
with loss of muscular power, prostration, feeble,
slow pulse.
Cold, perspiring skin, cold limbs, vomiting in
nearly all cases, diarrhea in one-third of them.
At first there was colic, but later on remarkable
freedom from pain. Pupils contracted in many,
in one they contracted during sleep, dilated
when aroused.

Physostigma venenosum
In cases of poisoning, people experience a
speedy general paralysis. Death occurs from
failure of respiration, although the heart may be
poisoned both directly and through its nerves.
The paralysis is seated in the spinal cord.
The muscles are affected by fluttering tremors.
Involuntary muscles are excited to active movements and expulsive efforts. The intestines are
often twisted up in knots. All the secretions are
somewhat increased.
Many provings have been made with Phys.,
among which a proving made by Christison on
himself is remarkable. Simpson and Douglas
Maclagan were sent for to attend to him in his
collapsed state. Simpson could only compare it
to the state produced by severe flooding, though
Christison's only sensation was oneof"extreme
but not unpleasant faintness." Maclagan thought
it a lot like aconite poisoning. Christison could
not get his will into his muscles except by a
tremendous effort.
Warmth to Christison's feet and a mustard
plaster to his whole abdomen gave great relief
and he was then able to turn on his left side, but
only remained there a very short time on account
of the tumultuous action of the heart it caused.
He became drowsy and slept, but his mind
was so active in sleep that on awaking he did not
know that he had slept. The tumultuous action of
the heart continued on waking, but strong coffee
quickly restored the whole condition and made
the heart regular.
Indigestion was observed by Christison and
many other provers, "as if large pieces of food
had been suddenly swallowed." It began under
the upper sternum, descending and increasing in
intensity until it reached the epigastrium.
Belchings then occurred and a reversal of
direction followed, the sensation ending where
it began. With other provers, there was a sensation of weight and hardness. Christison also
experienced giddiness and dimness of vision.
Phys., and its alkaloid eserine, are best known
in old school practice for its action on the eye,
especially of contracting the pupil.
The effects are more definite when the drug
(tincture, extract or solution of alkaloid) is applied
to the eye directly, but one myopic prover had
his myopia much diminished.

HERBAL - Phytolacca is a branching herbaceous
plant with a thick, perennial root. sometimes larger
than a man's leg in diameter. The plant is common
throughout North America, the Azores, North
Africa and China. It grows in damp places.
The young shoots, though extremely acrid,are
rendered harmless by boiling and are eaten like
asparagus in the United States. The berries have
a popular repute as a remedy for cancer and
rheumatism. The berries of Phytolacca octandra
are used in Mexico and the West Indiesas a soap.
According to Raffinesque, the ash of the plant is
45 percent caustic potash, and the plant contains
an acid, phytolactic acid, which is closely allied
to malic acid. Phytolacca has been used as an
escharotic in cancers, ulcers, etc.
HOMEOPATHIC- Phyt. is pre-eminently a glandular
and rheumatic remedy. lt powerfully affects the
fibrous and osseous tissues, and the sheathes
and fascias of muscles. Hence it becomes an
admirable remedy in rheumatic affections.
It has a special affinity for the muscles of the
shoulders and arms. Acts on the muscles of the
neck and back, tendons and joints, periosteum,
throat, digestive tract and the right side.
General soreness over the whole body, the
patient moans and groans every time he moves.
Lameness, soreness and a bruised feeling are
felt all over the body. It combines with the pain,
intense prostration and great exhaustion.
Rheumatic pain, tendency to affect the outer
aspect of limbs. Sudden achiness. Pains come
and go suddenly, change places. Sore, hard
aching pains. The pain occurs in such quick
succession that it renders the leg powerless
numb and heavy. Each movement elicits groans.

and painful nodes. Acts on scar tissue. Hastens

HOMEOPATHIC - Pic-ac. was discovered by Hausman in 1788. It is formed by the action of nitric
acid on carbolic acid, salicin, silk and many other
substances. Pic-ac. and its compounds are among
the most powerful explosives known,lydite being
an example.
Picric acid crystallizes in bright yellow needles
or scales of very bitter taste, sparingly soluble in
water. The yellow color is imparted to the eyes
and skins of patients who take it in the crude, and
it not only produces a semblance ofjaundice, but
actually disorganizes the liver if pushed.
Acts upon the brain, spinal cord, lumbar
region, occiput, kidneys and sexual organs.
Weakness. heavy. tired feeling in body and
mind. It causes degeneration of the spinal
cord with paralysis. It acts upon the generative
organs probably through the lumbar centers of
the spinal cord.
Occipital and bursting headaches (Gion.).
The headache, frontal or occipital is worse on
any attempt to use the mind and it may extend
down the spine. Headache extending from the
top of the spine up over the head to the eyes.
Neurasthenia (Ox-ac.). Worn out persons,
mentally and physically. Cachexia. Progressive, pernicious anemia. Prostration, weakness
and pain of back. Muscular debility. Heavy tired
feeling. Numbness. Formication. Pins and needle
sensation in limbs.
Burning in many parts, along spine in legs.
Sallow complexion. Uremia with complete
anuria. Brain-fatigue and sexual excitement.
Degeneration of the spinal cord with paralysis.
Myelitis with spasms and prostration. Acute
ascending paralysis. Typist's or writer's palsy.
Thery of Paris accidentally discovered in Picac. solution a remedy for bums. He twice dropped
burning matter on his hands while working with
a Pic-ac. disinfectant and was astonished at the
absence of pain or injury.
From that date Pic-ac. became his principal
remedy for burns and though others have
complained that it caused violent pains. Thery
has only once in some thousands of cases had
to abandon its use on that account. Aone percent
solution applied on lint is the best application for
bums until granulations begin to form.

A. C. Blackwood detailed the usesofPic-ac. for

The clothing was removed and the burnt surface

Blisters were opened but he carefully preserved
the epithelial covering.
Ifextensive, the whole surface might be bathed
with the solution and strips of sterilized gauze
soaked and applied to entirely cover it, a layer

over all.
After three or four days the dressing was
removed carefully after thorough moistening,
as it adhered closely. The second dressing was
applied as at first and allowed to remain a week.
The staining of the hands and linen caused by the
dressing can be removed by boric acid.

HOMEOPATHIC -Piloc. is one of the most characteristic of several alkaloids which have been isolated
from jaborandi (Pilocarpus pinnatus). It has been

The hair as well asthe skin is affected by Piloc.,

Schmitz of Cologne treated two bald men with

In both a secondary effect occurred ,the growth

hairs" of considerable growth, so as to entirely
obliterate his previous baldness. Piloc. has also
been known to turn white hair black.
In a case of lead paralysis, it produced profuse
salivation and sweat with sensation of great coldness and excessive tremors of limbs. Salivation
and sweating speedily occur.
Dilatation of blood vessels, temporal artery

peppers are tropical climbing shrubs. Pip. nigrum.
yields the pepper of commerce. When ripe, the fruit
is red. Black pepper is gathered before it is fully ripe
and spread on mats in the sun, when it loses it red
color and becomes black and shriveled. White
pepper is the same fruit freed from its outer skin
by maceration in water and subsequent rubbing .

PIPERAZINUM
(Piperazidine)
PHARMACY - pipe. Piperazinum. Piperazidine.
Diethylen-diamine. Trituration. Solution. Planets:
Moon. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL - Glaucoma. Gout. Lead paralysis.
Kidney, colic.
HOMEOPATHIC - Pipe. is a synthet.Jc product which
was intended to replace Sperrnin and was named
Disperrnine. lt was found. however to be a different
body both in chemical and physiological properties.
It occurs 1n well-defined, colorless. acicular
crystals (Helbing)orin lustrous tables(J. Gordon),
IS deliquescent and mostly soluble in water.
It readily unites with uric acid, forming a very
soluble compound (urate of piperazine). When
taken by the mouth 11 1s not entirely oxidized,
as part is discoverable unchanged in the urine.
John Gordon experimented with Pipe. and
found that a 1 percent solution in normal urine
at body temperature dissolved to a large extent
a fragment of uric acid calculus and converted
undissolved portions to a granular and pulpy
condition. The amount of urea is increased in
the urine of those taking it.
J. R. Hamilton of Hawick reported success
in treating kidney colic with Pipe. and Walter
of Odessa. cleared up two cases of glaucoma,
giving one grain daily in carbonated water. all
the symptoms disappearing within three weeks.
According to Cooper, a patient, after a teaspoonful dose of an effervescing preparation of
Pipe., complained that he was seized with a bad
attack of acute gout, that was quite unexpected.
Helbing said it has been used with success in
mental diseases and in a case of lead paralysis
with "very remarkable results."
RELATIONS- Compare: Phlor., Hydrang., Urt-u.
REFERENCES -Clarke.

HERBAL - This small tree has unequally pinnate
leaves and entire, oval leanets. The nowers
are in lateral clusters, and appear in profusion
before the leaves. The bark of the tree is very
astringent, and acts as a narcotic poison. When
Pisc. is chewed, there is an unpleasant acrimony
in mouth like that of Mez.
Locally the tincture is used for toothaches in
decayed teeth. Piscidia is sedative, hypnotic
and narcotic. A good nerve sedative and pain
killer. The pounded leaves and young branches
of Piscidia and some allied species are used like
cocculus, for poisoning fish hence the name
Piscidia (Piscis-caedere).
HOMEOPATHIC- Excessive restlessness and insomnia.lnsomnia due to pain, worry or nervous
excitement, it usually produces a quiet, deep

ovarian or uterine. Neuralgic and spasmodic
affections. Tetanus.
Toothaches in decayed teeth. Spasmodic
coughs, especially cough of phthisis. Bronchial
catarrhs, bronchitis. Asthma, nervous cough.
Fevers with a violent sensation of heat generally increasing in intensity, the sensation of
burning gradually extended to the surface and
a profuse diaphoresis burst out from every pore.
COMMENTS-The experiment recorded in Allen is
by W. Hamilton, who took a drachm of the Pisc.
tincture in water for toothache and went off to
sleep with great suddenness. Profound sleep,
he remained motionless the whole night, when
he awoke, twelve hours later, he was still holding
the glass and uncorked vial from which he had
taken the dose.

HOMEOPATHIC -The posterior lobe of pituitary
gland releases the oxytocin and antidiuretic
hormones. Removal or injury to the posterior lobe
will lead to the symptoms of diabetes insipidus.
It acts upon the parasympathetc center in the
hypothalamus. Rate of secretion is controlled
from the hypothalamic nucleri.
Antidiuretic hormone, or vasopressin, promotes the reabsorption of water in the kidneys.
It raises the blood pressure and plays a role in
the water balance. Also affects the production
of breast milk.
It constricts the arteries of the abdominal
organs, therefore it use to stop hemorrhage
involving abdominal blood vessels. It may
produce cerebral or coronary arterial spasms
in large doses.
Oxytocin causes uterine contractions at tenm.
Allopaths used it for the induction or stimulation
of the labor. It has been given to relieve painful breast engorgement. Promotes breast milk
release during lactation. Also for postpartum
hemorrhage and uterine atony.
Its action is controlled in pregnancy by progesterone, which diminishes its action, and estrogen,
which increases it.
An enzyme in the blood plasma of pregnant
women appears to mediate this control.
Mind, anxiety, Head, pain. Dropsy. Basal
metabolism rate increased. Blood pressure
elevated. Blood sugar increased, Blood vessels
constricted. Pulse, slow. Weakness.

COMMENTS- On the basis of these observations,
Ghose made use of this sarcode in its 30th
potency in anginal attacks with coronary spasms.
Ghose's first case was that of a middle aged
man of 45, suffering from diabetes for two years.
He developed mild anginal attacks after exertion
and a sense of heaviness in the precordium.
His cardiograph showed coronary disorder
and was advised perfect rest. Blood pressure
was more or less nonmal, pulse was 72 bpm.
He was apparently a well-built man and was on
a restricted diet for a long time due to diabetes.
Pitu-p. 30, three times a week, brought great
relief of the precordial pain and heaviness; within
a fortnight he could walk about in plain ground
without any discomfort.
Ghose also used it in a case of old man, 70, with
dyspepsia who used to get severe attacks of pain
in the heart when walking , and particularly when
getting up at night to attend calls for urination.
He was relieved with the very first dose of Pitup. 30 and could move about freely without any
discomfort and could also attend to his nature's
calls at night without feeling any pain.
In a third case, Ghose treated an old man, 65,
suffering from coronary thrombosis for about a
year and a half. He had W. R. 10/10 which was
treated homeopathically.
He was living without any heart symptom for
any other trouble for about a year, when suddenly
he felt agonizing pain in the heart at 11 o'clock
at night, with severe dyspnea and moist sounds
all over the chest.
All these symptoms pointed to edema of
lungs. Pulse was soft and slow. Blood pressure
was rather low.
Pitu-p. 30, repeated every half an hour, relieved
the pain completely and made the dyspnea tolerable. A sanguinous expectoration followed for
which he was given one dose of Mere-s. 200 and
later on a few doses of Thyr. 200 which stopped
the dyspnea completely.

Plantago major

HERBAL - Plantago has a reputation in herbal
medicine from remote antiquity, including for
use in intermittent fevers. In 1558 the Herbal of
Dodoens commended the juice of leaves or roots
for "toothache and bleeding of gums." External
use in toothache in hollow teeth, otorrhea, itching
and poison oak. Incised wounds.
John Parkinson, in his Theater of Plants (1640),
said that "the root taken fresh out of the ground,
washed and gently scraped with a knife, then put
into the ear, cures the toothache like a charm."
Reutlinger noted that in Switzerland the leaf
tissues were frayed out and put into the ear for
the same purpose. If they relieve the pain they
"turn black" and have to be removed, if there is
no relief the leaves remain green.
Hale summed up the ancient and modern history of Plantago Maj.,the weed that furnishes food
for cage-birds. In herbal practice, it is constantly
resorted to as an application in all disorders of
the skin with irritation, pain and heat, the bruised
leaves being applied to the part.
HOMEOPATHIC- Hale noted that erysipelas, rhus
poisoning, erythema, burns, inflammation of
the glands, bruises, incised wounds, animal
bites, chilblains, and frostbite had all been

relieved by its use.
Plan. has a considerable clinical reputation in
the treatment of earache, toothache and bedwetting. Pyorrhea alveolaris. Gums bleed easily.
Sharp pain in the eyes, reflex from decayed
teeth or inflammation of middle ear. Eyeball is
very tender to touch.
Affects the nerves, causing neuralgia of
