HERBAL -Ayurvedic physicians prized Sol-x.as an
excellent remedy for cough, respiratory troubles,
cough associated with hoarseness, ophthalmia,
stone or calculus, stricture, and retention or suppression of urine.
Sol-x. is an aperient, carminative, expectorant,
and diuretic. It is given in asthma, cough, catarrhal
affections of the lungs, fever, flatulent and pain
in the chest. As a diuretic, the decoction is given
in dysuria, cystitis, calculi and dropsy, also given
in costiveness.
A paste of the seeds is locally applied to
promote suppuration of boils, buboes, and other
indolent chronic abscesses. Fumigation of the
fruit is largely used by natives as sialogogue
and applied for the relief of pain in carious teeth.
Charaka recommended Sol-x.in hemorrhoids,
cough,delirium tremens, urinary difficulties,stone
and calculus. Shushruta found it efficacious in
ophthalmia, respiratory troubles, cough, urinary
difficulties and troubles and stricture.
Chakradatta said that Sol-x. is useful in cough,
stricture, and urinary troubles. Bangasena has
recommended it in the cough of children.
Sol-x. is used by them separately or as a
principal ingredient in their compound medicines
for the above mentioned complaints.
HOMEOPATHIC - Hoarseness (Caust., Phos.,
Sel.), associated with cough. Bronchitis, pneumonia, or bronco-pneumonia associated with
voice loss. Asthma.
Fevers associated with thirst, vomiting, aversion to food, burning sensation felt over the body
and pains felt over the collective body of the ribs.
Stricture, suppression or retention of urine and
kidney stone.
Preventive against smallpox. The Ayurvedic
physicians also used it against smallpox, dose

HERBAL- Also known as "Toothache Plant" or
"Paracress," Spilanthes acmella is a flowering
herb in the Asteraceae family. Its leaves and
flower heads contain an analgesic agent that
may be used to numb toothaches. It is native
to the tropics of Brazil, though it is grown as an
ornamental (and occasionally as a medicinal) in
various parts of the world.
Chewing on one of the flower buds will numb
your mouth and make you salivate. The leaves
may be used topically to treat bacterial and fungal
skin diseases such as ringworm. Leaf decoction
is used as diuretic and lithotriptic. Root decoction
is used as purgative.

s

Spilanthes acmella
The whole plant is used in treatment of dysentery. Useful for enhancing the immune system's
resistance to infections. It stimulates wound
healing, protects the individual from colds and
flu. Decreases allergic symptoms.
Anti-bacterial. Inhibits the yeasVfungal organism Candida albicans.
Indicated for swollen glands, gum disease and
all manner of acute bacterial, viral and fungal
infections. Herpes. Sore throats. Useful against
blood parasites, particularly malarial spirochetes,
either as a prophylactic or as a treatment for
malarial paroxysms. Lyme disease.
Because of their high isobutylamide content,
both Spilanthes and Prickly Ash have similar
stimulating and therapeutic actions.

PHARMACY - spira. Spiranthes autumnalis. Lady's
tresses. N. 0 . Orchidaceae. Tincture of the root.
Planets: Saturn. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL-Acidity. Back, pain. Belching. Breasts,
painful. Breath,putrid.Bums. Colic. Coryza. Dyspareunia.Eczema.Hysteria.Jaundice. Kidneys,pain.
Lumbago. Milk, excessive. Nausea. Nosebleed.
Rash. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Toothache.
Vision, dimness. Vomiting.
HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany reported that
the genus to which this orchid belongs received
its name from the spiral arrangement of flowers.
Spiranthes is an anti-phlogistic remedy akin to
Aeon. Its symptoms showing congestion and
inflammation. The tuberous roots of Spira. were
formerly esteemed as an aphrodisiac.
HOMEOPATHIC-Spira. has been used for milk-flow
in nursing women, lumbago and rheumatism.
Pulsations in arteries over whole body.Acidity and
burning in esophagus with eructation. Colic with
drowsiness and spasmodic yawning. Appears
intoxicated. Lies on left side rather than right.
MIND - Melancholy. Complaining and sobbing. Illhumor.Confusionofideas.lndolence and boredom.
Worse from mental effort. The least emotion or
excitement causes palpitations.
Abdomen - Intermittent pressure in umbilical
region. Colic. Pain, weakness, tympanites after
a meal. Borborygmi. Desire to tighten clothes.
Piercing, sharp insupportable pain in colon, on
becoming erect. Laughing heat in lower abdomen. Eruption in groin.
Back - Cramp-like pain in neck at night compelling change of position. Lumbago. Lumbago
preventing walking. Pain in center of scapula.
Pain in scapula, when standing, worse walking.

COMMENTS - The tincture of the root was proved
by Dr. Patti Chagon, Due de Sorentino, who said
of it, "The action of this drug begins with decided
symptoms of inflammation of the eyes, chin,
chest, which become red and hot, the whole skin
is dry and hot, the hands are burning, the limbs
of the feet are cold most of the time, there is a
sensation of oppression and heat with palpitation
and a desire to uncover.
"This condition lasted two hours and gave
place to others including desire to meditate and
complain, vertigo, pains in shoulders, boredom,
loss of appetite.
"The last symptoms to appear are: pains in
scalp, on vertex, distress in kidneys and intestinal
troubles after eating. The secretions of urine and
milk were first diminished afterwards increased.
"The aphrodisiac property of Spira. was shown
in some of the symptoms of the proving and
this bears on the increased secretion of milk. A
number of symptoms appear in the lower abdomen. The globus hystericus rises from thence to
esophagus. Heat in lower abdomen, preceding
belchings, caused by laughing."
RELATIONS- Compare: (1) Cypr. (2) Skin and mucus
membranes, Arum-!. (3) Desire for tight clothing,
dryness of vagina, Nat-m. (4) Pain followed by
numbness, Gnaph.

SPONGIA TOSTA
(Roasted Sponge)
PHARMACY - spong. Spongia tosta. Roasted
sponge. Common Sponge. Porifera. Radiata.
N. 0 . Coelenterata. Tincture of the powdered
sponge after toasting. Planets: Mercury. His tori·
cal dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Aneurysm. Angina,
pectoris. Asthma. Bronchitis. Catalepsy. Chin,
disorders. Clumsiness. Colds. Constipation.
Coughs. Croup. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Dyspnea. Endocarditis. Epididymitis. Exhaustion.
Exophthalmos. Fainting. Gland, disorders.
Goiter, exophthalmic. Headache. Heart,
hypertrophy. Hernia. Hyperthyroid. Jaw joint,
pain. Laryngismus. Laryngitis. Lung, disorders.
Myopia. Orchitis. Rheumatic, fever. Rheumatism. Somnambulism. Testicles, disorders.
Thyroid, disorders. Tuberculosis. Varicose,
veins. Whooping cough. Worms.
HOMEOPATHIC - According to Hahnemann,
toasted sponge was first mentioned as a specific
for goiter by the alchemist Arnold Von Villanova in
the thirteenth century, but it was generally given
mixed with other substances and had fallen into
disuse when Hahnemann proved it.
The virtues of Spong. have been attributed to
the iodine contained in it and partially liberated
by the presence of roasting. But Spong. contains
many other elements besides iodine and has a
distinctive action of its own.
Affects the heart valves, larynx, trachea
and glands. Anxiety with pain in the region of
heart or dyspnea. Hypertrophy of the heart. The

right heart is affected, with asthmatic symptoms
Dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic
heart disease. Useful for the symptoms of the

respiratory organs, cough, croup, heart disorders
and tubercular diathesis.
Dryness of mucus membranes, of tongue,
pharynx, larynx, and trachea. Cough is caused
by dryness, hacking, crowing, "dry as a bone,"
sounding like a saw being driven through a
pine board.
Cough is excited by talking, by dry, cold
winds, better by eating or drinking, swallowing,

especially from warm food .

Kent gave the indication "Rheumatic fever
after having been over-heated with arising heart
complications."
Nash gave the keynote of Spong. in valvular
diseases, "Awakes out of sleep from a sense of
suffocation with violent, loud cough, great alarm,
agitation, anxiety and difficult respiration." Nash
said it is better than Lach., and relieves the "dry,
chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart
disease" more frequently and more permanently
than Naja. Psor. also meets thickening of joints
after rheumatic fever.
Boenninghausen's croup powders consisted
of a sequence of Aeon., Spong., and Hep., given
in that order. Spong. is dry, Hep. rattling, Spong.
worse before midnight,Hep. worse after midnight.

SQUILLA MARITIMA
{Sea Onion)
PHARMACY - squil. Squilla maritima. Sea onion.
Squill. N.0 . Liliaceae. Red variety. Hyacinlhaceae.
Tincture of fresh bulb. Planets: Mercury. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL - Angina, pectoris. Ascites. Asthma.
Bright's, disease.Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Conjunctivitis, phlyctenular. Coryza. Cough,
catanhal. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy, splenic.Dyspnea. Eyes, disorders. Fidgets. Heart, palpitations.
Hydrothorax.Lungs, disorders. Measles.Pleurisy.
Pneumonia. Spleen, disorders.Toothaches. Urine,
excessive. Whooping cough. Worms.
HERBAL- Squilla maritima grows on the shores ofthe
Mediterranean Sea and has had aplace in medicine
from the most ancient time. The genus Squilla is
distinguished from Allium by having the flowers
inserted one above the other on the scape, and
from Omithogalum by having the petals deciduous.

1910

5

Squi/la maritima
Green's Herbal noted that Squil. promotes
expectoration and urine in large doses, vomiting
and purging. "Its cardiac action is exactly the
same as that of Digitalis."
An old rule runs "Put squills in every coughmixture." Mile recorded "Diuretic, expectorant,
emetic, cathartic and a narcotic-acrid poison
in large doses it produces inflammation of the
alimentary and urinary canals and a dose of 24
grains has proved fatal."
According to Hamilton, Avicenna employed
Squil. "in complaints of the gums in inveterate
coughs in diseases of the spleen in dropsy and
jaundice and forbids its use in ulceration of the
viscera," the last caution also being mentioned
by Celsus.
HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper noted that Squil., if
much handled, irritates the skin, and in large
doses excites nausea, strangury, bloody urine
and hemorrhoids. Fatal inflammation, gangrene
of stomach and bowels in small doses. The
continuous use of squills seems to cause teeth
and gums to ache.
The reputation of Squil. as a splenic was revived by Rademacher, whom Burnett quoted, "I
have found it quickly and surely helpful in painful
spleen diseases disorders painful and beyond
any doubt in and of the spleen.
In those dull pains on the border of the left
hypochondriac and epigastric regions, there
being no signs of any liver affection, I have used
Squil. as a remedy with advantage."
Rademacher also mentioned as cured by Squil.
those so-called "stomach pains"that are made
much better by lying on the left side, one case of
asthma from a splenic affection with nocturnal
exacerbation, and possibly splenic dropsy.

HERBAL - Wood betony has been used in

used in European countries for the treatment
of edema, hives, and shingles. Poultice made
from wood betony may also help to reduce
inflammation and pain associated with skin tears,
stings, and bites.
It has anti-inflammatory properties that help
ease the inflammation of the skin caused by
eczema as well as other skin conditions.
Wood betony help to relieve asthma and respiratory infections like pneumonia and bronchitis.

help to soften the buildup of thick mucus. This
will assist in helping drainage of mucus, in tum
alleviating sinus congestion.

of the wood betony plant is used as mouthwash.
Gargling with an infusion of wood betony can
help to relieve sore throats. Herbal mouthwash of
wood betony helps to reduce gum inflammation
and stop gum bleeding.
Wood betony displays diuretic activity, which
helps to increase urinary rate. This may help to
remove toxins from the urinary system, in turn
enhancing kidney function. The diuretic action of
wood betony also helps urinary tract infections.
This herb was used to relieve the discomfort
of menstrual cramps.
Herbalists also recommend betony tea and
tinctures for the treatment of migraines. Wood
betony has been used to lower blood pressure.

HERBAL-Dioscorides used the seed ofStavesacre
to producing vomiting and salivation and to cure
atoothache,"the origin of which application," said
Hahnemann, "was evidently domestic practice."
Stavesacre is a very poisonous plant that is
rarely used in modern herbal medicine. The
seed is antispasmodic, cathartic, emetic and
vermifuge. The seeds cause a strong salivation if they are chewed and have been used
in the treatment of toothache and other painful
conditions of the throat and gums. They are so
strongly emetic and cathartic, however, that they
are rarely used internally.
Externally, adecoction is used to treat itchy skin
and parasites. The plant has been used externally
in the treatment of warts, lice and itches.
Stavesacre seeds, though poisonous when
taken by mouth, are used to make medicine
that is applied to the skin. Washes or ointments
made from stavesacre seeds are applied to the
skin to treat lice and nerve pain.

COMMENTS - J. H. Schultze, when suffering
from toothache, took some of the Staphysagria
seed in his mouth, but it gave him such a violent
exacerbation that he thought he should go mad.
Brunton noted that the seed was called "an
exterminator of vermin" by the Greeks and as
such it enters into the composition of an ointment
(unguentum pediculosum). This last is the only
use of Staph. known to orthodox medicine.
Teste remarked that Staph., like Cocc., is used
in some countries for the purpose of stupefying
fish .Teste found Staph. 6c, like Cocc., useful as a
remedy for seasickness.To be successful, Staph.
had to be taken at the moment when diuiness
and nausea commenced, before vomiting set in
and it always helped ·nervous persons, not over
fat and disposed to sadness."
Staph. produced in Teste a"long lasting vertigo,
accompanied by continued nausea as in seasickness" and "vertigo, which ceases on rapidly
turning round on one's heel." This corresponds
with one of Hahnemann's symptoms, "wheeling
vertigo, especially while sitting, better by walking
about in a circle."
It is noteworthy that Staph. and Cocc. are both
head remedies and both effective against head
lice. Both also affect the genitals, Staph. more
so, and are remedies for crab lice.
An application of one part a dilution of the
tincture to four parts water will destroy the
parasites,although concurrent internal treatment
increases success.
In Teste's experience, Staph. was no less effective in nausea during pregnancy than nausea
caused by seasickness.
Tab. is another remedy for sickness and Teste
cured with Staph. effects of tobacco smoking
(excoriated tongue, stomach pain) and the habit
of "swallowing the tobacco smoke."
For the ill effects of anger, especially if the
indignation cannot have its natural expression.
"Was insulted, being too dignified to fight, swallowed his wrath and went home sick, trembling

Antioxidant· Antioxidants targetfree radicals
-atoms or molecules with unpaired electronsthat can cause disease and cellular damage.
Free radicals can damage cellular DNA and
initiate carcinogenesis-the beginnings ofcancer.
You can't really avoid free radicals, which are
byproducts of your body's metabolic processes,
but you can neutralize them by eating a diet rich
in antioxidants.
Anti-bacterial -The upsurge in bacterial infections that exhibit resistance to existing antibiotics
has intensified the search for new agents that
may prove more effective against these resistant
strains of bacteria. Researchers in Taiwan tested
four new antimicrobial compounds from star
anise and that were effective against 67 strains
of drug-resistant bacteria.
Appetite • Because of the herb's stimulating
effect on the digestive system, it has also been
used as an appetite enhancer for many decades
·in Asia. Sipping star anise tea is believed to help
increase a diminished appetite, especially when
the problem is related to illness or stress.

blackstrap molasses, raw organic honey or raw

Candida • Researchers found that extracts
and essential oils of star.anise exhibited strong
anti-fungal properties when tested against
Candida albicans. Candida is a yeast, a form of
fungi that occurs naturally in the human mouth,
throat, intestines and genitourinary tract.

Cook gave the case of Mr. X., 63, florid, robust,
temperature, had been many months under
treatment with 1ntense prostration, intermittent
pulse, and dyspnea, traced originally to cooling
off too rapidly when perspiring.
The urine contained much albumen, mucus
and some blood, specific gravity 1010. Great
tenderness over entire abdomen, especially
in region of ureters. Under remedies he would
improve for a few days, when a slight chill would
be followed by fever and the symptoms would
come back in full force.
The microscope revealed pus cells and
granular epithelial cells in abundance. Stigm.
was then given, a teaspoonful of the fluid extract
every four hours. In less than a week there was
visible improvement. The constant calls to urinate
ceased and the patient could go through the night
w1thout being disturbed more than once or twice.
The specific gravity of the urine increased
and pus, blood and albumen disappeared. Only
a little abdominal tenderness remained, which
did not prevent the patient from attending to his
business and enjoying life.
Another use of Stigm. was communicated to
the profession by Dr. J. W. Pruitt. Pruitt's son took
a chill in the Arkansas river bottom. The chills
were stopped with the usual remedies, Chin.,
Ferr., Pipe., but every fourteen days would come
back with increased severity.
Presently gastric symptoms set in with anemia
and other symptoms of chronicity. "Shuck tea"
was recommended by a lay friend and was taken
for one day only. There was never a chill after.
Pruitt thence forward used Stigm. largely and
he found it was only in the chronic cases that it
was beneficial.

sandy prairies and meadows.
Stillingia was used traditionally in Native American medicine and by the Eclectic physicians in
the early 1900s to support skin health, the upper

Streptococcinum
COMMENTS - When there has been a number of
severe acute illnesses, Dr. Gordon, of Edinburgh,
maintained that the best results can be obtained
by antidoting the most recent infection first by its
appropriate nosode, proceeding backwards and
thus "curing in layers."
Another view is that, other things being equal,
the first lapse from health is of greatest importance and that this should be antidoted first to
undermine the superstructure and then deal with
the case according to the remaining symptoms.
Ghose wrote, "I have used Streptococcin
with very remarkable results in acute Bacillary
dysentery with excessive hemorrhage and high
rise of temperature with toxemia.
The more the blood the more it is indicated like
Mercurius, but there is no tenesmus or urinary
complications of Mercurius in Streptococcin.
"In very bad cases of bacillary dysentery, very
bad complications will follow and take a very
long time to cure if it cannot be checked in the
very beginning. In chronic cases of Dysentery
where blood with mucopurulent discharge does
not respond to indicated remedies or recurs and
prolongs unduly. I have seen it to stop the bloody
and mucopurulent discharge within a very short
time with a dose of Streptococcin 200c."

HOMEOPATHIC- The native method of preparing
the medicine is by moistening the mixture of the
three powders with a little vinegar and forming the
paste into pills of about a centimeter in diameter.
When taken by a healthy person these pills
cause fatigue, general indisposition, vertigo,
tingling of the hands and feet involuntary movements of jaw. When a person is bitten by a
poisonous animal, a dose of three or four grams
is administered in vinegar.
If none of these symptoms appear it is understood that the medicine is antagonized and the
dose is increased until some of the symptoms
manifest themselves, when the poison is considered to be destroyed. The use of alcohol is
forbidden while a patient is taking this medicine.
Vinegar appears to modify its virulence.
In animals poisoned with it, tetanicconvulsions
always begin in the hind legs and spread all over
the body. Brain, liver, kidneys and lungs were
found congested post mortem.
Generally improves nutrition, especially in
constitutional syphilis. Exhaustion with vertigo,
numbness and tingling in hands and feet involuntary action of lower jaw. Tetanic convulsions
beginning in legs and spreading over body.
Eczema, prurigo. Pustules and boils. Old
ulcers. Leprosy. Snakebites. Tertiary syphilis
and paralysis. Glandular disorders. Cancer of
glandular structures. Removes fetor and hemorrhage in cancer, revives the healing process.

distillation.The fumes of thecrude acid, he said,are

On this indication, he treated thirty people suffering from hay fever and cured them all, saving
them the necessity of making an annual exodus.
He gave one or two grains of the 3x trituration of
Succ. diluted in twelve teaspoonfuls of water, a
teaspoonful every two hours.
Burnett wrote in Diseases of Spleen, that the
non-rectified oil is used as an organ remedy in
spleen affections, especially when accompanied
by nervous and hysterical phenomena.
The crude oil is a thick brown liquid having a
strong empyreumatic odor. It is a powerful local
irritant and has been used with success as such
in lumbago, rheumatism and sciatica.
Succ-ac. enters into the composition of
"Roche's Embrocation," and "Haarlem Oil," and
has a popular reputation as a remedy for whooping cough, the directions being for it to be rubbed
into the spine night and morning.
Succ-ac. produces many nervous and hysterical symptoms.Asthma. Fear of trains and closed
places. Affections of spleen. Burnett noted it for
hysterical convulsions in women.

Burnett's keynote was "Painful spleen disorders where there are convulsive attacks such as
the hysterical and hypochondriacal often have."
Burnett related in his book a most remarkable

hyperesthesia, head pain, Dyspnea orthopnea,
convulsions" in a young woman "towards the
end of her teens."
After years of treatment, Burnett concluded
from Rademacher's account of Succ-ac. that
it might provide the remedy. It was given in
five-drop doses three times a day. In forty-eight
hours the convulsive attacks ceased and all the
phenomena slowly disappeared.
A keynote of Burnett's is "Fear of trains and

HOMEOPATHIC - Sulphur is an elementary substance, occurring in nature as a brittle crystalline
solid, burning in the air with a blue flame, being
oxidized to Sulphur dioxide (Sulphurous acid).

Sulphur is a product of volcanic eruptions,
found free in nature and was used from ancient
times to remove skin disorders. The reputation
of Sulphur as a remedy is perhaps as old as
medicine. "As early as 2,000 years ago," said
Hahnemann, "Sulph. had been used as the
most powerful specific against the scabies.
"The itch with which the workers in wool are
so much affected, causes an intolerably agreeable, tingling, itching, gnawing as of vermin.
Some designate it as an intolerably voluptuous
titillating itching, ceasing as soon as the parts
are scratched and commencing to bum, which
burning continues after the scratching.
"Sulph. frequently produces in healthy persons
burning-itching pimples and vesicles resembling
the itch vesicles and especially itching in the
joints and in the night."
The domestic use of Sulph. as a "Spring
medicine" is based on its anti-psoric properties.
"It is one of the most popular diaphoretics of the
day," said Milne, "few old women failing to use it
when any eruption is supposed to be struggling
through the skin."
The specific power of Sulph. to cure itch can
be abused if applied externally as baths and
ointments. Instead of being cured, the skin affection can be repelled and a host of secondary
disorders will appear in its place.
Sulph. is a majoranti-psoric.Agreat reabsorbent and is frequently needed after acute illnesses
which do not entirely clear up. Complaints that
relapse. When carefully selected remedies fail
to act, especially in acute diseases.
It is often of great use in beginning the treatment
of chronic diseases and in finishing acute ones
or when the reaction is deficient.
Irregular distribution of circulation, causing
local burning, throbbing or congestion,
flushes of heat, rush of blood to head, chest,

Ascending effects.
Affinity for the skin, where it produces heat

COMMENTS- Sulph. is used in various countries
for allaying pain in a variety of forms. A piece of
stick Sulph. carried in the pocket is commonly
used in England to ward off rheumatism. Natives of South America apply Sulph. in solid
form to painful parts and allow it to act for an
hour before result is effected. For lumbago and
chronic rheumatic pains a bag filled with Flowers of Sulphur, heated and applied to the part,
immediately relieves the pain.

An experienced sea captain testified to the
extreme frequency of rheumatism among his
sailors, but, he added, when carrying cargoes
of Sulph., he had never had a case of acute
rheumatism on board.
Dr. Laugardiere of Toulouse, reported to the
Academy of Medicine that he had discovered
a cure for croup: a tablespoonful of Flowers of
Sulphur dissolved in a tumbler of water.After three
days of this treatment his patients were rescued
from imminent death and fully recovered. Many
practitioners spoke highly of a local application
of Sulph. to the fauces in the treatment of croup
and diphtheria.
Nettle rash is often relieved by a little Flowers
of Sulphur, water and Sulph. mixed with sea sand
and rubbed over itch vesicles destroys the acarus
at once. In the early days of vaccination it was
found that the action of Sui ph. was adverse to the
receptivity of vaccine. According to Dr. Tierney,
Dr. Jenner failed in vaccinating thirty soldiers,
all under treatment by Sulph.
Cooper noted that operatives in sulphur mines
enjoy an immunity against ague when prevalent
in surrounding districts, and that, before going on
hunting expeditions in malarious districts, men in
Ethiopia submit themselves to fumigations with
Sulph. and find it an efficient prevention of ague.
Cooper thought there was a great probability of
Sulph. having a power of destroying the organisms in the blood of ague patients.
Hahnemann found in Sulph. the homeopathic
counterpart of the peculiar constitutional weakness which tends to manifest in itch-like eruptions
and which he named Psora. Su/ph. is the chief
of the anti-psoric remedies. It is this property
of Sulph. to divert to the surface constitutional
irritants which renders itthe chief of Hahnemann's
anti-psorics.
Sulph. has also an anti-psoric action independently of its power of "bringing out" rashes. The
psoric poison may be present and active in a
case of disease and "apparently well-indicated
remedies may fail to act" in consequence.
In such cases, one or two doses of Sulph. will
frequently antidote the psora and either clear up
the case or open the way for the action of other
remedies.ln such cases there will almost certainly
be some Sulph. indications present.

Sulphur

Sulph. is a potent antiseptic and is one of the
most certain destroyers of scabies. The exact
relati~n of acarus itch to psora and other itching
eruptions need not be considered.
But as Sulph. has the power of repressing
constitutional eruptions when locally applied, as
well as the power of destroying the acarus, it is
best to use other means (e.g., oil of lavender)
for the latter purpose and give Sulph. or other
indicated remedies internally.
The symptoms of latent psora are detailed in
Hahnemann's Chronic Diseases. They are, for
the most part, almost exact reproductions of the
symptoms of Sulph. But while Sulph. is the chief
of anti-psorics, it is only one of many and Sulph.
is in no way limited in its uses to cases of latent
or declared psora.
When well-selected remedies fail to act or
act too short a time because of the patient's
feeble reactive powers. Sulph. will often build
up the vital powers of the patient to effect the
cure. lt will clear the way by removing the psoric
miasm to permit other similar remedies on their
indications to cure the patient.
Useful for complaints that are always
relapsing (menses, leucorrhea, etc.), patient
seems to get almost well when the disease
returns again and again.

SULPHUR HYDROGENISATUM
(Sulfuretted Hydrogen)
PHARMACY - sui-h. Sulphur hydrogenisatum. Sulfuretted hydrogen. Solution of the gas. Planets:
Mercury. Historical dose: All potencies.
CLINICAL -Asphyxia. Asthma. Blood, poisoning.
Convulsions. Delirium. Fever. Headache. Mania.
Prostration. Tetanus. Typhoid fever.
HOMEOPATHIC - Sui-h. is a colorless inflammable
gas, having a sweetish taste and an exceedingly
fetid smell resembling rotten eggs. It is extremely
poisonous when inhaled. It is evolved when animal
.or vegetable tissues containing sulphur decay. It
also occurs in mineral springs, being liberated by
the reduction of gypsum or other sulphates through
the action of a microbe.
Sulph-h. is one of the remedies which help
"blood poisoning" especially when bad smells
are encountered.A5phyxia, tetanus, delirium,low
continued fever have been observed as resulting
from the gas.
COMMENTS - J. Wiglesworth recorded two cases
of insanity, one certainly and both probably, due to
inhaling the gas. The first concerned R. H., 32, an
engine man at chemical works, who had been kept
at home with an attack of bronchitis for ten days. A
fewdaysafterhis return to work he became "gassed"
(i.e., accidentally inhaled Sui-h.).
This caused headache, stupor, prostration,
compelling him to stay at home for a few days,
when he became wildly delirious. He passed into
a very excited state, shouting and gesticulating,
said he was Jesus Christ.
He tried to bury his head in the floor and to
raise his feet above his head.

1958

Sulphur hydrogenisatum
Three days later he was admitted to Rainhill
Asylum and there was still very violent and
excited, gesticulating and talking incoherently,
chiefly on religious subjects. At the end of a
month there was some improvement and he
was discharged, he recovered five months after
admission.
In the other case, that of a laborer at chemical works, Wiglesworth is not quite certain that
Sui-h. was the poison inhaled. This patient was
greatly excited, threw his arms about, shouted
and laughed by turns, was excited and talkative.
He remained permanently insane.
REFERENCES- Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Known as Vitriol of the AI·

Middle Ages. It was used extensively in dilution

venereal ulcers, as a gargle and mouthwash for

The "Acid Soap" of Achard was prescribed

nephritis, obstinate intermittent fevers, visceral
obstructions, dropsy, jaundice, cachexia and
"certain tumors of the feet."
Elixir of vitriol is a mixture of the sulphuric
acid, alcohol and water. It was a popular remedy
for nervous weakness in women. Dippel, Hailer
and others each had an "Elixir," differing only in
the proportions of the chief ingredients.
The elixirs were used in intermittent fever,
putrid, malignant, contagious, comatose and
petechial fevers, scarlatina, confluent and
malignant variola.

strong or diluted in varying proportions, speedily removes thrush." In potencies, it has cured
ulcerative inflammation ofthe mouth. Headache,

COMMENTS - When Burdick gave some of the
Sym-r. to the first prover, a woman, she felt the
marked nausea, and exclaimed, as soon as it
was produced, "Doctor, this is precisely like the
morning sickness I always experienced during
pregnancy."
Dr. Burdick became more interested, repeated
the experiment with other provers, and obtained
almost uniform results, viz., a feeling varying
from qualmishness to intense vomiting. It was
given to female provers only and merely tested
far enough to verify that symptom.
Upon this clue, Dr. Burdick gave Sym-r. in the
higher potencies to patients suffering from the
vomiting of pregnancy with the most satisfactory
results. After a trial of many years, he found it
so far superior to other remedies that he relied
on it altogether with rarely any but entirely
satisfactory results.
Burdick mentioned the drug in his course of
lectures, so Moaffat bore it in mind waiting for
a test case. Soon that came in the person of a
young woman three months advanced in her
first pregnancy.
She was suffering from a deathly nausea with
vomiting and retching so prolonged and violent as
to produce hematemesis. The smell or thought
of food was repugnant in the extreme.
An examination disclosed no malposition or
apparent cause for the trouble, so he procured
some Sym-r. 200c from Dr. Burdick and gave
her one dose in the midst of a violent paroxysm.
In a few minutes she stopped vomiting and said
she felt soothed and quieted all over. In half an
hour the nausea began again, but a few pellets
checked it promptly and she fell asleep. Once
during the night she awoke distressed and took
a dose, but slept again quite soon.
For a month or so she felt very well until after
over-exerting herself she became nauseated
once more, but it was promptly checked, nor
did it retum during her pregnancy.
In more severe cases, there is a deathly
nausea, the vomiting is continuous, violent
retching. Sym-r. does not seem to be confined to
any particular morning aggravation, a prominent
symptom is the disgust at the sight, smell or
thought of food.

Squire knew a bonesetter who rendered

Sir Wm. Thomson of Dublin related a case of
malignant tumor of the face that had extended
to the nose. Microscopic examination proved it
to be round-celled sarcoma.
The patient, a man, refused advice at the time,
and was examined by Felix Semon, who saw the
man later. After still further delay, Thomson performed the operation in the month of May, 1896.
Amonth later the growth began to show again,
increased rapidly, closed the right eye, was
blue, tense, firm, lobulated, but did not break.
Thomson declined to operate again. Early in
October, the man walked into Thomson's study
well. "The tumor had completely disappeared
from the face and I could not identify any trace
of it in the mouth." The man had applied poultices
of comfrey root and the swelling disappeared.

TABERNANTHEIBOGA
(lboga Bark)
PHARMACY-tab-ib. Tabemanthe iboga.lboga bark.
Black bugbane. Bitter grass. N. O.Apocynacae.
Bark and root. Planets: Moon, Saturn. Historical
dose: Tincture and all potencies.
CLINICAL- Addictions. Aphrodisiac. Alcoholism.
Delirium tremens. Drug, abuse. Fatigue. Heroin,
habit. Opioid addictions. Tobacco, habit.
HERBAL - Tabernanthe iboga, also known as
black bugbane, is a perennial rainforest shrub
and hallucinogen, native to western Africa.
lboga stimulates the central nervous system
when taken in small doses and induces visions
in larger doses.
Ibogaine is the active chemical in the African
root. It is a strong, long-lasting psychedelic
used traditionally in a coming of age ritual, but
also known for its modem use in treating heroin
addiction.

1986

T

Tabernanthe iboga
The drug's story as an anti-addictive began in
1962, when college dropout and heroin addict
Howard Lotsof obtained a dose from a chemist
friend.lboga relieved him of all cravings for heroin.
In 1986, Lotsof began to supply ibogaine to a
clinic for addicts in Holland. The clinic found that
ibogaine works in three stages. First the addict
has about four hours of waking dreams in which
he seems to confront inner demons.
This is followed by an eight- to 10-hour
"cognitive evaluation period," during which the
user analyzes the waking dream. Then comes
a sleepless day or two, which Lotsof calls the
"residual stimulation phase."
Lotsof said ibogaine allows addicts, especially
heroin users, to put aside their fears ofwithdrawal
and begin the process of detoxification.
One methadone patient said that in just four
days he reached a state that normally would have
taken him three months, but without the agony.
The heroin addiction therapy may last several
days and upon completion the subject is generally no longer physically dependent. Research
suggests that ibogaine may also help to treat
addictions to alcohol and nicotine.
Ibogaine breaks down in the liver into a
metabolite called nor-ibogaine. This metabolite
has been shown in clinical research to prevent
cravings for several weeks after a single dose
in some individuals.
Others have observed lboga having some
undesirable side effects regarding blood pressure and heartbeat.
COMMENTS -The lboga was brought back from
Gabon in 1864 by Dr. Griffon du Bellay, a navy
surgeon. He wrote, "The root of this plant is the
part that the Gabonese eat. They say that it is
inebriating, aphrodisiac, and, with it, they claim
that they feel no need for sleep."
However, as early as 1885, Father Henri Neu
had written in a manuscript entitled "Le Gabon"
(Neu 1885), "The natives use an infusion ofiboga
root scrapings as a potent philter that enables one
to discover hidden things and to tell the future.
The one who drinks it falls into a deep sleep
during which he is obsessed by uninterrupted
dreams which, until the time that he awakens,
he takes to be actual events."
REFERENCES - Lotsof. Murphy.

wither cattle will eat it in large quantities and in
that state it is deadly poison." "My people," said

hogs dug it up, ate it and all died."

Kent had a case in which a boy, 4, slid down
banisters and struck his head on a tiled floor.
He became unconscious and a surgeon was
summoned, who found him unconscious with a
clear, watery discharge from the ear, which the
surgeon pronounced to be cerebrospinal fluid.
This condition lasted three days and the case
had been pronounced hopeless when Kent first
saw the boy. Kent noticed that the discharge
was acrid and reddened whatever part it came
in contact with. One dose of Tell. was given. In
two hours the child vomited, a sign of reaction ,
and in two weeks was well.
Shelton related three cases using Tell. The
first concerned a widow, 50, who had pain and
soreness in the upper part of her back for a long
time. She shrank from the slightest touch on the
part. The sensitiveness was so acute that, when
touched, the pain extended into the occiput and
all over the upper region of the back. Tell. 6c
cured in eighteen days.
The second case concerned Miss X., 45, who
had a fall, striking a severe blow on the sacrum.
She suffered for some weeks from concussion
with one point of great soreness in the sacral
region, just above the spot where the blow was
received. She was kept in bed for some weeks
and improved generally, but the painful spot
remained and sensitiveness appeared over the
back, its upper third. Tell. 6c cured all completely.
The third case concerned MissY., 29, who had
severe spinal meningitis ten years before, and
consulted Shelton for a burning, pressing pain
at base of brain. He diagnosed the condition as
meningitis. The patient grew worse and gradually
ptosis, and then hemiplegia set in.
Finally hyperesthesia of the back became so
distressing that it was a question of finding any
support that did not intensify the pain. She could
not bear the slightest touch, complaining that it
not only hurt her at the point of contact, but that
she felt it in the head and in remote parts of the
body. Tell. cleared up the case.

behavior, persistent painful erections, shrinking
testicles and breast growth have been reported
in men. Long term use of high dose anabolics

A year later, being in the same district, he
called at the house and inquired of a man whom
he saw there, apparently in perfect health, what
had become of the invalid.

it took some time to convince Martiny of it.
An old woman had recommended him to make
a tisane of the wood germander which grew
abundantly about there. He had taken it daily
and got well. "A similar case," said Cooper, "was
told me by a distinguished scientist.

in five or ten-drop doses two or three times a day.

HOMEOPATHIC -Thyroiodine is now more generally

to maintain the accelerated metabolic rhythm.
· Milk contains the internal secretion of the thyroid.

the goiter had vanished, but the cyst was not
changed.

feeble, 76, functions normal, appetite and sleep
good, weight 230 pounds.
With increasing doses of Thyri., up to ten
tablets daily the weight steadily went down to
160 pounds, activity increasing in proportion.
When the dose had reached four tablets daily
the urine became very abundant, but was free
from albumen. The daily dose was increased
one tablet every four days.

TILLANDSIA USNEOIDES
(Spanish Moss)
PHARMACY -till-u. Tillandsia usneoides. Spanish
moss. Tree hair. Old mans beard. Florida moss.
N. 0 . Bromeliaceae (Bromeliad or Pineapple
family). Planets: Moon. Historical dose: Tincture
and all potencies potencies.
CLINICAL - Blood, sugar. Breast. milk. Childbirth.
Diabetes. Epilepsy. Hemorrhages. Rheumatism.
HERBAL - Tillandsia is usually an epiphytic plant
with reduced to absent stems. Found mostly in
tropical to temperate Americas. Hangs in the
trees and swamps of the southeast coastal plains.
Many Native American tribes used the moss
while cooking to absorb unwanted liquids, for
bedding, for tanning hides, and to rub on newborn
babies heads for curly hair. It is also used as
fodder for animals.
Colonial pickers harvested moss with long
poles during the winter. The harvest hung for
several months to cure in a moss yard. Curing
loosened the outer gray scales making it ready
for commercial ginning.
Medicinal use of Spanish moss has a long
history. Extracts from it have been used in the
treatment of diabetes and it has been used to
help control blood sugar levels.
Spanish moss was taken, while green, and
brewed into tea for expectant mothers, supposedly to aid the flow of breast milk and make the
delivery easier. Tea from the plant was also used
as a folk remedy for rheumatism.

Tillandsia usneoides
In Mexico, it has been used to treat infantile
epilepsy. In the early 1950s, it was used as an
estrogen substitute and scientists have found
the plant exhibits anti-bacterial properties. In the
West Indies it has been used to make a styptic
ointment for the purpose of stopping bleeding.
COMMENTS- Dr. C. W Mayo reported that, in the
Feb. 9, 1944 "Staff Meetings of the Mayo Clinic,"
the absorptive qualities of Spanish Moss for use
in surgical dressings had been investigated with
interesting results.
"The dried moss will retain its absorptive power
better than a substance like cotton, as the liquid
taken up is stored chiefly inside the leaves and
cells, instead of merely being held between
adjoining strands. Spanish moss will take up
from six to ten times its dry weight of water."
REFERENCES- Buttimer. Murphy.

HOMEOPATHIC - TNT is a high explosive, obtained
by nitrating toluene, a product of coal tar distillation.
When the skin or hair is exposed to TNT by contact
a characteristic yellow or tawny-orange stain is
produced, which lasts for some weeks. Indicated in
graver forms of anemia (pernicious) and jaundice.
Produces fatal toxic jaundice.
Symptoms were noted in ammunition workers handling TNT who inhale and ingest it, and
also absorb some through the skin. They were
compiled by Dr. C. Wesselhoeft and published
in the December, 1926 issue of the Journal of
the American Institute of Homeopathy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tub-a. is prepared from the

Tub-a. acts most prominently on the apices

tuberculosis, having cured several hopelesslooking cases. It has also done excellently in
some cases of bronchitis following measles.

prostration after the influenza."

In 1892, Arnuphy began giving Tub. 6x and
8x trituration in acute and chronic tuberculosis
cases, with encouraging success, but with
undesired aggravations at times. These were
avoided with 12x and 30x.
In one case, originating in influenza, both
apices were affected, the right one breaking down
and abundant pleuritic effusion on the left side.
Six weeks' treatment with Tub. brought about
recovery. When seen a year later, the patient
was quite well except for retraction of the left side.
Amuphy frequently used Tub. for bronchitis,
catarrhal pneumonia, lobular pneumonia, tubercular pleurisy, parenchymatous nephritis and
influenza. He gave two cases of acute lobular
pneumonia with characteristic symptoms and
high temperatures quickly resolved by Tub.
One case concerned a boy, 3, who received
the 12x; the other was a man, 78, who suffered
from chronic bronchial catarrh. The latte'r was
taken with influenza, pneumonia developed and
he was in a very serious state. Tub. 30x made
an almost immediate change for the better and
recovery followed.

Arnuphy related that, in this case, an abundant
perspiration took place (the skin had been dry)
during the night and he observed this in all cases

Clarke found Tub. 30c, 100c, 200c and 1000c

A curious use of Tub. was made by Jauregg
of Vienna in a case of insanity. He had observed
that cases of insanity are always benefited by an
attack of an acute infectious disease, especially
if it is accompanied with high fever.The idea then
occurred to him to utilize the fever produced by
Koch's Tuberculinic injections.
He tried it on some patients and though the
favorable symptoms soon disappeared after the
fever subsided, there remained a steady clearing
of the confused sensorium.
Insanity is very frequently a manifestation of
the tuberculosis miasm and there is something
more than a pyrexial power in Tub.

'

failed, by an injection into the bowels of an infusion of 1 oz of powdered bark to 1 pt of boiling
water, used while warm. Slippery elm is also used
in lozenges to relieve irritation of the pharynx.
The food or gruel should be made as follows:
Take a teaspoonful of the powder, mix well with
the same quantity of powdered sugar and add 1pt
of boiling water slowly, mixing as it is poured on.

COMMENTS-S. Mills Folwer mentioned the use of

dying by hundreds of scurvy and Mr. T. (who told
the story) was one of the sufferers.
His legs were flexed upon the thighs and the
thighs upon the body in such violent contraction
that it was impossible to extend them an inch and
any attempt to do so was attended with shocks
of pain as from an electric battery. He could only
move on his elbows and rump.
Within the stockade were growing two large
turpentine trees. Of the pitch from these trees the
patients would take enough to make their urine
"clear and white as crystal." The urine voided
was allowed to stand until it began to sour, which
took twelve to twenty-four hours.
The patients then took a "good swallow" four
or five times a day. They felt the good effect of
every dose. The treatment cured Mr. T. and all
his companions in misfortune who adopted it.

the children's own urine.

Burnett may be said to have rediscovered
Urt-u. as a remedy. The history of how he came
to use it is one of the most fascinating passages
of his works. Burnett's tincture is made of the
small nettle, Urt-u., which is the variety used in
homeopathy.
Burnett noted that the nettle springs up everywhere near human habitations. He noticed
it flourishing more by the side of ditches that
carry off fluid sewage, thus possibly living to
some extent on uric acid.
Burnett's discovery of its fever action occurred
when a female patient was cured of ague (which
he had not succeeded in helping) by drinking
nettle-tea on the advice of her herbalist.
Urt-u. was useful to him in cases of the fevers
of the East India, Burma and Siam. It also has a
marked anti-gout action.
Urt-u. causes fever as well as cures it, and one
of Burnett's patients was obliged to stop taking it:
"It sets all my pulses beating, makes me terribly
giddy, makes me feel as if I was going to topple
(forwards) on my head and then a bad headache
comes on and when I take it at night, it makes
me very feverish ."
When she took the dose in the morning she did
not have the fever, and Burnett said, "The fever
of gout generally comes on at night."
With Urt-u., Burnett cured severe cases of
uremia, vertigo. Burnett used Urt-u. a good deal
in spleen disorders and found patients under

the whooping cough vanished.
Burnett repeated the experiment in other cases

G. M. H. recorded the experience he had
concerning Varia. 6c given to the mother and
children of a family, one of whose members was
taken with smallpox and removed to an isolation
hospital with his mother to nurse him.
The patient (who did not receive Varia.) was
dangerously ill for a month. Neither the mother
who nursed him nor any of the other children
caught smallpox.

Variolinum
Vaccines were sent by the government, and
all the family were vaccinated, but it did not take
with any of those who had taken Vario., although
the vaccination was repeated.
Moreover, G. M. H. himself, who had taken
a dose of Vario., submitted to vaccination, but
"although four thorough inoculations were given,
they healed up immediately and did not even
itch or smart."
A school of two hundred children were "internally variolated" with Va rio. (100, OOOc, Swan) on
the evening of February 18th and the morning
of February 19th. Of two school mistresses, one
was not at all affected, the other was ill for two
days in bed.
On February 21st many of the children were ill,
by the 23'd, all except forty were. The symptoms
were the usual preliminary symptoms of smallpox,
and later, Swan found pustules on many.
After the varioloid had passed off, but before
the patients had recovered their vitality, twentythree children were vaccinated without Swan's
knowledge. All but one took and had terrible
ulcers on the arms and had to be remedied by
Vac. (100,000c, Swan).

HOMEOPATHIC - Verin. is both a paralyzer and a
great pain producer. It causes a sensation like
electric streams in nerves, shooting pains like
electric-shocks in veins, muscles and joints.
Verin. causes tetanus, which Farrington distinguishes from the convulsive action of Nux-v. in
that Verin. causes purgation and vomiting with
the spasms and that general paralysis does not
take place from exhaustion as with Nux-v., but
from devitalization of the muscles.
In large doses, it causes violent sneezing and
great gastro-intestinal irritation, vomiting, purging
and symptoms of collapse. The pulse is rapid,
small and irregular and often involuntary muscular
tremors come on.
A peculiar creeping and prickling sensation in
skin generally accompanies these symptoms.
Externally applied to the unbroken skin it has
no marked action. If rubbed on with some fat, it
passes through the epidermis and causes first
irritation and then paralysis of the ends of the
sensory nerves and producing a prickly and
creepy sensation, succeeded by numbness.
Jhis effect is produced whether applied locally
or taken internally. Brunton noted this irritating
action in the sensory nerves is also observed if
it is inhaled through the nose, where it causes
violent sneezing, which also occurs after absorption through the stomach.

Heat, worse "the cooler the better."
Cold sweat with the attacks. Headache from
both temples to base of brain, worse by heat.
Vertex itched during attacks. Pain compelled
her to move about, but no better from motion.

HERBAL- Growing side by side, Verat. and Verat-v.
are scarcely distinguishable when not in flower.
Millspaugh, however. said that Verat-v. is strikingly
different in general appearance.
Verat-v. having a much more pointed leaf,
panicles looser and more compound , the
racemes of Verat. being more compact and as
a whole cylindrical, those of Verat-v. scattered,
compound and craggy. Verat. flourishes in
mountain meadows, Verat-v. grows in swamps
and wet meadows and along mountain creeks
from Canada to the Carolinas.
Through this confusion, an accidental proving
of the latter has been included in the pathogenesis
of Verat-v. The plants belong to different orders,
though it must be admitted there is a close
resemblance in their effects.
The root of Verat-v. contains Veratrine and the
other alkaloids found in the root of Verat., but in
different proportions.
HOMEOPATHIC - Burt proved Squibb's liquid
extract of Verat-v, and said he found no other
preparation satisfactory.
Hinsdale noted that it is known clinically
that such diseases as Tiegel's contracture,
Thompson's disease, athetosis and muscular
paralysis present a symptomatology quite like
that produced by Verat-v. upon muscular tissue.
Verat-v. produces violent congestive conditions, base ofbrain, medulla, lungs with nausea
and vomiting and weakness. Stomach, heart
and capillaries are also affected. Congestions,
especially to lungs, base of brain with nausea
and vomiting. Congestive stage and early manifestations of hepatization in pneumonia.
Twitchings and convulsions, here and there
during sleep, jerking and trembling, threatened
with convulsions. Chorea, twitching, contortions,
unaffected by sleep, froth about the lips. Lies
with head low.

VERBASCUM THAPSUS
(Mullein Oil)
PHARMACY -verb. Verbascum thapsus. Mullein oil.
Verbascum thapsiforrne. Oleum mullein. Great
Mullein. N. 0. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh
plantat the commencement of flowering.To prepare
mullein oil, fill a bottle with the blossoms from the
Verbascum thapsus, cork it tight and hang inthe sun
for four or five weeks. By that time there will be an
oily liquid distilled. Mix with ten percent of alcohol.
Tincture of the whole plant beginning to flower.
Planets: Mercury. Historical dose: Tincture and
all potencies.
CLINICAL - Anus, itching. Asthma. Bedwetting.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany said, ''The thick
woolly leaves of Verbascum thapsus, the Great
Mullein, have a mucilaginous, bitter taste and a
decoction of them is employed in domestic practice
in catarrhs and diarrhea.
"The leaves are also used as emollient applications to hard tumors and in pulmonary
complaints in cattle hence one of its popular
names is Bullock's Lung-wort. It is also called
Adam's flannel from its flannel-like leaves."
Among its traditional uses Gerarde mentioned
it as a remedy for hemorrhoids and as applications for itching hemorrhoids or anal itching. An
ointment is made of the tincture. Gerarde said
that the oil of the yellow flowers is also curative
in hemorrhoids.

Cushing introduced this now rather well-known
remedy to the medical profession in 1884. He
wrote "My father's house was the home for all
poor tramps, as well as ministers, etc. He fell
into the river, got water in his ears and was quite
deaf for months.
"Ablind man had called, heard loud conversation, asked the cause, etc., then said for kindness
received he would tell us how to make something
that would surely cure him and it was worth a
thousand dollars in New York City.
"We made the oil, put it in his ears at night and
he was well in the morning. For years we kept a
bottle of it and ittraveled all around the towns and
did wonders. That was when I was a youngster."
Hering, in "Hearing and Ears," noticed "In
Germany flowers of Verbascum thapsus put in
a dark-colored bottle, hung up in the sunlight,
give in two or three weeks an oily fluid which has
cured many old people and children."
Hahnemann proved Verb. and his proving

Chronic dennatitis of the external meatus and
drumhead or exfoliation after furuncle. Catarrhal

Nash described a "Cough, deep, hollow,

many cases and always used it low. It is more
especially a night cough. It occurs in children

Mullein was used as a popular specific for
tuberculosis, the leaves being boiled in milk,
which was then strained and given warm.
W. B. McCoy gave several illustrations.According to him Verb. (i.e., the "oil") has a "soothing
.effect on the entire nervous system in many
cases acting as a soporific."
In summer diarrhea he gave one to four drops
in two ounces of warm water, a teaspoonful every
hour. In bedwetting or dribbling of urine one-drop
doses in warm water three or four times a day.
Among his cases were those of two boys who
had become deaf from getting water in their ears
when swimming. They were cured by having three
drops of the oil instilled "in each ear alternately
night and morning."
0. S. Laws cured a youth of 16 of bedwetting
with fifteen drops of the oils three times a day.
The oil plainly acts on the indications of the
proving and may be regarded as an alternative
preparation to the official tincture. It might be
called Verbasci oleum.
Mr. Kemmis spent a large amount of money
treating with various physicians for what they
pronounced a rose cancer and without any relief.
An Indian woman told him to use mullein oil. He
distilled it (by sun exposure) and for a short time
bathed the cancer with the oil.
The growth of cancer was permanently
checked, but it was not healed. Mr. K. lived,
perhaps, forty years after the treatment was
used and the cancer never again bothered him.

dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - Verbena, in the form of a tea as a diuretic

for a long time.
HOMEOPATHIC - Verbe-h. affects the skin and

Passive congestion.
Epilepsy, insomnia, mental exhaustion. In

Viburnum prunifolium is a uterine tonic. Useful
for habitual miscarriage. After-pains. Menstrual
irregularities of infertile females with uterine
displacements. Morning sickness. Cancer of
the tongue, obstinate hiccough.
Phares said of it, "Vib-p. is particularly valuable
in preventing abortion and miscarriage, whether

COMMENTS - Phares noted the case of Mrs. W.
had never gone to full tenn, had several children
at eight months, all of them dying one month after
birth. Frequent pregnancies and hemorrhages had
seriously impaired her health.
When next pregnant Vib-p. was ordered and
at the eighth month when pains set in vigorously
with copious bloody discharge, Vib-p. was given
freely and she went to term, giving birth to a
healthy boy, who survived.
He also recorded the case of Mrs. L., married
eighteen months, had miscarried and suffered
long and much in consequence. Being again
pregnant, Phares gave her Vib-p. tincture, a
teaspoonful thrice daily. At the third month, she
was severely injured by a fall from her carriage.
Strong uterine contractions ensued, but
were arrested by Vib-p., which had to be given
freely for several days, the dose being gradually diminished. For nearly a week, miscarriage
was threatened whenever Vib-p. was too long
suspended. The patient went to tenn and gave
birth to a large boy.

HERBAL- This is a special Ayurvedic herb used
for both diabetes mellitus as well as cancer. It
is useful in treating gastritis, cystitis, enteritis,
diarrhea, diabetes, etc when taken internally.
Chinese medicine uses the extracts of the
sadabahar plant to treat conditions such as diabetes, malaria, leukemia, and Hodgkin's disease.
Vinca rosea leaves and stems are a source of
alkaloids that have anti-tumor and anti-cancer
properties.Vinca rosea controls nosebleeds,
bleeding gums, mouth ulcers and sore throats.
For wasp stings, apply the juice of the leaves
at the spot. It helps to neutralize the poison,
prevents swelling, and relieves pain.
Vinca rosea is used for "general brain health"
Increasing blood circulation in the brain, supporting brain metabolism, increasing mental
productivity. Also preventing memory and concentration problems and feebleness, improving
memory and thinking ability, preventing senility.
Vinca rosea plants contain various alkaloids that
are useful in conditions such as cancer, diabetes,
high blood pressure and stroke. The bioactive
ingredients vinblastine and vincristine are used in
the treatment of leukemia and Hodgkin'slymphoma.
COMMENTS - Use only in very small doses or as a
homeopathic remedy. The Vinca rosea plant itself
is toxic and can be deadly if consumed in large
quantities. Vinca rosea can cause nausea, vomiting, dizziness, seizures, and liver damage, among
other side effects, when consumed orally. If you
are taking lithium or medication for diabetes, there
may be interactions with Madagascar periwinkle.
RELATIONS - Buah merah. Vinca minor. Chaga.

Watercress is best consumed as fresh as possible. For those with digestive disorders, toss your
watercress in a little vinegar and olive oil to improve
digestion and absorption of nutrients. The fresh,
tender leaves of watercress have to be harvested
just before flowering, because after flowering they
become bitter and are no longer good to eat.
Preparing watercress is simple.Aftertrimming the
stems, rinse the greens in cold water and dry on a
paper towel or in a salad spinner. Use immediately,
or store in a closed container in the refrigerator for
up to four days.
Watercress has a unique, peppery taste that can
add punch to almost any salad and it makes delicious soups. Chinese people like to boil watercress
soup with ingredients like carrots, onions, black
pepper, ginger, etc.
Watercress has a variety of uses, either as salad
greens, flavoring herb, juice or as a medicinal herb.
Watercress can take the place of lettuce in any salad,
sandwich, or other recipe, and can be used as a
nutritious garnish. Watercress can also be enjoyed
lightly steamed, stir-fried, or as a hearty soup.
Raw watercress has greater cancer-fighting
power than cooked watercress, as cooking
inactivates the myrosinase enzyme that is responsible for hydrolyzing glucosinolates to beneficial
isothiocyanates.

Under Gels., and laterBry., she was improving,

Her head was retracted, with complete unconsciousness. Staring eyes rolled upward. Lying

F. W. Payne reported a case of cataract in which

Slight irritation of conjunctiva and tendency of

by artificial light. Patient nervous, tremulous,

jerking of individual muscles.
Zinc 200c, given occasionally, steadily improved the case. In six months. the right eye
was quite clear and the left steadily gaining.
Eleven years later, vision was practically perfect,
though some small streaks could still be found
in the left lens.

Homeopathic-Herbal Glossa
Abscess-A localized collection in a cavity or lump formed
by the process of suppuration and disintegration of tissue.

Agoraphobia - Fear of being in open spaces or crossing
open spaces.

Absinthism - The pathological state resulting from the
excessive and habitual use of absinth, characterized
by neuritis, hyperesthesia, hallucinations, convulsions,
acute mania and general paralysis.

Ague - A chill. Recurrent chill. An intermittent fever with
alternating fits of hot and cold. Ottens refers to malaria
and periodic fevers.

Accoucheur - To assist in childbirth, from old French
meaning to lay down. A midwife, obstetrician, one who
helps deliver babies.
Acne rosacea - Acne of cheeks and nose associated with
congestion and formation of telangiectases (stretching
and dilation of small vessels).
Acne vulgaris - Acne simplex or common acne. It is
considered an abnormal response to normal levels ofthe
male hormone testosterone.Acne lesions are commonly
referred to as pimples, spots or zits.
Acromegaly -Acromegaly (from Greek akros "h1gh" and
megas "large· extremities enlargement) is a hormonal
disorder that results when the pituitary gland produces
excess human growth hormone (HGH). Most commonly
from a benign HGH producing tumor called pituitary
adenoma.
Actinomycosis - An infectious disease caused by a
parasite. The jaw is most commonly affected being the
site of slow growing suppurating tumors. (Lumpy jaw,
clyers. wooden tongue).
Acute remedies - These are the type of homeopathic
remedies prescribed for acute infections and fevers.
Examples: Aconite, Arsenicum album, Baptisia,
Belladonna, Bryonia, Chamomille, Gelsemium, Ferrum
phos., Pulsatilla, Pyrogen.

AIDS - Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS or
Aids) isa collection of symptoms and infections in humans
resulting from the specific weakness of the immune
system caused by the human immunodeficiency virus
(HIV). The late stage of the condition leaves individuals
prone to opportunistic infections and tumors.
Alexia -An Inability to read, word blindness.
Allopathy - Remed1es or treatments that are inopposition

Zymotic fever • Zymotic diseases (for the Greek term
zumoun for "ferment"), an obsolete term in medicine,
formerly applied to the class of acute infectiousmaladies,
presumed to be due to some virus or organism which
acts in the system like a ferment The term, however,
came to be restricted in medical nomenclature tothe chief
fevers and contagious diseases (e.g. typhus and typhoid
fevers. smallpox, scarlet fever, measles, erysipelas,
cholera. whooping-cough, diphtheria.
